World.title: Abia PCC Flag Off: How Umuahia Roared For Renewed Hope Through Deputy Speaker Kalu
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

By James Nwachukwu

As predicted, the Abia State Presidential Campaign Council flag off held at Umuahia Township Stadium on Monday, November 16, 2026 was a success. Yet success is a word too small for what transpired. What transpired in Umuahia was history, succinctly put. It was spectacular, electric and unforgettable.

Even before the dawn of the day, Umuahia, the Abia State capital was already awake. And the roads got busy even earlier than usual. By 8am, the roads leading to the Stadium, the venue of the event suddenly became a carnival of colours. The green, white, blue colours, and the proud broom colours of the All Progressives Congress (APC) had become commonplace, adoring the streets. Music blared from loudspeakers from within. Women in their colourful wrappers danced. Youths in customized and branded shirts chanted “Tinubu, Tinubu, Tinubu”. Drivers honked in excitement. Traders abandoned their shops to join the moving crowd. Hawkers, of course, made brisk business. Umuahia was awake.

The crowd was massive and enthusiastic. It was the people celebrating their own. The stadium filled to capacity hours before the programme even started. The stands were packed, fully packed. The field was packed, barely a foothold. The VIP pavilion was packed. Groups marched along the edge of the field, displaying their flags and banners, defying the scorching sun. The atmosphere was charged and colourful. The weather was very clement. The air was thick with joy, hope and unity. Drummers drummed. The live band led by a popular gospel artist, Mr. Felix Ndukwe, sang gloriously. Dancers danced. Masquerades and mascots thrilled the crowd. The famous Ohafia War dance was on full display. It was, for me, a festival of democracy.

People came from far and near, across the 17 LGAs of Abia State, and emptied themselves in Umuahia. Of course, APC as a party fielded candidates from the nooks and crannies of the State and so, Aba came with its full force. Ohafia came with its warriors. Bende came with its youths, women and elders. Isiala Ngwa North and South came in their numbers. Ukwa East and West came. Ikwuano, Umuahia North and South, Umunneochi, Isuikwuato, Obingwa, Ugwunagbo, Osisioma and Arochukwu gathered. No LGA was left behind. No senatorial district was also left out. They all queued behind their respective candidates at all levels in the 2027 general elections. To say the least, Abia emptied itself into Umuahia.

There was a gridlock at the entrance, depicting the high turnout, showing acceptability of the APC and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in Abia. For several minutes, human traffic built, jamming every entrance. But it was a beautiful gridlock, a gridlock of love and acceptance. The one that signposted that Abia has indeed embraced the APC.

Then came the moment that shook the stadium. The stadium roared unusually at the entrance of the Deputy Speaker, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu, the leader of the party in Abia, as his convoy snaked into the arena. The roar was different. It was louder and deeper. It was the roar of a people welcoming their leader and son, their pride. As his convoy rolled in, the entire stadium stood up. Thousands of hands went up in the air. Beautiful chants of “Deputy Speaker” rented the air. The drums went wild. The music played louder. The leader and member representing Bende Federal Constituency of the State had arrived.

He did not rush past the crowd. He stood in his open vehicle, waving, smiling, shaking hands, acknowledging every section. He moved slowly through the stretch, from one end of the stadium to the other, greeting and acknowledging cheers from the crowd of men, youths and women in strong admiration of their presence and support for President Tinubu and the APC. The crowd responded with even louder cheers, surging forward to greet and shake hands with him. It was like a triumphant entry, the entry of a general returning home to his troops.

Before coming to the stadium event, the Deputy Speaker had performed another historic duty. It was the commissioning of the Abia State Presidential Campaign Council office in the heart of Umuahia. The office, beautifully branded and strategically located, was unveiled amidst jubilation. It was a symbol that the campaign is not just an event, but also a structure. A structure that will drive the Tinubu message to every polling unit, ward and home in Abia.

Back in the stadium, the event had gotten underway. Speaker after speaker pledged their support for President Tinubu and his reelection bid. From the State Chairman of APC, Hon. Chijioke Chukwu, to the Managing Director of the South East Development Commission, Mr. Mike Okoye, down to Rt. Hon. Cosmos Ndukwe who spoke for Abia North, Chief Henry Ikoh for Abia Central, Rt. Hon. Emeka Stanley for Abia South, Hon. Blessing Nwagba for the Women and Chimamkpam for the youths, the message of renewed hope permeated. Every speaker had the same message, which is that Abia is for Tinubu and Tinubu is for Abia. All the APC candidates in the elections had an opportunity to speak through their representative as they filed out in their numbers.

The National Welfare Secretary of APC, Chief Donatus Nwamkpa, the National Vice Chairman, South East, Dr. Ijeoma Arudiogbu and the APC South East Women Leader, Dr Oby Ajih, also lent their voices. The message was the same.

The immediate past Minister of State for Labour and candidate for Isuikwuato Umunneochi Federal Constituency of the State, Hon. Nkiruka Onyejiocha, while speaking said that the crowd in Abia and their support for the President were unprecedented.

Chief Eric Opah, the governorship candidate also laid it bare. He said the turnout demonstrated Tinubu’s acceptability in Abia and the commitment of the people to re-elect him. Similarly, the National Chairman of APC, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, represented by the Deputy National Chairman South, Dr. Benjamin Obi Nwoye, agreed that with the massive support, Abia is APC.

In his extemporaneous brief speech that drew roars of approval and applause, the Deputy Speaker who is also the Deputy Director General South, declared that APC has come to stay in Abia. He reminded the crowd of President Tinubu love for the Southeast, his bold reforms, and his determination to rebuild Nigeria. Kalu assured President Tinubu of at least 75 percent of the votes in the general elections. He said that the President has given birth to sons and daughters in Abia that will mobilize for his victory, traversing the length and breadth of the State to preach the gospel of the Renewed Hope Agenda. Kalu also assured the people that the reforms of the federal government seen as though earlier, have started producing positive results.

He said: “In the last 3 years, Mr. President chose a tough route. He chose a tough road. The tough path came with the reform. The reform came with its pain and I want to tell you that today we have gone from reform to the time of prosperity. We have gone from shedding tears to the point of commencing our laughter. It is in the moment of this pain that a lot of new developments have been given birth to. And they listed it here today that the pain, like the pain of a pregnant woman after nine months delivers a bundle of joy. We are now in our moment of joy. How many projects shall we count? Is it the work in the south East region in terms of roads or Forex? We are traders in the south East, and often times in the past years, we found it difficult to project into the future with regards to our business calculations. When we import our containers, the dollar will be so epileptic that when the goods arrive here, we will be selling at a loss but today, this President has considered us and has stabilized our currency that we can now make our projection for our trade and it will be as projected. That is the President we are talking about. We are talking about the President that has stopped the ASUU strike. We have forgotten that not too long ago, the universities would close down from time to time and our children will come home because of strike. There is no more strike. Thank you President Tinubu.”

Kalu was not done chronicling the legacies of President Tinubu in the South East.

“Before now, our children would not go to school because there is no money but now NELFUND is solving the problem. We can go on and on. The tax reform has brought stability in our fiscal policy. Thanks to Mr. President. Our reasons for voting for you are many. I want to say thank you to Mr. President for remembering the South East and our pain after the war. A man who did not wait any day longer in office to fulfill the promises made to Ndi Igbo, through the South East Development Commission (SEDC). We will not stop saying thank you to you, Sir.

“We want to thank you for what you are doing about stopping insecurity in our country, the effort you are making, the increase in the number of those who are recruited in the military and in the police, the funding that has increased from what it used to be to what it is now. Our own is to say thank you to you. And one of the best ways we are going to say thank you to you is to vote for you, come January 16”, he said.

Prior to now, some quarters had made jest of the party and their paltry membership. But they were still living in the past when the party struggled to have about 5,000,000 members. Since coming on board as the Deputy Speaker, Kalu has worked assiduously to grow the party from 5,000 to now 162,000 membership, still counting. At the stadium, Kalu said APC is now fully on the ground.

“They were boasting before now, saying there was no APC in Abia State. The members here are all APC. Those people who are going about spreading lies that we don’t have APC in Abia State, this is just a small film show. This event was put together in one week. I charge you on the 7th of December, we are going to be hitting Aba Enyimba Stadium and then, the people of Abia State will see the number of APC and our strength in Abia State”, he said.

Kalu also begged on President Tinubu to visit Abia.

“Mr. President, you have given birth to sons and daughters in Abia. Nobody will make you a beggar. We are mobilizing. We are not sleeping. We are going from house to house, village to village, community to community. We are not playing our politics in Abuja. Mr President, our daddy, see yourself today what we have showcased within 7 days. By the time, we are supported and we prepare more, on the 7th, we want to encourage to wave your decision not to be in Abia State since you have already chosen Enugu State for the region. If there is time, please, consider coming to Aba to see the number of those who are supporting you. The numbers you have in Abia will give you the votes you are looking for”, Kalu said.

This is the first time such a massive crowd from an opposition party will fill the stadium in a ruling state. Let that sink in. In a state controlled by another party, the opposition filled the stadium to overflowing. That has never happened before in Abia. It is revolutionary. Legendary. Unprecedented. And it can only be possible with an aggressive and goal-oriented.

To many Abians especially supporters of APC, the Monday event was not just flag-off but a victory march. A march that will end in resounding victory for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

Indeed, the rich attendance proved that Abia has heeded the call of the Deputy Speaker to vote for President Tinubu in 2027. But until the President is eventually declared winner, the Deputy Speaker said Abia APC will not stop working. The must be reason he announced a donation of 100 buses to the Campaign Council to help reach everywhere with the renewed hope message.

*Nwachukwu, a social analyst and commentator writes from Umuahia, Abia State capital

World.title: From Global Blacklist To International Recognition: Tinubu’s Unprecedented Aviation Transformation
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

By Seyi Bakare

91.45% ICAO safety rating breaks all previous records; five international airports achieve full certification; $850m trapped airline funds cleared; Emirates returns; indigenous airlines empowered as massive infrastructure renewal takes off.

Nigeria’s aviation industry is undergoing one of the most remarkable transformations in its history, with the administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu recording unprecedented milestones in aviation safety, airport infrastructure, international relations, airline operations and the restoration of investor confidence.

What was once an industry struggling with international credibility, restricted access to aircraft financing, trapped foreign airline revenues, deteriorating infrastructure and regulatory deficiencies is gradually emerging as a more competitive and internationally respected aviation destination.

The transformation is not merely reflected in government announcements or policy pronouncements. It is increasingly evident in measurable improvements in safety oversight, the return of major international airlines, renewed access to aircraft leasing markets, the expansion of indigenous carriers and substantial investments in airport infrastructure across the country.

Perhaps the most compelling evidence of this turnaround is Nigeria’s historic 91.45 per cent Effective Implementation score in the International Civil Aviation Organisation’s (ICAO) safety oversight assessment conducted in April 2026.

The achievement represents Nigeria’s highest aviation safety rating in history, placing the country significantly above the global average of 70.4 per cent and the West African regional average of 61.1 per cent.

It is a remarkable departure from the approximately 70 per cent performance that had characterised previous assessments.

For an industry where safety standards determine international confidence, investment decisions and operational credibility, the improvement represents a significant national achievement.

The administration has also achieved full aerodrome certification of Nigeria’s five international airports in Lagos, Abuja, Kano, Port Harcourt and Enugu for the first time in the country’s history.

These accomplishments demonstrate the impact of deliberate regulatory reforms, institutional strengthening and investments in modern aviation infrastructure.

REBUILDING NIGERIA’S AVIATION GATEWAYS

Beyond regulatory improvements, the Tinubu administration has embarked on an ambitious programme to modernise the country’s airport infrastructure.

The flagship project is the comprehensive reconstruction and modernisation of Terminal 1 at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, with a Federal Government commitment of N712.3 billion.

The project, which is more than 50 per cent complete as of November 2026, is designed to transform Nigeria’s busiest international gateway into a modern aviation facility capable of meeting contemporary international standards.

The scope includes redesigned passenger movement systems, modern baggage handling facilities, a new overhead bridge and a skywalk connecting passengers to the departure halls of Terminals 1 and 2.

Significantly, the project is being financed through the Renewed Hope Infrastructure Development Fund, using savings from subsidy reforms rather than new external borrowing.

In Kano, N46 billion has been committed to the resurfacing of the runway at the Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport. The domestic terminal has also been completely remodelled, while a new Hajj terminal was commissioned in July 2026.

The administration has equally supported the upgrading of the Muhammadu Buhari Airport in Maiduguri to full international status, including a new international terminal and facilities for immigration, customs and other relevant agencies.

Other notable interventions include the upgrading of Victor Attah International Airport in Uyo to full international operations, the rehabilitation and expansion of the Benin Airport terminal, the provision of runway lighting at Osubi Airport, the construction of a new terminal at Akure Airport and the ongoing runway expansion programme at Sam Mbakwe International Cargo Airport, Owerri.

The Federal Government has also approved the development of a new international airport at Ubaha Nsulu in Abia State.

These projects reflect an emerging national aviation network in which more states can participate meaningfully in international commerce, tourism, cargo transportation and investment.

RESTORING INTERNATIONAL CONFIDENCE

One of the most significant achievements of the Tinubu administration has been its success in addressing the crisis of trapped airline funds that threatened Nigeria’s international aviation relationships.

At its peak in June 2023, foreign airlines had approximately $850 million in revenues trapped in Nigerian banks because of foreign exchange liquidity challenges.

The situation was so serious that some international airlines suspended operations, while others threatened to withdraw from the Nigerian market.

Through coordinated intervention by the Central Bank of Nigeria and the Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development, the backlog was substantially cleared by mid-2024.

The International Air Transport Association subsequently acknowledged the progress, while Nigeria was removed from the list of countries with blocked airline funds.

As of November 2026, Nigeria has emerged as Africa’s leading country in the repatriation of airline funds.

Another significant diplomatic and aviation milestone was the return of Emirates Airlines to Nigeria on October 1, 2024, after suspending operations in 2022.

The resumption followed high-level diplomatic engagements between Nigeria and the United Arab Emirates, culminating in a renewed bilateral aviation agreement.

The return of Emirates restored an important international connection and demonstrated renewed confidence in Nigeria’s aviation market.

BREAKING THE AIRCRAFT LEASING BARRIER

For years, Nigerian airlines faced enormous difficulties accessing aircraft through international leasing arrangements.

Nigeria’s poor compliance standing under the Cape Town Convention had placed the country on the Aviation Working Group’s non-compliance watchlist, making international lessors reluctant to expose their aircraft to the Nigerian market.

The Tinubu administration addressed this challenge through legal and regulatory reforms, including the signing of a Practice Direction by the Chief Judge of the Federal High Court in 2024 and the operationalisation of the Irrevocable De-registration and Export Request Authorisation (IDERA).

Consequently, Nigeria’s compliance score improved from 49.5 per cent to 75.5 per cent, leading to its removal from the Aviation Working Group’s watchlist.

The practical benefit became evident when Air Peace secured a Boeing 737-700 NG on dry lease from AerCap, one of the world’s leading aircraft leasing companies.

To consolidate this achievement, the Federal Executive Council approved the establishment of the Nigeria Aircraft Leasing Company in April 2026.

The initiative, which is fully privately funded, is projected to unlock more than $1 billion in aircraft financing capacity for Nigerian airlines through a locally based special-purpose vehicle supported by limited government guarantees.

This is a potentially transformative intervention for indigenous carriers that have historically paid significantly higher aircraft leasing costs than their international competitors.

STRENGTHENING INDIGENOUS AIRLINES

The administration has also demonstrated a clear commitment to strengthening Nigerian-owned airlines.

Rather than proceeding with the controversial inherited national carrier arrangement involving Ethiopian Airlines, which faced significant legal challenges, the government discontinued the proposed structure and redirected attention towards supporting existing indigenous operators.

Air Peace’s entry into the Lagos-London route in March 2024 was a significant demonstration of this policy direction.

The airline subsequently expanded its London operations to include Abuja, with services to Heathrow and Gatwick following diplomatic engagements with the United Kingdom.

Approval has also been secured for the proposed Owerri-Lagos-London and London-Owerri operations, further strengthening the international aviation prospects of the South-East.

In April 2026, President Tinubu also approved a 30 per cent discount on outstanding debts owed by domestic airlines to aviation agencies, following concerns over rising aviation fuel costs and threats of operational shutdowns.

These interventions, alongside engagements with major aircraft manufacturers including Boeing, Airbus, Embraer and Bombardier, are aimed at creating a more favourable operating environment for Nigerian carriers.

ENDING TWO DECADES OF LEGAL UNCERTAINTY

Another major achievement is the resolution of the nearly two-decade dispute between the Federal Government and Bi-Courtney Aviation Services Limited over the operation of Murtala Muhammed Airport Terminal 2.

The prolonged disagreement had denied the Federal Government expected revenue from the terminal for almost twenty years and created considerable uncertainty around the public-private partnership arrangement.

Following approval by the Federal Executive Council in April 2026, a negotiated settlement was finally signed in October 2026.

The resolution represents an important breakthrough in the management of aviation infrastructure and provides a clearer framework for investment and operational responsibilities.

BUILDING AVIATION EXPERTISE AND CREATING LOCAL VALUE

The administration has also moved to strengthen Nigeria’s aviation human capital through the commencement of full operations at the African Aviation and Aerospace University in Abuja.

The institution is expected to develop specialised manpower in aviation management, engineering and regulatory studies, reducing the country’s dependence on expensive foreign training institutions.

Similarly, the government’s policy requiring international airlines operating in Nigeria to source onboard meals for outbound flights from local caterers has created new opportunities for indigenous businesses.

The impact is becoming visible in the expansion of local aviation catering companies, including the opening of a N10 billion catering facility in Abuja in October 2026.

The administration has equally approved approximately N36 billion for the payment of pensions and severance benefits to more than 3,300 former employees of the defunct Nigeria Airways, with an initial N18 billion already released.

This represents a long-awaited resolution of an outstanding obligation that had lingered for more than two decades.

NIGERIA’S RISING INTERNATIONAL AVIATION PROFILE

Perhaps one of the strongest indications of the country’s improved aviation standing is the growing international recognition of its leadership and regulatory achievements.

The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, was named among Africa’s top four aviation figures by the International Air Transport Association in April 2026.

He was also appointed Chairman of the Council of Ministers of the Banjul Accord Group, a regional aviation organisation promoting harmonised safety oversight and regulatory standards among West African countries.

Furthermore, the African Development Bank appointed him champion of its $7 billion Integrated Aviation Transformation Programme for Africa, with Nigeria as a pilot country.

Nigeria also hosted its first-ever International Airshow in December 2025, attracting international aircraft manufacturers, lessors, airlines and other aviation stakeholders.

For a country that had previously struggled with international aircraft leasing restrictions, hosting such an event was a powerful demonstration of its renewed ambition and growing relevance in the global aviation community.

A NEW CHAPTER FOR NIGERIAN AVIATION

Taken together, these developments represent a significant departure from the challenges that confronted Nigeria’s aviation industry in 2023.

The record-breaking ICAO safety score, the certification of all five international airports, the return of Emirates, the clearance of trapped airline funds, improved aircraft leasing opportunities, support for indigenous carriers and the extensive airport modernisation programme constitute important milestones in the industry’s development.

While challenges relating to operating costs, passenger experience, infrastructure delivery and airline sustainability remain, the foundations for a more competitive and internationally respected aviation sector are increasingly being established.

The significance of President Tinubu’s intervention lies not simply in the number of projects undertaken, but in the deliberate effort to address structural weaknesses that had constrained the industry for years.

From regulatory credibility to international partnerships, from airport infrastructure to indigenous airline development, Nigeria’s aviation sector is witnessing a major institutional and operational reset.

The journey is far from complete, but one thing is increasingly evident: Nigeria is reclaiming its place in the international aviation community, and the Tinubu administration’s reforms are providing the foundation for that renewed ambition.

*Bakare sent this piece through seyibakre@aol.com

World.title: Senate Sends State Police Bill to Tinubu, Demands Operational Guidelines
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

* Oshiomhole, others warn against political abuse

* insists on safeguards as Akpabio says new policing structure could tackle 70% of insecurity

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Senate on Wednesday approved the transmission of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, providing for the establishment of State Police Services, to President Bola Tinubu for assent, following its approval by the required number of State Houses of Assembly.

However, the upper legislative chamber urged the president to expeditiously forward the proposed National Policing Bill to the National Assembly to establish operational guidelines, define the relationship between federal and state police authorities and provide safeguards against possible abuses.

The Senate’s resolution followed the adoption of a motion sponsored by the Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, directing the Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, to transmit the constitutional amendment to the president in accordance with the Acts Authentication Act, 2004.

The development marks a major milestone in Nigeria’s efforts to decentralise its policing architecture amid persistent security challenges, including terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, communal conflicts and other violent crimes.

Leading the debate, Bamidele recalled that the Senate approved the constitutional amendment on June 24, 2026, while the House of Representatives passed it on July 23, 2026, with both chambers securing the constitutionally required two-thirds majority.

He informed his colleagues that the 36 State Houses of Assembly had also transmitted their resolutions approving the amendment to the National Assembly, thereby satisfying the requirements of Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution.

Under the amendment process, the National Assembly is required to secure the support of at least two-thirds of the State Houses of Assembly before forwarding a constitutional alteration to the president for assent.

Bamidele said the Senate should recognise the completion of the constitutional requirements and proceed with the transmission of the bill.

He also commended Tinubu for providing the political leadership and support that facilitated the initiative, urging him to forward the National Policing Bill to the legislature for scrutiny and expeditious passage.

Seconding the motion, the Senate Minority Leader, Senator Abba Moro, said the establishment of State Police had become necessary given the country’s worsening security situation.

He maintained that the proposed arrangement would complement the existing security architecture and strengthen the capacity of governments to respond to threats within their jurisdictions.

In his contribution, Deputy Senate President and Chairman of the Senate Committee on Constitution Review, Senator Barau Jibrin, described the development as a historic achievement for the Tinubu administration and the 10th National Assembly.

Barau said successive administrations had considered introducing State Police but failed to translate the proposal into reality.

He attributed the progress to Tinubu’s commitment, describing the proposed arrangement as a collaborative policing structure designed to strengthen the Nigeria Police Force rather than undermine it.

“This is a wonderful achievement for the present administration and the current National Assembly. As we know, this matter has been under discussion for a long time. Successive governments have considered how to introduce State Police into the country’s policing system.

“However, no administration was able to achieve this until the present government came into office. Credit must go to the president for his commitment to ensuring that this bill is passed to allow the establishment of State Police in our policing system,” he said.

Senate President Godswill Akpabio also described the constitutional amendment as one of the major accomplishments of the 10th National Assembly, expressing optimism that the new policing structure would significantly reduce insecurity.

He projected that the establishment of State Police could address as much as 70 per cent of the country’s security challenges.

“This is a legislation that will not be forgotten. It is a major achievement of the 10th National Assembly,” Akpabio said.

He, however, stressed that the next phase would be to address the operationalisation of the system and prevent conflicts between state and federal police authorities.

The most pointed intervention came from former Edo State Governor, Senator Adams Oshiomhole, who warned that the proposed State Police system must not become an instrument of political oppression in the hands of state governors.

While congratulating the Senate leadership and the president, Oshiomhole said concerns about possible abuses should not prevent Nigeria from adopting a policing structure capable of responding more effectively to local security threats.

He recalled that as governor, he had expressed reservations about the possibility of future administrations using State Police against political opponents.

Oshiomhole therefore called for comprehensive operational guidelines with the force of law to regulate the activities of the proposed security institutions.

“We can foresee the possibility of some people misusing the police, but that should not be enough reason to abandon the idea,” he said.

He added: “While we pass the bill and transmit it for presidential assent, we should also encourage the executive to send a bill addressing the operational guidelines and how State Police will function alongside the federal police.”

The former governor further warned that disagreements could arise between federal and state authorities over security responsibilities, insisting that clear legal provisions were necessary to prevent institutional conflicts.

He said the guidelines should establish limits on the use of State Police, particularly in political matters, and ensure that the initiative achieved its primary objective of making Nigeria safer.

Similarly, former Senate Leader, Senator Adamu Aliero, supported the amendment, arguing that Nigeria’s existing security architecture required an overhaul to accommodate multiple policing structures.

He said the country could eventually consider local government policing, alongside federal and state police, to address its diverse security challenges.

Also contributing, Senator Ekon Sampson said the judiciary must play a critical role in checking possible abuses through effective oversight and accountability mechanisms.

He argued that concerns about misuse should not overshadow the urgent need to strengthen Nigeria’s security institutions.

The Senate subsequently adopted all three prayers of the motion, directing the Clerk to transmit the constitutional amendment to Tinubu, commending the president for supporting the initiative and requesting the National Policing Bill.

Akpabio, in further clarification, said the executive was expected to forward the implementation framework to the National Assembly without unnecessary delay.

He, however, indicated that the legislature could initiate the necessary legislation if the executive failed to act within a reasonable period.

The Senate’s resolution has therefore shifted attention to presidential assent and the subsequent legislative framework that will determine the structure, powers, funding, accountability and operational relationship between the proposed State Police Services and the Nigeria Police Force.

World.title: Dozi breaks silence on cancer rumours
World.content:
Dozi has denied rumours he has cancer. Image via Facebook

Afrikaans singer Dozi, real name Hendrick Opperman, has rubbished social media rumours that he is dying from cancer.

The veteran entertainer – known for hit songs like Ou Ryperd, Maybe, My Baby, and Tussen My en Jou – recently underwent surgery to remove growths on his vocal cords.

DOZI NOT DYING OF CANCER

In recent days, social media users have been circulating rumours about Dozi’s dire diagnosis, including claims he has developed cancer of the vocal cords.



The claims were rubbished by the singer’s publicist, Alishia van Deventer, who accused individuals of altering images of Dozi to appear frail and thin.

Dozi himself has called out the trolls in a Facebook video, in which he says: “You have to wake up one morning and hear you have a disease… cancer.

“I don’t have cancer, ladies and gentlemen, I’m very sorry. I’ve worked hard, and I’m keeping myself busy. I’m so happy to see so many people still love me and care. You’re not going to believe this, but I’m healthy.”

He added: “We can’t stop fake news from being created, but we can stop sharing it.”

Earlier this month, Dozi underwent surgery to remove polyps on his vocal cord.

BACKABUDDY CAMPAIGN

Meanwhile, a BackaBuddy campaign has been set up to help Dozi cover the costs of his recent surgery.



According to the crowdfunding initiative, which has raised over R80 000, the veteran entertainer could be out of action for several months as he recovers.

“We therefore want to help alleviate the financial pressure of his medical expenses, recovery period and essential living expenses”, it reads.

Ahead of his surgery, industry colleagues hosted a fundraising concert called Dozi JAM – Back Our Buddy, in Hartbeespoort.

World.title: Anele Mdoda’s sister claims friends ‘didn’t trust’ her husband, Buzza
World.content:
Zamalisa Mdoda, the younger sister of Anele Mgudlwa (née Mdoda), came out guns blazing, claiming that two of Anele’s friends did not trust her husband, Bonelela “Buzza” Mgudlwa.

ZAMALISA MDODA CLAIMS ANELE’S FRIENDS ‘DIDN’T TRUST’ BUZZA

In a tweet posted on 15 November 2026, Zamalisa alleged that two of Anele’s “long-time friends” had approached their father, asking him to persuade Anele to sign a prenuptial agreement because they did not trust her husband.

She further alleged that Anele had ignored warnings about Buzza and that he might “turn on her.”



2 of @Anele’s long-time friends went to our father asking him to get Anele to sign a pre-nup because they didn’t trust @BonelelaM. Did she listen? No. She had multiple warnings about him but she wanted her Netflix wedding. When he does turn on her, remember that she chose this. — Zamalisa (@Zamedyzamzam) November 15, 2026

FANS DEFEND ANELE

Judging by their reactions to Zamalisa’s allegations, Anele’s fans are clearly in her corner. They defended her fiercely amid the buzz surrounding her Netflix wedding special.

Ziminaphakade: I guess Anele was right when she said you 3 sisters couldn’t state clearly what the problem was between her and you guys; instead, you fought amongst yourselves. You’ve been talking for 2 weeks now, and we still can’t make out what the problem is.

SouthAfricansFirst🇿🇦@_SAFirst_: Reading all your tweets, you are trying everything to humiliate your sister, and it is sad. Pathetic actually. The things you are saying about Anele say A LOT about who you are & less about her.

veve@Leveve18: It’s now clear that Anele’s sister is a bully, and she is hurting that they can no longer control her It’s good that Anele isn’t giving this fire any oxygen. This one needs to heal shem.

MORE ALLEGATIONS MADE BY ZAMALISA MDODA

The allegations involving Anele’s friends are among multiple claims made by Zamalisa.



The Mdoda family drama unfolded when Zamalisa dished out a heated response to a tweet in which Anele shared her thoughts on firstborns.

Zamalisa interpreted the tweet as a reference to their family dynamics, writing:

“This girl has used her platform to harass and lie about our family for YEARS! @947, is this how your hosts conduct themselves? Using personal vendettas as topics of discussion?”

Without delving into their family drama, Zamalisa alleged that Anele had been a topic of discussion during family meetings over the years. She also insinuated that Anele was involved in witchcraft.

@Anele I told your father a touch is a move. So since you wanna touch, here is my move. That meeting was about YOUR broom activities. And while we’re here, bring back our photo albums or did you leave them at umhlaba uyalingana? — Zamalisa (@Zamedyzamzam) November 13, 2026

Zamalisa also accused Buzza of failing to pay her cousin for the alcohol she supplied at his wedding.

She paired the tweet with a post referencing the allegations of corruption involving COVID-19 PPE tenders.

She also alleged that Buzza only married her sister for financial gain.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs suffer defensive blow ahead of Sundowns semi-final
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs defender Inacio Miguel has been ruled out of the highly anticipated clash against Mamelodi Sundowns at Loftus Versfeld Stadium this weekend.

Amakhosi face the Brazilians in the semi-final of the Carling Knockout Cup on Sunday afternoon.

Miguel, who serves as Chiefs’ vice-captain, is currently completing a two-match suspension following a straight red card in the heated 2-1 Soweto Derby defeat to Orlando Pirates last month.



His absence leaves a significant void in the heart of the Kaizer Chiefs defence, particularly if the team suffers an injury during the encounter.

In recent matches, Amakhosi head coach Fernando Da Cruz has opted to partner Rushwin Dortley and Thabo Moloisane in central defence. The duo have been impressive so far and will likely continue their partnership against Sundowns.

Kaizer Chiefs need a strong defence on Sunday

Chiefs will need to remain defensively solid, especially against a Sundowns side boasting one of the strongest attacking forces in the PSL and across the continent.

The last meeting between the two sides ended in a 1-1 draw in August. Da Cruz will take encouragement from the fact that Amakhosi have avoided defeat in their last four meetings against the Brazilians.

Kaizer Chiefs have not reached a final since winning the Nedbank Cup. Ironically, they played Downs in the semi-final, where they won 2-1. At the time, they were coached by Tunisian tactician Nasreddine Nabi, who ended their 10-year trophyless drought.

Do you think Miguel missing Sunday’s match will help Chiefs?

World.title: Rassie’s ‘cousin’ claps back at critics
World.content:
Rassie Erasmus has been praised by a relative. Image via IG

Rassie Erasmus’s reported cousin has spoken out in his defence following his six-match suspension by World Rugby this week. This follows comments by the Springbok coach, who implied that match officials may have deliberately ignored 17 dangerous tackles by the French against South African players.

RASSIE ERASMUS’S COUSIN COMES TO HIS DEFENCE

In an Instagram post, Gerhard Boshoff, who claims to be Rassie Erasmus’s cousin, showed his public support for the Springbok coach.

He also praised the rugby hero for his bold comments questioning the television match official (TMO)’s lack of intervention in several tackles he believed were dangerous. 

Gerhard, a fitness coach, posted: “When protecting the game of rugby matters more than protecting yourself. That’s leadership!”

He added: “Proud of you for speaking up, cuz!”

Gerard added that Rassie was a “leader and innovator” who is “not scared of the truth”.



In the comments section, Gerhard continued to defend Rassie against critics who accused the latter of selective outrage.

He clapped back: “He is living rent-free in your head, and I understand that can be hard to swallow”

He added: “He took one for World Rugby, as we all know it’s rotten on the top”



DAUGHTER HINTS AT DOUBLE STANDARDS

Meanwhile, Rassie’s daughter, Nikki Erasmus, has indirectly reacted to her father’s si-match suspension.

The netball star – the twin sister of Carli – made a subtle hint at double standards after she posted an IG Story about Irish player Sam Prendergast, who has been cleared to play against the Springboks, despite being cited for a dangerous tackle.



Over the weekend, Prendergast was involved in a hip-drop tackle on Fiji captain Peceli Yato, who was forced off the field due to injury.

Just weeks earlier, World Rugby outlawed the dangerous technique under its updated laws.

In his comments, Rassie predicted that Predergast suggested that Prendergast would escape punishment because of a technicality.



This comes just days ahead of the Springboks match against Ireland on Saturday, 21 November, at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

World.title: Dladla leaves Yanga as Fadlu Davids reshuffles backroom staff
World.content:
Former Durban City head coach Simo Dladla has reportedly parted ways with Tanzanian giants Yanga SC.

Dladla had joined Yanga SC as one of Manqoba Mngqithi’s assistants at the start of the season.

Mngqithi was let go after 13 games alongside some of the technical members he came with but Dladla remained behind as caretaker coach.



Now, according to FARpost, Dladla has now left Yanga SC who recently appointed Fadlu Davids as Mngqithi’s permanent successor.

The publication further reports that Dladla will be returning to Richards Bay FC who sacked Dimitar Pantev two weeks ago.

Dladla coached the Natal Rich Boyz between 2020 and 2021, the management believes he can help them steer the ship in the right direction.

Richards Bay FC are winless in their last 10 competitive games, and they are early candidates for relegation.

World.title: ‘Disgusting’: South Africans fume over R2 400 SASSA grant update
World.content:
South Africans are venting their anger at the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA), with many saying the R2 400 SASSA grant is not enough for vulnerable recipients to survive.

The Older Persons Grant is R2 400 per month for beneficiaries aged 60 and older, amounts that took effect from 1 April 2026. The Disability Grant and Care Dependency Grant also rose from R2 315 to R2 400.

Grant recipients and their families shared their frustrations in the comments on The South African’s Facebook page.



Grant recipients accuse SASSA of ‘games’

Several commenters said they felt SASSA was toying with people who depend on their R2 400 SASSA grants.

“What waiting game,” Liz Zugloi wrote.

Letitia Cullen was among the most outspoken. She questioned how recipients are expected to cope.

“How cruel can SASSA be? How must we survive now? You want to play games?” Cullen wrote.

She said elderly South Africans are the hardest hit, adding that “there are thousands of old people suffering, sick and even dying.”

Long days at SASSA offices

Others turned their frustration to the service recipients receive at SASSA offices.



Isaiah Oupa said people in Soshanguve often spend the entire day at the local office without getting help.

“Sometimes in SA you will hate the way our government works, especially in SASSA Soshanguve, most people go there without help, stay there the whole day without help,” Oupa wrote.

One word sums up the mood

For some South Africans, a single word was enough to express how they felt.

“Disgusting,” Dina Chorn wrote.

The reactions reflect growing frustration among grant recipients, particularly pensioners, who rely on their monthly payments to cover food, electricity, transport and medical costs.

Many older South Africans also support children and grandchildren in their homes, which means a single grant often has to feed an entire household.

For them, any change, delay or uncertainty around their grants can mean the difference between getting by and going without.

The comments also show how many recipients feel unheard by SASSA, both in decisions about their payments and in the service they receive at local offices.

World.title: Thabang Matuludi named Sundowns’ best player for October
World.content:
Thabang Matuludi is Sundowns' best player for October. Image: Mamelodi Sundowns WhatsApp Channel.

Mamelodi Sundowns right-back Thabang Matuludi has been named the club’s best player for the month of October.

Signed in September from Polokwane City, Matuludi needed no introduction from the majority of Sundowns fans.

And he fitted like a hand in a glove after taking over from the injured Khuliso Mudau, cementing his place in the Sundowns team.



In October, the right-footed defender featured in all five competitive matches for the Brazilians.

Matuludi, despite being a defender, scored two goals in those five games and helped the team win the MTN8 final.

As a result, he won the Cherry Player of Month award where he will be handed the vehicle and get to drive it for a month.

Matuludi was nominated alongside the Fawaaz Basadien, Iqraam Rayners, Ronwen Williams and Teboho Mokoena.

He becomes the third Sundowns player to win the Cherry Player of the Month award this season after Marcelo Allende (August) and Siyanda Ndlovu (September).

The 27-year-old was instrumental as Bafana Bafana recently collected four points off Kenya in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers.



Pitso Mosimane’s men played to a 2-2 draw with Kenya in the first leg which played at Orlando Amstel Arena before beating the same opponents 2-1 on Tuesday.

As reported by The South African, Bafana Bafana have since returned to the country from Nairobi, Kenya.

World.title: Harry Styles, Cher to headline Glastonbury
World.content:
LONDON - The UK's iconic Glastonbury Festival on Wednesday unveiled its 2027 line-up with top names Harry Styles, Billie Eilish and Sam Fender, set to headline alongside veteran star Cher.

Tickets for the event next June sold out in 45 minutes last month with thousands rushing for sought-after places despite the hefty price tag.

Other big names on the bill include Massive Attack, Lily Allen, Lola Young, Kraftwerk, Texas and De La Soul, according to the line-up poster released on the festival's website.

Country star Kacey Musgraves, rising star FKA twigs and newcomer Adela also make the cut, with more acts still to be announced.

Cher, 80, will play the legend slot on Sunday. Aged 81 by the time she performs she will be the oldest artist to do so, taking the crown from Rod Stewart.

The festival held at Worthy Farm in southwest England has become a fixture of the international musical calendar, after first launching in 1970 inspired by British hippie and counterculture movements.

Prices have risen steadily in the last decade, with standard tickets costing £408 ($539) for the June 2027 iteration, which follows the "fallow year" of no festival in 2026.

"We are so happy to be coming back after our fallow year," said organiser Emily Eavis on Instagram, describing the line-up as an "incredible" spread of artists.

World.title: 'Rockstar' climate expert urges world to defend science
World.content:
ANTALYA - He's briefed world leaders and business tycoons, appeared in a documentary with Leonardo DiCaprio, and amassed a cult following with his animated, no-nonsense warnings about the perils of climate change.

For a scientist, Johan Rockstrom is about as close to a rock star as it gets and at the United Nations climate conferences, the straight-talking Swede is in his element.

But this year, Rockstrom is on the offensive as science emerges as a key battleground at COP31 in Turkey.

Debates have dragged over the science of crossing the 1.5C temperature limit while a long-running standoff over the work of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has spilled into the talks.

Rockstrom, who is director of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research in Germany, paused to speak with AFP after shaking hands with admirers in Antalya. This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

Q: You've been warning for years that the 1.5C goal would be crossed without urgent cuts to planet-heating emissions. The UN says overshooting 1.5C is now imminent and unavoidable. Have we failed this goal?

A: "I think science clearly shows that we need to have a more nuanced way of describing this. The first is that we have to admit failure. We signed the Paris agreement 11 years ago and so far we've just added emissions. And now we will inevitably be crashing through the 1.5C limit. That is failure so far and that has to be admitted, because that's the key why we need to accelerate. For every year that we fail in bending the curve, the pathway to safety becomes steeper and steeper."

Q: Where are we heading?

A: "We're not following a pathway that brings us back to 1.5C. We're following a pathway that takes us to 2.8C, 2.9C, perhaps even 3C of warming within just 75 years... there's no evidence we can support the world as we know it at that level. It's a path to disaster."

Q: Does science have a solution?

A: "The best the science can offer is to limit warming, and peak warming, somewhere around 1.8C and then potentially bring it back to 1.5C. And that is what policy-wise is described as 'keeping 1.5C alive'. But that is an enormously heavy lift... and the first step is the most urgent one, which is to put a brake on warming."

Q: So by drastically and immediately reducing emissions, and then pulling carbon from the atmosphere, it might theoretically be possible in future to return to 1.5C?

A: "I think it is correct to say that 1.5C is theoretically still possible. We definitely need to hold on to it as the landing zone. That would be a big mistake to now compromise with 1.5C.

"Exceeding 1.5C brings us into danger in two ways. One is that it increases the frequency and severity of extreme events... but it's also pushing us closer to tipping points which if crossed, would bring us to irreversible changes that would push us forever into less and less liveable conditions on Earth."

Q: Some nations at COP31 have questioned recent studies into overshooting 1.5C -- is the science sound?

A: "This is obstruction, it's complete nonsense, and everybody knows that... these are robust, scientifically verified scenarios."

Q: There's also a separate spat involving the IPCC, with some nations pushing to delay the publication of its next major reports. Is science under attack here?

A: "We are seeing efforts of doing that -- to undermine the role of science as the basis for the whole policy regime around climate. This is highly frustrating... We have to stand up and defend science very, very clearly."

Q: Are you optimistic humanity will change course?

A: "That's the big question, isn't it? If you look at the world today, the answer would be -- I'm sceptical.

"We are in a world that is so fragmented and focusing entirely on geopolitics... In that sense I'm really, really nervous."

Q: Is there any light in the tunnel?

A: "We are on a journey. We're showing that solar, wind, biomass, hydro, efficiency of energy systems, are starting to scale in a way that almost exceeds our expectations.

"We are at this collision point. That is one reason why countries that feel threatened are digging in their heels even deeper. Because they see this is no longer a sideshow -- this is a main show. This is really the path toward not only solving the climate crisis, but it's also a pathway to competitiveness."

World.title: New Zealand, India lean on seam for first Test in Wellington
World.content:
WELLINGTON - New Zealand said Wednesday they would play four seamers in the first Test against India in Wellington, kicking off a hectic period of six matches in seven weeks for Tom Latham's side.

India under captain Shubman Gill will also field four pace bowlers for Thursday's opening match of the two-Test series on a Basin Reserve pitch expected to favour the seamers.

Matt Henry, Jacob Duffy, Nathan Smith and the returning Kyle Jamieson will lead New Zealand's attack, Latham told reporters.

The series sees the two nations clash in red-ball cricket for the first time since New Zealand's historic 3-0 Test series win in India in 2024.

Gill described having to choose which of his brigade of top-class bowlers to leave out as a "good kind of headache".

"All the fast bowlers did pretty well (in the ODI series) and we are still deciding on the final combination, which fast bowlers to go with," said Gill.

Quick bowling great Jasprit Bumrah is almost certain to lead the attack in what will be his first Test match for almost a year.

Bumrah played one warm-up match for India A against New Zealand A in Christchurch, bowling six wicketless overs before rain intervened.

"We know he's going to be a huge challenge especially on the surfaces that we have here," said Latham.

- Race to WTC final -

New Zealand's two Tests against India at home will be followed by four away in Australia, with all counting for the current World Test Championship cycle.

New Zealand top the WTC table after four wins in their first six matches as they seek to become the first team to win the competition twice.

The top two in the standings will progress to next year's final.

"What we focus on is the things that we can do and the things that we can control," Latham said when asked about the WTC.

"And we know if we do that, then hopefully we'll give ourselves a chance of being in the race for those top two positions come March."

Gill said the WTC was a priority for India, who sit fourth in the standings and will play a five-Test series at home against Australia beginning in January.

"I believe if we win these two Test matches we have a very good chance at playing the WTC final," he said.

"Even before coming here I knew these two Test matches are going to be really crucial."

Latham said his players would not be distracted by the launch of blockbuster video game Grand Theft Auto VI, which becomes available at midnight on the eve of the Test, with New Zealand the first country to receive it.

New Zealand's Rachin Ravindra told AFP he had agreed with coach Rob Walter to avoid late nights in "Vice City", where the game is set.

"Well, I'm not a gamer," Latham said, smiling.

"But there's obviously been a little bit of chat about it, that it comes out at midnight or whatever it is.

"But yeah, we certainly trust guys to prepare the best they can for the next couple of days."

The second Test in Christchurch begins on November 27.

World.title: Number Of The Day | 5.2% | 18 November 2026
World.content:
South Africa's 5.2% Inflation Rate Reveals the Real Cost of Getting By

A national inflation figure is supposed to describe what is happening to prices across an economy. Yet for the people living inside that economy, the experience is far more personal. It is measured in how much money remains after paying for transport, whether the monthly grocery budget still stretches far enough, and which expenses must be postponed until the next payday. South Africa's latest inflation figures have sharpened that reality, exposing how quickly an increase in one essential cost can place pressure on almost everything else.

Annual consumer inflation reached 5.2% in October 2026, rising from 4.5% in September and reaching its highest level since May 2024. The increase moves inflation further above the South African Reserve Bank's 3% target, but the headline figure tells only part of the story. Inflation measures the average change in prices across a representative basket of goods and services. It does not mean that every household has experienced precisely the same increase, nor does it reveal how easily different households can absorb those increases. For families already spending most of their income on essentials, even relatively small changes can force difficult financial choices.

Fuel has become one of the clearest examples of how an inflation shock spreads beyond its original source. Statistics South Africa reports that annual fuel inflation reached 42.9% in October, following an 11.8% increase between September and October. The broader transport category recorded annual inflation of 15.2% and contributed 2.1 percentage points to the headline inflation rate. Those figures help explain why consumers are feeling renewed pressure, but their significance extends beyond the amount motorists pay to fill their vehicles.

South Africa's economy depends heavily on the movement of people and goods. Workers use taxis, buses and private vehicles to reach their jobs, while businesses rely on transport networks to move products between farms, factories, distribution centres and shops. Higher fuel costs can increase the cost of providing these services, creating pressure for businesses and transport operators to raise prices. Some may absorb the increases temporarily, while others may pass part of the additional expense to customers. The extent of that pass-through depends on competition, demand, existing contracts and the financial position of individual businesses. The important distinction is that the effects of rising fuel prices can continue to emerge long after the initial increase at the pump.

This creates a particularly difficult environment for households because the costs most exposed to inflation are not always discretionary. A family can postpone replacing a television, delay a holiday or reduce entertainment spending, but it cannot necessarily avoid travelling to work or purchasing basic food. The pressure becomes even more complicated when different prices move in different directions. Some food categories may experience relatively modest increases while others become significantly more expensive. An improvement in the overall inflation rate would not automatically reverse those price increases either. Slower inflation usually means prices are rising more slowly, not that they have returned to previous levels.

The approaching festive shopping season introduces another dimension. Black Friday discounts and promotional campaigns encourage consumers to look for savings, but borrowing to take advantage of a discounted price can undermine the benefit. A product bought on credit may ultimately cost substantially more once interest and other borrowing charges are included. This is especially relevant when households are already managing higher transport costs, monthly debt repayments and other unavoidable expenses. A bargain should be assessed against the total amount eventually paid, not simply the price displayed during a promotion.

The Reserve Bank faces its own version of this balancing act. Higher interest rates can restrain borrowing and demand, helping prevent price pressures from becoming entrenched. They can also support the rand and potentially moderate the cost of imported goods. Yet tighter monetary policy places additional pressure on borrowers and businesses, potentially limiting consumption, investment and growth. Where inflation is driven heavily by international energy costs, the problem becomes especially difficult because domestic interest rates cannot directly reverse an external oil-price shock.

The deeper issue exposed by South Africa's 5.2% inflation rate is therefore not simply that prices are rising. It is that the economy has limited room to absorb another sustained period of higher essential costs without consequences for spending, business activity and household financial stability. The Reserve Bank must decide how best to protect purchasing power over time, while consumers and businesses must manage costs that are already affecting them today. Whether the latest fuel-price shock proves temporary or develops into broader inflationary pressure will be crucial to understanding how much relief households can realistically expect.

World.title: Mistral AI not French president's 'personal project': CEO
World.content:
PARIS - The boss of French AI startup Mistral rejected on Tuesday that the firm was a "personal project" of President Emmanuel Macron, insisting support for artificial intelligence transcended political boundaries.

The French government holds an indirect stake in Mistral, which is considered Europe's top AI model developer, though its technology lags behind Chinese and American competitors.

Mistral's chief executive Arthur Mensch told the Semafor tech conference in California he was confident the firm, which is valued at $24 billion, would enjoy support in Europe regardless of the outcome of the French presidential election in April next year.

On stage, the moderator described Mistral as "sort of a personal project of Macron's" and asked how the company would fare under Marine Le Pen, the far-right candidate currently ahead in polls for the top job.

"We are not a personal project of Macron," Mensch replied.

"We happen to have created a company that grew pretty quickly in France where the president was Macron," he said.

Macron has "been very helpful to the company in the same way the US president has been promoting US technology pretty aggressively across the world," Mensch added.

He stressed the importance of AI sovereignty -- the idea of countries developing domestic models serving their own security, privacy and business interests.

Europe's technological dependence on the United States prompted jitters in the Old Continent after Washington cut off access in June for all foreign nations to AI giant Anthropic's most powerful models for two weeks.

"Wherever we look, the realization that AI is super important goes way beyond the political orientation, so we're very confident that in Europe, we'll still have a lot of support," Mensch told the conference.

He said he had met some of the candidates running for the French presidency, but that "many of them are not technical".

"They need to get a little more technical because there's going to be five years of very technical discussions," he added, referring to the duration of the French president's term in office.

He also made a jab at US giants OpenAI and Anthropic for allegedly using businesses' data to create products that compete directly against them.

"They may deny that they're doing that," he said. "There is some track record of them doing that a little bit."

When asked whether the company would mount an initial public offering, Mensch said Europe -- where Mistral is headquartered -- was the "natural place" to do it.

"We won't be doing this this year, but we're definitely getting ready for it."

World.title: Bezos says 'heavily involved' in casting Robert Pattinson as Bond
World.content:
LOS ANGELES - Amazon boss Jeff Bezos said Tuesday he was "heavily involved" in choosing British actor Robert Pattinson as the new James Bond.

Amazon MGM Studios announced on Monday that Pattinson would step into the coveted role of the world's most famous fictional spy following months of speculation.

"There was something special about Rob Pattinson and his performances," Bezos said at the Semafor tech conference in California.

"Initially, I would say we were slightly biased a little against him just because he's already so famous," he added.

"But in the screening tests, it was so obvious, 'he is James Bond'".

Amazon bought the storied Hollywood studio MGM in 2022, but it was not until last year that the company struck a deal with Bond producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael Wilson to obtain full creative control over the franchise.

It had been fiercely guarded by the Broccoli family since 1962's "Dr. No", when screen legend Sean Connery first starred as Bond, as they insisted on preserving the integrity of the character and brand.

Pattinson got his early break in "Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire" (2005) as Cedric Diggory, a champion for Hogwarts, but rocketed to global fame as Edward Cullen in romantic vampire saga "Twilight".

World.title: Haiti formalises security agreement with El Salvador following troop deployment
World.content:
PORT-AU-PRINCE - Haiti announced that it had formalised a "cooperation agreement" with El Salvador, the same day thousands of Haitians showed support in the streets of Port-au-Prince for soldiers sent by President Nayib Bukele to confront armed gangs in the capital.

"The Council of Ministers has approved the Cooperation agreement between the Republic of Haiti and the Republic of El Salvador," according to a Facebook post from the Haitian executive, who called it "a new stage in strengthening bilateral relations and cooperation."

Signs carried by the demonstrators on Tuesday read "Thank you, Bukele," and "Long live Bukele," according to photographs taken by an AFP journalist.

"Bukele, the country belongs to you! Do whatever you want with it," some chanted in the streets of a capital long subsumed by gang violence that has seized control of large sections.

Bukele has sent more than 2,000 troops into Haiti since late October, after four soldiers from his country went missing during an operation of the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF).

The new Salvadoran deployment, despite being separate from the GSF, has been welcomed by Haitian authorities, who have long sought reinforcements.

"We are asking President Bukele to ignore the detractors and to continue supporting Haiti," a demonstrator who declined to be identified for security reasons told AFP.

Numerous armed forces are now operating in Haiti, with uncertain levels of coordination, including the Haitian police and army, the multinational GSF, foreign mercenaries and most recently, the Salvadoran soldiers.

Bukele, whose forceful gang crackdown at home has won public support but sparked accusations of rights violations, appears prepared for more than just finding the four lost soldiers.

On November 10, he boasted of having destroyed the "headquarters" of one of Haiti's main gangs, accompanied by video footage of the helicopter attack.

Since then, Bukele's forces have taken over a football stadium in the capital with the support of Haiti's national police.

On Tuesday, the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights called on all security forces to protect the population and resort to lethal force only as a last resort.

In the first 10 months of 2026, the UN recorded 4,595 deaths and 2,050 injuries to armed violence in Haiti.
