World.title: MAGIC: The Manufacturing of the Adversary
World.content:
“So we fix our eyes not on what is seen, but on what is unseen, since what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.” — 2 Corinthians 4:18

By Lynn Cruz

HAVANA TIMES – Over time, Cuba could come to be seen as an island full of hostages. The story began with a revolution that promised to fulfill the ideals of the 1953 attack on the Moncada barracks. Fidel Castro had the exceptional ability to turn words into physical reality. A political animal and a lucky man, he awakened genuine hopes for social justice, sovereignty, and access to education and culture.

But when did the story begin to go wrong? Perhaps when one man’s power began to be confused with the destiny of a nation. Nationalizations, debts, and restrictions progressively narrowed the room for maneuver until the Revolution became a Leviathan. The consequences fell upon a people also trapped in a collective identity and a war against imperialism that outlived its central figure.

Fidel Castro lands in Washington, D.C.

From the Image to the Algorithm

In 1959, the Cuban Institute of Cinematographic Art and Industry (ICAIC) was established. Beginning in 1960, the ICAIC Latin American Newsreel, directed by Santiago Alvarez, produced 1,493 editions through 1990. Constructing political images required time, coordination, and control over the channels through which they circulated. That control also extended to the press. But editing is not correcting: it means making decisions about thought itself. Even documenting reality involves constructing a representation of it.

Fidel Castro died on November 25, 2016. He had been a speechmaking machine, a creator of political content whose voice occupied public and domestic spaces for decades. With the Internet and social media, the circulation of images changed. Post-truth found new means of expansion, and those in power learned to adapt. The Leviathan can mutate; its mechanisms of control do not disappear.

Since 2021, we have all become increasingly attached to the machine. What have algorithms changed? And what is changing now with artificial intelligence?

The Manufacturing of the Adversary

I want to focus on October 26, eight days before the US midterm elections. That day, Donald Trump and Truth Social seemed to speak with a single voice. Cubans, accustomed to seeing Granma present an official version of the truth, have historical reasons to distrust a platform that carries that word in its name.

Between 4:33 and 4:34 p.m., four Democratic figures appeared in succession: Adam Hamilton, Ilhan Omar, James Talarico, and Abdul El-Sayed. Four different contexts, reduced to controversies over identity, race, citizenship, gender, and religion. Six minutes later, the electoral endorsements began. At 4:52 p.m., Trump endorsed Sydney Gruters, a candidate in Florida’s 16th Congressional District, wife of then-state senator Joe Gruters, a Trump ally and the current chairman of the Republican National Committee. Her opponent, Kelly Kirschner, was portrayed as radical, reckless, and dangerous.

Attention shifted. What mattered was no longer what the candidates would do if elected, but which side they were on and what identity they represented.

Collage created in Photoshop using images of Kelly Kirscher, Sydney Gruters, Joe Gruters, Donald Trump, and Trump’s second inauguration ceremony.

Congressional District 16 is located on Florida’s west coast, in the Tampa Bay region along the Gulf of Mexico. Under the new 2026 electoral map, it includes portions of six counties: Manatee, Sarasota, DeSoto, Hardee, Polk, and Pinellas. It also includes part of St. Petersburg.

I met Kirschner personally. That is why I was not looking at an abstract confrontation between political parties: I was following people, their stories, and the communities they claimed to represent. His repeated invitations to his opponent to participate in a debate caught my attention. Accustomed to the absence of dialogue between those in power and the opposition in Cuba, I recognized a fundamental question: What happens when disagreement ceases to be an opportunity for conversation and becomes a spectacle?

Kirschner had built his career through community work. He participated in neighborhood mobilization efforts for Payne Park, a public park near Sarasota. As mayor, he promoted campaign finance reforms and, through UnidosNow, an organization he co-founded, helped first-generation students gain access to college. Gruters, by contrast, developed her career within political and administrative institutions. Her campaign defended familiar conservative priorities: taxes, border security, education, and family values.

Kelly Kirschner and his team connect with the community. Screeshot

Florida: The Stage for Magic

In 2022, after Disney criticized the Parental Rights in Education law, known by its critics as “Don’t Say Gay,” Governor Ron DeSantis pushed to eliminate the special administrative autonomy of Reedy Creek, a special improvement district created in 1967 by the Florida legislature to manage and provide municipal services (water, electricity, roads, fire protection) to the lands of the Walt Disney World Resort. The dispute became a political and legal battle.

Disney is a factory of stories. Florida became the stage for another kind of factory: one that manufactures adversarial characters. And onto that stage stepped Sydney Gruters. Sydney, Disney: two names that, when brought together, seem to suggest something more than a coincidence of sound. Magic ceased to be merely entertainment and became a metaphor for the power to manufacture realities.

There, politics, entertainment, and business shared the same landscape of representation. Disney, culturally associated with a liberal worldview, and DeSantis, a representative of Republican conservatism, appeared to occupy opposite extremes. Yet their interests revealed that party colors do not always define the principal boundaries of power.

I ask: “Mr. Trump, did you write the script for Sydney Gruters’ campaign?”

All we know is that there were flyers, a post on Truth Social, and a video that translated those words into images. The written word begins to abandon its role, and in its place—much like a memory—there emerges this fictional image.

AI-generated image: Kelly Kirschner transformed into a knight. On the right, Countess Sydney de Gruters, Joe Gruters, Donald Trump, and his technological court.

The Child as Political Territory

While major technology companies promote artificial intelligence literacy, pro-Gruters propaganda constructed another image of childhood: that of a child threatened by a cultural transformation from which someone had to protect them. A flyer from the super PAC Conservatives for American Excellence used AI-generated images to portray that threat

AI-generated image.

When the defense of transgender rights became part of Democratic discourse, an aspiration toward inclusion emerged. But what happens when a cause ceases to be discussed and becomes an identity marker, a boundary separating one group from another? Childhood became the center of a dispute among adults. Children appeared less as individuals with rights than as figures in a political representation.

MAGIC

On October 28, six days before the elections, an artificial intelligence-generated video appeared on television showing Kelly Kirschner being arrested. The words Trump had posted two days earlier were now being transformed into images.

The image evoked the assassination of Lee Harvey Oswald during his transfer in police custody in Dallas in 1963. But the difference was fundamental: Oswald had actually been arrested; Kirschner appeared in a fictional situation, digitally fabricated. The image no longer needed to document an event. It could produce one.

It is easier to dismantle a lie than a fiction. A lie can be checked against the facts; fiction constructs a scene, creates associations, and leaves images in the memory. It does not need to prove what it tells: it needs the viewer to remember it.

Kirschner lost the contest by little more than four points. Propaganda, however, does not act upon an empty audience: it encounters experiences, expectations, and frustrations that it cannot always control. Nor did the electoral fiction manage to fully control those who entered its stage.

Florida, After Texas

The Republican defeat in Texas has a central figure who was not on the ballot but had invested hundreds of millions of dollars to influence the outcome: Elon Musk. The businessman hoped to maintain Republican control of the state, but found himself facing a Democratic victory that threatens to change the conditions under which his technological projects can expand. The newly elected governor, Gina Hinojosa, has promised to halt permits for new data centers until safeguards are established for communities, water supplies, and the electrical grid.

Musk responded with a statement worth noting: Data centers in space were beginning to look like an attractive alternative.

But while Texas prepares to review the conditions governing that expansion, Florida offers another setting. There, tax incentives and legislation favorable to certain technological investments coexist with growing community resistance to the consumption of water, electricity, and land required by these facilities.

Could Florida become a new frontier for Musk’s technological interests?

District 16 was one battle over control of political representation. What is at stake in the rest of the country is much greater: who controls technology, who pays the price of its expansion, and who has the power to manufacture the images through which citizens interpret reality.

Propaganda can win an election. The infrastructure that makes it possible can determine who will have the power to construct the next reality.

And Cuba? Where will Cuba fit into all this? This increasingly abstract island.

Read more from Lynn Cruz’s diary here on Havana Times.

World.title: Journalist Who Reported on Drug Trafficking Murdered in Costa Rica
World.content:
Costa Rican journalist Camilo Rodríguez. Foto: Tomada de redes sociales

Camilo Rodríguez had reported death threats and declined to enter a protection program recommended by the Prosecutor’s Office.

By EFE (Confidencial)

HAVANA TIMES – Costa Rican journalist Camilo Rodriguez, who reported on drug trafficking cases through his social media accounts, was murdered on Monday, November 16, 2026, while driving his vehicle, apparently by hitmen riding a motorcycle.

The Judicial Investigation Agency reported that the case is under investigation as authorities work to identify those responsible for the crime.

Costa Rica’s Attorney General, Carlo Diaz, confirmed the victim’s identity to Channel 7 and said that Camilo Rodriguez had reported threats against his life and was receiving assistance through a victim and witness support program. However, he had declined to enter a protection program recommended by the Prosecutor’s Office.

The murder occurred in San Miguel de Santo Domingo, in the central province of Heredia, when the victim was driving his vehicle and was shot, apparently by two hitmen on a motorcycle.

Rodriguez frequently posted videos on social media denouncing drug trafficking and corruption cases. He even identified individuals by their full names, linking them to local and international criminal organizations.

“Part of the investigation will involve examining the victim’s background, reviewing all the people he publicly denounced on social media, as well as anyone else who might have had an interest in killing him. The Judicial Investigation Agency and the Prosecutor’s Office will make a major effort to identify those responsible for this death,” Attorney General Diaz said.

He also expressed regret over the crime, describing it as “a very strong indication that we do not have freedom of expression in this country and that if we denounce these acts, we could be subjected to a death like this.”

In his social media posts, Rodríguez often said that he turned over all his investigations to the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA).

The last Costa Rican journalists to be murdered were Parmenio Medina, in 2001, and Ivania Mora, in 2003.

Medina was the producer of the radio program La Patada, which exposed acts of corruption in Costa Rica. He was killed on July 7, 2001, near his home after three unidentified individuals shot him from a car.

Mora, meanwhile, was murdered while driving along a busy road in eastern San Jose, where two men shot her from a motorcycle before fleeing.

In recent years, Costa Rica has experienced record-high homicide figures, with approximately 900 killings annually. Authorities attribute 70% of these deaths to drug trafficking, with the vast majority committed using firearms.

The Judicial Investigation Agency has warned that, because of its strategic geographic location, Costa Rica has become a hub for the transit, storage, and reexport of cocaine originating in South America and destined for North America and Europe.

First published in Spanish by Confidencial and translated and posted in English by Havana Times.

World.title: Xi and Putin reaffirm their alliance on the eve of the first three-way summit with Trump
World.content:
Xi and Putin reaffirm their alliance on the eve of the first three-way summit with Trump

18th Wednesday, November 2026 - 17:25 UTC Full article

Before the opening banquet, Trump and Putin greeted each other in Xi’s presence, their first encounter since the Alaska summit in August 2025.

Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin reaffirmed their strategic alliance in Shenzhen on Wednesday, hours before Xi personally greeted Donald Trump at the airport, on the eve of the first three-way meeting between the heads of state of China, Russia and the United States, to be held on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.

At their bilateral meeting, Xi described relations between the two countries as “as firm as a mountain in the face of any adversity or storm” and called for continued work towards a multipolar world order. “Coordination between Russia and China in foreign policy remains firm and produces good results. In a complex geopolitical situation, we continue to pursue constructive paths to forge a fairer multipolar world order,” Putin replied, referring to Europe’s “humiliating decline” and arguing that the sanctions imposed on Russia over the invasion of Ukraine have backfired.

Hours later, Xi went to the airport to greet Trump, an unprecedented gesture in his 14 years in power which, according to international media, had not occurred since Mao Zedong welcomed Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev in 1959. “China is a country of courtesy with a long tradition of reciprocity,” Xi told him, according to the official Xinhua news agency, referring to the welcome Trump gave him in Washington in September. Before the opening banquet, Trump and Putin greeted each other in Xi’s presence, their first encounter since the Alaska summit in August 2025.

Opening the summit’s business forum, Xi warned that “unilateralism and protectionism are gaining strength” and called for global supply chains to be kept open. “Openness brings progress and isolation inevitably leads to backwardness,” he said.

According to China’s Foreign Ministry, Thursday’s three-way meeting will address how to “preserve world peace and promote strategic stability in relations between major powers”. Trump has said he wants to discuss reducing nuclear arsenals and, according to press reports, also the wars in Ukraine and Iran, although the White House had said Ukraine was not on the trilateral agenda. No agreements are expected.

Trade will also be on the table at the bilateral meeting between Xi and Trump. The tariff truce between the two countries expires on January 10, and China holds a dominant position in rare earths: in 2024 it mined about 60% of those used in magnets and accounted for 91% of their refining, according to the International Energy Agency. During his earlier stop in Manila, Trump promoted critical minerals agreements with Asian partners and approved arms sales to the Philippines worth more than US$5 billion.

World.title: Hamburg tribunal confirms it will deliver its Sea Lion order on November 28
World.content:
Hamburg tribunal confirms it will deliver its Sea Lion order on November 28

18th Wednesday, November 2026 - 14:21 UTC Full article

The tribunal’s statement makes final the date it had announced provisionally at the close of the hearings on November 10 and 11

The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea has confirmed it will announce on Saturday, November 28, at noon Hamburg time — 8 a.m. in Montevideo and Buenos Aires — its decision on Argentina’s request for provisional measures to halt the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands. The order will be read at a public sitting by the tribunal’s president, Judge Maurice Kamga.

The tribunal’s statement makes final the date it had announced provisionally at the close of the hearings on November 10 and 11. The reading will be broadcast live on its website, where the text of the order will be published shortly afterwards.

In its final submissions, Argentina asked that the United Kingdom prevent new drilling for exploitation and the installation of production infrastructure in the North Falklands Basin, referred to in the Argentine filing as the North Malvinas Basin, in connection with Sea Lion; refrain from using information obtained during exploration to the detriment of Argentina’s rights; cease preventing Argentina from protecting the marine environment of the disputed areas; and refrain from measures that might aggravate the dispute, in particular the granting of new exploitation authorisations. The United Kingdom asked the tribunal to reject all the requests.

Sea Lion, operated by Israel’s Navitas Petroleum and Britain’s Rockhopper Exploration, is expected to begin drilling in January 2027.

World.title: Argentina’s lower house debates Falklands sovereignty bill today, with one chapter short of votes
World.content:
Argentina’s lower house debates Falklands sovereignty bill today, with one chapter short of votes

18th Wednesday, November 2026 - 03:46 UTC Full article

The bill, known as the Malvinas law, toughens sanctions for unauthorised exploration and exploitation of natural resources in the islands and their maritime areas

Argentina’s Chamber of Deputies debates the national sovereignty defence bill from noon on Wednesday, legislation that toughens sanctions for unauthorised resource exploitation in the Falklands. Javier Milei’s government is confident of passing it in general, but does not have the votes secured for the chapter on foreign interference, which requires a special majority.

The bill, known as the Malvinas law, toughens sanctions for unauthorised exploration and exploitation of natural resources in the islands and their maritime areas, reorganises defence and intelligence bodies and creates a National Security Council chaired by the head of state. It was cleared by committee on October 27, after the ruling party narrowed the sanctions to operators, licence holders and direct suppliers, in line with objections raised by the United States.

According to Ámbito, La Libertad Avanza is in talks with PRO, the Radical Civic Union, Argentina Federal and Provincias Unidas to resolve differences. The main obstacle is chapter 7, which introduces criminal offences related to foreign interference and electoral financing from abroad. Because it concerns electoral matters, that section requires 129 votes, a figure the ruling party has yet to secure.

The session also includes final approval of the reform of the Central Bank’s charter, which returns from the Senate with amendments, and approval of the free trade agreement between Mercosur and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) — Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland — signed in Rio de Janeiro in September 2025. It is the first of five sessions planned for the final two weeks of the ordinary session; the Chamber of Deputies will consider the 2027 budget on November 25.

The debate comes as the dispute over the islands escalates. Argentina on Tuesday rejected Princess Anne’s visit to the archipelago as a “provocation”, and the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea will announce on November 28 its decision on Argentina’s request to halt the Sea Lion oil project.

World.title: Argentina calls Princess Anne’s visit to the Falklands a “provocation”
World.content:
Argentina calls Princess Anne’s visit to the Falklands a “provocation”

18th Wednesday, November 2026 - 02:47 UTC Full article

According to the text, the visit “constitutes a provocation at a time when the United Kingdom is advancing in the illegal unilateral exploitation of hydrocarbons”

The Argentine government on Tuesday rejected the visit by Princess Anne, the sister of King Charles III, to the Falklands and South Georgia, calling it a “provocation” at a time when the United Kingdom, according to Buenos Aires, is advancing hydrocarbon exploitation in waters whose sovereignty Argentina claims. The Princess has been in the archipelago since November 9.

“The Argentine government rejects the official activities of Princess Anne, of the British Royal Household, in the Malvinas Islands and South Georgia, since they are carried out in the exercise of the illegal British occupation,” the Foreign Ministry said in a statement, which extends the rejection to the South Sandwich Islands and the surrounding maritime areas. According to the text, the visit “constitutes a provocation at a time when the United Kingdom is advancing in the illegal unilateral exploitation of hydrocarbons through the granting of illegitimate licences”.

The Foreign Ministry called on the United Kingdom to resume sovereignty negotiations in compliance with Resolution 2065 and other resolutions of the UN General Assembly and its Special Committee on Decolonisation. “It is time for the United Kingdom to comply with the mandate of the international community and put an end to the anachronistic colonial situation in those archipelagos, which are an integral part of the Argentine Republic,” it said. Argentina also protested against the Princess’s previous visit to the islands in 2022.

Princess Anne, travelling with her husband, Vice Admiral Sir Tim Laurence, is visiting as Patron of the South Georgia Heritage Trust, an organisation dedicated to protecting South Georgia’s heritage and environment. On November 10 she opened Stanley’s new National Sports Complex, an investment of about £5 million, and visited Cape Pembroke Lighthouse. In South Georgia she is due to unveil a memorial at a former whaling station, open the restored Stromness Managers’ Villa and visit Possession Bay, where navigator James Cook landed in 1775, as well as commemorate the explorer Sir Ernest Shackleton. Buckingham Palace presented the trip, which runs until November 20, as a heritage and commemorative visit. At the time of writing, neither the British government nor the Falkland Islands Government had responded to the Argentine statement.

The visit coincides with a moment of tension in the dispute. The sports complex opened on the same day the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea began hearings in Hamburg on Argentina’s request to halt the Sea Lion oil project north of the islands; the tribunal will announce its decision on November 28. Argentina is also in a diplomatic row with Chile over the Danstar, a vessel due to reopen the commercial route between Punta Arenas and the islands in December, and its Chamber of Deputies has yet to debate the sovereignty defence bill, which toughens sanctions on companies linked to resource exploitation in the archipelago.

World.title: Microsoft, flights, banks and now the NSA: a week of tech outages in the US
World.content:
Microsoft, flights, banks and now the NSA: a week of tech outages in the US

18th Wednesday, November 2026 - 02:37 UTC Full article

The outage of NSA Net, the network that allows agency staff to share classified information, was revealed by CNN, citing six people familiar with the incident

The highly classified network the US National Security Agency (NSA) uses for its internal communications went down on Tuesday, the latest in a series of technology failures that in less than a week have hit Microsoft’s email, air traffic, online banking and Apple. No sign of a cyberattack has been found in any of the cases.

The outage of NSA Net, the network that allows agency staff to share classified information, was revealed by CNN, citing six people familiar with the incident. According to those sources, the agency staggered staff arrivals while assessing the scope of the problem, although the failure did not affect its ability to pass urgent intelligence to President Donald Trump, who is touring Asia. The NSA attributed the incident to “temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance” and said “mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational”. According to The Wall Street Journal, the agency was updating its software. “We see no evidence that this was a cyberattack. There is no crisis,” White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said.

The incident follows a string of failures. On Thursday, a global Microsoft outage left millions of users without Outlook email, Teams and other applications for hours. On Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration grounded all flights nationwide for about four and a half hours; the government blamed overloaded, outdated telecommunications equipment, and according to El País the fault was traced to a router in Arkansas. Problems followed, according to the newspaper, in online banking at institutions such as Wells Fargo and Chase and in United Airlines systems. On Tuesday, Apple also suffered an outage of its internal systems after an update, affecting the App Store, its stores and services such as iCloud, according to Bloomberg.

Although there is no evidence linking the incidents, their rapid succession has caused concern. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries called on the administration “to come up to the Hill and explain themselves so we can be informed about the steps that need to be taken”. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy had asked Congress on Friday for US$50 billion to overhaul the air traffic control system.

World.title: Leo XIV after his tour: “There is no need to hate each other or use such violent language”
World.content:
Leo XIV after his tour: “There is no need to hate each other or use such violent language”

17th Tuesday, November 2026 - 16:37 UTC Full article

Pope Leo XIV criticised aggressive political debate and polarisation, “in many situations intentionally provoked”, at the press conference he gave on his flight back to Rome

Pope Leo XIV criticised aggressive political debate and polarisation, “in many situations intentionally provoked”, at the press conference he gave on his flight back to Rome after an eleven-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, in which he also said his health is good and recounted that he spoke with Argentine President Javier Milei about caring for those most in need.

Pope Leo XIV criticised aggressive political debate and polarisation, “in many situations intentionally provoked”, at the press conference he gave on his flight back to Rome after an eleven-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, in which he also said his health is good and recounted that he spoke with Argentine President Javier Milei about caring for those most in need.

“There will no doubt continue to be differences of opinion. But there is no need to hate each other, to use such violent language and to create, even within families, an inability to dialogue and rediscover unity,” the pontiff said. He blamed part of the problem on algorithms and “a polarisation that is not accidental”, citing his visit to Argentina as an example: “How is it possible that people of the right and the left were together in the streets, celebrating and rejoicing over something much more important than a political debate?” The media, he added, have a “very great” role in reducing polarisation.

On his meeting with Milei, the Pope said his message “is not political”. “Although in some countries there are those who try to push me to the right or the left, asking me to criticise or not, I speak of the encyclical Magnifica humanitas. And that is precisely what I spoke about with President Milei: respect for human beings and the need for greater consideration, especially for the neediest in Argentine society,” he explained. “He was willing to listen to this message. It was very positive.” The Pope also argued for a fairer redistribution of wealth and for “strengthening the working class, individuals and social movements”.

On his health, after the removal of a lung tumour on October 13, he said: “I cannot say I am at 100%, but I am quite well.” He reiterated that he will need no further treatment and said he has not signed any letter of resignation: “For now, I see no need, thank God.”

On clergy abuse, he called on bishops to take “responsibility for accompanying the victims”. He ruled out doctrinal changes for now, and said why Francis never returned to Argentina would remain “a mystery”. He promised Mexican faithful a visit: “I will come, I will come!”

The plane landed in Rome at 8.48 a.m. local time on Tuesday. According to El País, more than 13 million people attended his events in the three countries.

World.title: Venezuela uses US$12 billion in US-supervised oil revenue to prop up the bolívar
World.content:
Venezuela uses US$12 billion in US-supervised oil revenue to prop up the bolívar

17th Tuesday, November 2026 - 16:30 UTC Full article

An oil pump jack in Venezuela, where crude sales under US oversight have funded dollar sales to prop up the bolívar.

Venezuela has spent most of the more than US$12 billion earned from oil sales under US supervision on propping up the bolívar, with modest results: inflation has slowed but remains the world's highest, and consumption has yet to recover.

Venezuela has spent most of the more than US$12 billion earned from oil sales under US supervision on propping up the bolívar, with modest results: inflation has slowed but remains the world's highest, and consumption has yet to recover.

According to a US State Department report cited by El País, the account through which Washington has supervised Venezuelan revenue since the January 3 military operation received US$12.263 billion by September 30, almost all from crude sales. Some 98.7% has already been disbursed at the request of Venezuela's Central Bank, which used it mainly to sell dollars to commercial banks to prevent shortages and keep the currency's price from soaring. Venezuela now sells its oil without discounts, at just over US$90 a barrel, and has raised output to 1.22 million barrels a day.

The intervention has had some effect. According to the Central Bank, October inflation was 6.2%, the lowest of the year and the third consecutive month below 10%. The bolívar lost 67% of its value against the dollar in the first ten months of the year, but over the past two months the decline has been around 6%, and the gap between the official and parallel dollar has narrowed from 50% in January to about 15%. Even so, prices rose 245% between January and October, and annual inflation stands at 376.9%. The minimum wage has been frozen at 130 bolívares since March 2022.

Economists blame the limited results on the design of exchange rate policy. “There are too many restrictions on access to the official market,” said Leonardo Vera, president of the National Academy of Economic Sciences, which pushes buyers to the parallel dollar and fuels prices. “The slowdown in inflation is very slow, too slow for the effort that has been made,” said José Guerra, a former opposition lawmaker and professor at the Central University of Venezuela. “The market does not trust the government's word.” Jesús Palacios, of the Andrés Bello Catholic University, called for a single exchange rate and fiscal reforms, with a deficit of 7.2% of GDP, according to that university's economic research institute.

The government of acting President Delcy Rodríguez last week signed a memorandum with ExxonMobil for the US oil company's return to the country.

World.title: The smarter mobile matchday starts with better sports data habits
World.content:
The smarter mobile matchday starts with better sports data habits

17th Tuesday, November 2026 - 15:34 UTC Full article

Across South America, following sport increasingly means moving between a live broadcast, a score alert, a group chat and a stream of statistics. A supporter in Buenos Aires may compare lineups before a Copa Libertadores match, while a fan in Bogotá follows a club abroad through a phone. The opportunity is obvious: more information, more access and more ways to understand a game. The challenge is knowing which numbers explain the contest and which simply demand attention.

MercoPress's overview of sports apps and mobile solutions captures this convergence. Score services, fitness tools, team-management platforms and betting applications now sit in the same broad mobile ecosystem. That makes matchday more convenient, but convenience can also flatten important distinctions between verified reporting, user-generated opinion, advertising and live-market prompts.

Build a reliable information stack

A useful mobile routine begins with a primary source for the event itself. Use the league, club or competition for the fixture, kickoff time, squad announcements and disciplinary information. Then use a reputable statistics service to compare results, shot volume, possession, expected goals or other measures that fit the sport. Finally, use commentary and social feeds for context, remembering that speed is not the same as accuracy.

One number rarely tells the whole story. A football team can dominate possession without creating clear chances. A high shot count can include low-quality attempts. A striker's goal total may be inflated by penalties, while a goalkeeper's save percentage depends partly on the quality and location of shots faced. A basketball team's pace changes how raw scoring totals should be read. Baseball performance is shaped by park, opponent and role. The best questions are comparative and specific: compared with what, over which period and under which conditions?

South American audiences also need to read competition context carefully. MercoPress's overview of what South American audiences are watching points to the continent's deep football culture while noting interest in women's football and other sports. Popularity is not evidence of performance, and a large audience does not make a forecast more reliable. It does, however, explain why broadcasters, clubs and platforms compete so intensely for attention during major tournaments.

Separate analysis from a price

Betting odds are another data stream, but they answer a different question from a match preview. An odds price reflects an operator's view of probability and includes a margin. It may change because of injuries, lineup news, weather, money entering the market or a correction in the price itself. A shorter price does not mean an outcome is certain, and a longer price does not automatically mean value.

Readers may encounter online sports betting while looking at markets for football, basketball, hockey or tennis. The page illustrates how a commercial service packages odds and live options; it is not a substitute for local licensing information. South American rules differ by country, and eligibility depends on location and applicable law. Check the relevant authority before using any service, rather than assuming a globally visible page is available to you.

A simple probability check can improve media literacy. Decimal odds of 2.00 imply 50 percent before margin; odds of 5.00 imply 20 percent. The calculation does not predict a result or account for every market condition. It only translates a price into a rough probability signal. Comparing that signal with your own estimate can reveal how much uncertainty remains, but it cannot create an advantage from thin information.

Notice the business behind the screen

The digital sports economy is not limited to wagering. MercoPress's report on a cryptocurrency sponsorship of an Argentine football team shows how technology brands can enter sport through shirts, partnerships and promises of a wider digital future. Sponsorship may fund visibility and experimentation, but fans should still ask who benefits, what is being promoted and whether the product suits the audience.

The same questions apply to data. Who collected the statistic? Is it updated live or after review? Does a headline describe a verified event or a prediction? Is a chart using the same definition across teams and seasons? Screenshots without timestamps can be misleading, especially during transfer windows and tournament schedules. A good fan keeps a small record of source, date and competition instead of forwarding every dramatic number.

Brazil's official responsible-gambling guidance reflects the same principle: betting should be safe, conscious and bounded. Responsible gambling means keeping wagers separate from household money and treating them as optional entertainment, not income. Set a limit before the match, never chase a loss or borrow to continue, and step away if betting becomes stressful or secretive. If control is slipping, seek confidential help through a local health or gambling-support service.

The mobile matchday is not becoming less informed; it is becoming more crowded. The clearest perspective comes from slowing down long enough to identify the source, define the statistic and understand the commercial context. Better data habits make sport more interesting whether the final screen shows a score, a table or nothing more than a good conversation after the whistle.

World.title: Why was a Frida Kahlo painting pulled from auction at the last minute?
World.content:
Christie’s pulled a Frida Kahlo painting from a New York auction on Tuesday, hours before bidding was set to begin, after Mexican authorities asked the auction house to postpone the sale and document the work’s ownership history.

Kahlo painted “Congreso de los pueblos por la paz” (“Congress of the Peoples for Peace”) in October 1952 for a peace gathering in Vienna.

The work, which sold for US $2.66 million at Sotheby’s in 2020, was expected to fetch up to $3.5 million. The top price ever for an auctioned Kahlo work was US $54.7 million for her 1940 self portrait “El sueño (La cama).”

Christie’s told ARTnews this week it had agreed with the seller to withdraw “Congreso” for further research and hoped to offer it again. The Frida Kahlo Museum said Mexican authorities were investigating the work.

The advocacy group Defendamos la Colección Gelman (Let’s Defend the Gelman Collection) says the painting appears in an inventory that Kahlo’s husband, muralist Diego Rivera, compiled for the trust that oversees Casa Azul, her former home in Mexico City. The group contends the painting was removed from Casa Azul without authorization.

Mexico’s National Institute of Fine Arts and Literature initially said Kahlo donated the painting and that it left Mexico before a 1984 decree restricted the permanent export of her works still in the country.

The institute has since asked Christie’s for records to establish ownership history and clarify when the painting left Mexico.

The dispute comes as President Claudia Sheinbaum seeks to strengthen export restrictions on protected artworks amid controversy over the transfer of works from the Gelman Collection to Spain. That agreement covered 160 works, including 18 by Kahlo, that now fall under the management of Banco Santander.

The late Jacques Gelman, a leading producer in the Golden Age of Mexican Cinema and a business partner of comedian Cantinflas, began collecting modern Mexican art with his wife, Natasha, in the 1940s. In 2023, Mexico’s Zambrano family bought the privately held collection, which includes pieces by Kahlo, Rivera, Rufino Tamayo and María Izquierdo.

Mexican officials say the works sent to Spain are there temporarily.

Kahlo’s auction record of US $54.7 million in 2025 surpassed her previous mark of US $34.9 million paid in 2021 for “Diego y yo,” a self-portrait that shows Rivera on Kahlo’s forehead.

With reports from ARTnews, El País and Forbes Colombia

World.title: Travel+Leisure names 2 Mexican destinations to its 50 best places to visit in 2027
World.content:
The central state of Puebla and the resort city of Los Cabos at the tip of the Baja Peninsula have been included in the magazine Travel+Leisure’s 50 Best Places to Travel in 2027 — and for very different reasons.

Puebla was selected for its culinary offering, while Los Cabos, Baja California Sur, was included in the “For Nature Lovers” section. The magazine groups the destinations by type of experience, without assigning them a ranking.

Puebla and Los Cabos were the only Mexican destinations selected.

The recommendations come just weeks after another renowned travel publication, Britain’s CondéNast Traveller, featured Valle de Guadalupe, in Baja California, as one of the best places to travel to in North America and the Caribbean next year, highlighting the destination’s seafood and wine.

Here’s why Puebla and Los Cabos made T+L’s list:

Puebla

T+L praised the state of Puebla for its contributions to Mexican cuisine, including the staple dishes of chiles en nogada and mole.

It also highlighted a new development: the arrival in 2026 of the Michelin Guide, which recognized 14 restaurants, placing Puebla on the culinary global map.

“From acclaimed fine-dining establishments to family-run fondas, traditional markets, and generations-old kitchens, Puebla offers culinary excellence at every level,” Puebla’s Tourism Minister Carla López-Malo said.

The recent increase in international attention paid to Puebla has helped bring visibility to restaurants and kitchens throughout the state, beyond those recognized by Michelin. At Macuitl Molino, for example, chef and co-owner Gustavo Macuitl notes that his dining room is fuller these days, with lines that, in the past, were not typical outside of peak season.

Los Cabos

Although Los Cabos appears under the nature category, T+L focuses on the proliferation of luxury accommodations in what was once a fishing village and later a little-known getaway.

It begins its review with a new development in the hospitality sector: the arrival of the first Aman resort in Mexico, located in the East Cape. The complex features 18 casitas and, according to the magazine, a single night can cost as much as US $7,000.

Golf courses with big-name designers also stand out, with the magazine highlighting a new Ernie Els course at Oleada Golf Links; Old Lighthouse Golf & Ocean Club by Jack Nicklaus; and Tiger Woods’s third Los Cabos golf course, set to open at Diamante Cabo San Lucas next year.

World.title: The MND Peso Index™ for November: At 18.67, MXN is 4.2% undervalued against USD
World.content:
THE MND PESO INDEX™

Tracking the exchange rate people actually experience MND Intelligence · Seventh edition Welcome to the seventh edition of the MND Peso Index™, part of the MND Intelligence™ suite of data products developed by Mexico News Daily. The MND Peso Index™ is a monthly purchasing power parity measure that assesses whether the Mexican peso is overvalued, undervalued or fairly valued against the US dollar by comparing the prices of a standardized basket of 20 goods and services in Mexico and Dallas, Texas. In November 2026, the index determined that the peso was undervalued against the dollar by 4.2%, an increase of 3.5 percentage points compared to a 0.7% undervaluation in October. This is just the second undervaluation assessment the MND Peso Index™ has yielded for the peso in seven editions. For a detailed explanation of the purpose of the MND Peso Index™, the makeup of the basket and more, please refer to the index article we published in June. You can read even more about the index in our introductory article published in early May. What did the MND Peso Index™ tell us in November 2026?

In November 2026, the MND Peso Index™ suggests that the USD:MXN exchange rate on the date we collected prices in various Mexican cities and in Dallas, Texas, undervalued the Mexican peso by 4.2%.

The Mexican and Dallas prices were collected on Nov. 10, 2026. The MND Peso Rate — the simple average of the 20 item-level implied exchange rates, rather than the rate produced by dividing the total Mexican basket cost by the total Dallas basket cost — came in at 17.89 pesos per dollar, compared with a Banxico FIX rate of 18.67 pesos per dollar on Nov. 10.

The gap between those two figures indicates that the peso — at a rate of 18.67 pesos to the US dollar — was undervalued by 4.2% on Nov. 10.

In the table above, you can see the Mexico and U.S. prices for all 20 goods and services in the basket, the total costs of the two baskets, the implied exchange rate for each item, the MND Peso Rate (i.e., the overall implied rate), the Banxico FIX rate on the date prices were collected and the undervalued assessment for the peso.

Why did the peso’s ‘undervalued’ assessment increase between October and November?

For a second consecutive month, the MND Peso Rate (17.89) is lower than the Banxico FIX rate on the date prices were collected (18.67).

The gap between the two rates widened to 78 centavos in November from 13 centavos in October, an increase of 65 centavos. The widening is the reason why the undervaluation assessment for the peso increased to 4.2% from 0.7% last month.

The depreciation of the peso between Oct. 6 and Nov. 10 was the sole reason for the larger gap.

Based on Banxico’s FIX rate on the two dates, the peso depreciated 3.7% against the dollar over the period, with the USD:MXN exchange rate rising by 70 centavos to 18.67 pesos per dollar from 17.97 pesos per dollar on Oct. 6. Among the reasons why the peso depreciated between Oct. 6 and Nov. 10 was the narrower gap between the Bank of Mexico’s key interest rate (currently 6.25% after a 25-basis-point cut in early November) and that of the U.S. Federal Reserve (currently set at a 3.75%-4% target range after a 25-basis-point increase in mid-September).

The increase in the MND Peso Rate from 17.84 in October to 17.89 in November tempered the widening of its gap with the FIX rate by five centavos.

The slight variation in the MND Peso Rate is due to month-over-month changes in the implied rates for some individual goods and services. The implied rates that changed due to price fluctuations are highlighted in the table above.

7 months of the MND Peso Index™

Through the use of the MND Peso Index™, we have now determined that the peso was overvalued against the US dollar by 2.8% in late April, 4% in late May, 2.9% in late June, 2.4% in early August and 5.8% in early September. We subsequently determined that the peso was undervalued against the dollar by 0.7% in early October and 4.2% in early November.

The difference between this month’s undervaluation assessment for the peso and the highest overvaluation assessment — that in early September — is 10 percentage points. The peso was trading at 16.98 to the dollar when we determined September’s 5.8% overvaluation, whereas November’s 4.2% undervaluation assessment was calculated based on a USD:MXN rate of 18.67.

The higher exchange rate represents a 9% depreciation for the peso compared with the lower rate. The 10-percentage-point swing between September’s overvaluation assessment and November’s undervaluation assessment was almost entirely driven by the peso’s 9% depreciation against the US dollar.

So far in 2026, the peso has depreciated around 2.3% against the US dollar. It closed at 18.00 to the greenback on the final day of 2025, according to the Bank of Mexico, while the closing USD:MXN rate on Tuesday, Nov. 17 was 18.43. If the Banxico FIX rate was 18.43 when we collected the prices for the Mexican and Dallas baskets on Nov. 10, the undervaluation assessment for the peso would have been 2.9%.

MND Intelligence

World.title: El Jalapeño: Sheinbaum arrives at China summit after clearing standby for middle seat 46B, splitting UberX to hostel
World.content:
All stories in El Jalapeño are satire and not real news. Check out the original article here.

SHENZHEN, China — Demonstrating an unwavering commitment to government austerity ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum arrived in southern China on Monday after flying standby in middle seat 46B, splitting an UberX to a youth hostel and eating tacos for dinner.

While previous Mexican administrations traveled abroad on a dedicated presidential Boeing 787 — sold to Tajikistan in 2023 — Sheinbaum’s travel office confirmed that standard commercial economy fares had been deemed insufficiently austere for a high-level diplomatic mission. Instead, the president arrived at Mexico City International Airport four hours before Saturday’s 12:35 a.m. departure of China Southern Airlines flight CZ8032, waiting near the gate podium with a single personal item, hoping to clear the standby list.

“She stood right behind a family of four and refreshed the airline app just like the rest of us,” said Rodrigo Méndez, a fellow passenger on the flight. “When the gate agent cleared her for 46B, she pumped her fist and asked if there was still overhead bin space near Row 14. There wasn’t.”

According to a statement from the National Palace, the middle seat — wedged between a sleeping software engineer and the rear galley — saved Mexican taxpayers about 7,000 pesos in seat-selection fees. During the flight’s scheduled 2 a.m. technical refueling stop in Tijuana, Sheinbaum declined to wait inside the airport’s VIP lounge, instead recording a video update for citizens from a plastic chair near Gate 9 while sharing a vending-machine bag of peanuts with Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard.

Upon touching down in Shenzhen at 11:30 a.m. Monday, Sheinbaum bypassed the traditional diplomatic motorcade of armored vehicles, opting instead for a shared rideshare that made two additional stops at a suburban logistics warehouse and a dental clinic before dropping the head of state at the Nanshan Backpacker Haven, where she secured a bottom bunk for the equivalent of 444 pesos a night.

“A true servant of the people does not require a diplomatic convoy, nor does she require a private bathroom,” Sheinbaum told reporters outside the hostel while waiting for a roommate to finish brushing his teeth. “True transformation begins when the executive branch negotiates quiet hours and air-conditioning settings with five strangers.”

Later that evening, rather than attending a formal state banquet, the president walked eight blocks to eat tacos at Tequila Coyote’s with Mexican citizens living in China, barely making it back to the hostel before the 11 p.m. door lock.

Presidential spokespeople noted that the trip successfully generated enough airline loyalty miles to cover a checked bag for next month’s G20 summit, provided the president qualifies for off-peak Tuesday departures.

World.title: Mexico-US trade talks ‘very far along,’ says Sheinbaum after meeting Trump
World.content:
Listen to this article

Trade was the main focus of a formal meeting between Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday.

Sheinbaum and Trump — who are both in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders’ Meeting — met at The Langham Hotel in the southern Chinese city.

“We held a very good meeting with President Trump and his team,” Sheinbaum wrote on social media at around 6:30 a.m. Mexico City time.

“We continue to make progress on our shared agenda,” she added.

Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard and Foreign Affairs Minister Roberto Velasco accompanied Sheinbaum at her first formal face-to-face meeting with Trump.

The meeting took place as Mexico and the United States seek to resolve a range of trade differences that contributed to the U.S. government’s decision in July to not renew the USMCA free trade pact for an additional 16 years to 2042. Trump is particularly concerned about the United States’ large trade deficit with Mexico, while the Mexican government is pushing for a reduction of U.S. tariffs that currently apply to Mexican steel, aluminum and vehicles.

Bilateral trade negotiations are ‘very far along,’ says Sheinbaum

Speaking by video link from Shenzhen, Sheinbaum elaborated on her meeting with Trump during the government’s Wednesday morning press conference, which was led by Interior Minister Rosa Icela Rodríguez.

“The meeting lasted around 20 minutes and we mainly discussed the issue of trade agreements,” she said, noting that U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller and Trade Representative Jamieson Greer were also present.

She said that Trump was informed about the progress that has been made in the bilateral trade talks that have taken place in the months since the U.S. government decided not to renew the USMCA.

“We can say that we’re very far along,” Sheinbaum said without offering any details on when a bilateral deal might be reached.

“It was a very good meeting, very pleasant. President Trump was in a very good mood,” she said.

“We agreed to meet again at the G20 meeting at Mar-a-Lago,” Sheinbaum added, referring to next month’s G20 Leaders’ Summit in Florida.

Ebrard, who leads Mexico’s trade negotiations with the U.S., said that 56 bilateral trade-related “technical meetings” have taken place. He also said that progress has been made in trade talks, but didn’t reveal whether the United States was prepared to cede ground on tariffs.

Standing next to Sheinbaum in Shenzhen, Ebrard described the relationship between the Mexican and U.S. presidents as “warm” and “respectful.”

Neither he nor Sheinbaum mentioned Trump’s recent tariff threat in their remarks on Wednesday morning. Last Thursday, the U.S. president threatened to double tariffs on Mexican goods if Mexico didn’t stop a migrant caravan that is currently heading north through the southern state of Chiapas.

As of midday Wednesday, neither Trump nor the U.S. government had publicly commented on the meeting with Sheinbaum. Trump arrived in Shenzhen shortly before the meeting took place.

Sheinbaum and Trump speak regularly by telephone and met at the FIFA men’s World Cup draw in Washington, D.C., last December and at the World Cup final in New Jersey in July. However, their meeting in Shenzhen was the first time they held formal in-person talks.

Beyond trade, there are several pressure points in the Mexico-U.S. relationship, including Sheinbaum’s allegation that the United States has interfered in Mexican affairs.

Outcome of bilateral trade negotiations is ‘critical’ for Mexican and US manufacturers, reports Reuters

Reuters reported on Wednesday that the outcome of the trade negotiations between Mexico and the United States is “critical for manufacturers on both sides of the border.”

“The two ‌countries ⁠are each other’s biggest trading partners and exchanged about [US] $779 billion in goods in the first nine months of this year, while supply chains in industries such as auto manufacturing routinely span the border,” reported the news agency, which noted that Mexico’s economy is “deeply intertwined” with that of the U.S.

A trade deal between Mexico and the United States — which both Sheinbaum and Trump said last month is “very close” — could make the U.S. government more willing to back a 16-year extension of the USMCA, although unresolved trade disputes between Washington and Ottawa could still stand in the way.

Beyond its large trade deficit with Mexico, other concerns for the United States include Mexico’s energy sector rules and its trade relationship with China. Trump has accused Mexico of being a transshipment hub for Chinese goods, a claim the Mexican government has denied.

Still, the Mexican government imposed new and higher tariffs on a wide range of imports from China at the start of 2026, a move seen, in part, as an effort to allay U.S. concerns.

Despite increased protectionism against Chinese goods, Mexico is seeking closer ties with China across a range of areas including science, technology, healthcare and clean energy. Sheinbaum, who met with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on Tuesday, has said that Mexico’s engagement with China shouldn’t affect its trade negotiations with the U.S.

Sheinbaum also held a bilateral meeting with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in Shenzhen. Both expressed firm support for the renewal of the USMCA, which was negotiated and took effect during Trump’s first term as president.

Carney also met with Trump in Shenzhen on Wednesday. According to a statement from his office, the two leaders “discussed the work underway to reach a mutually beneficial trade agreement that would create good jobs, boost affordability, and fully respect Canada’s languages, culture and sovereignty.”

With reports from Reforma, EFE and Reuters

World.title: US and Mexico lose ‘measles-free’ status
World.content:
The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) revoked Mexico’s status as a measles-free country, along with the United States and Bolivia, following at least 12 months of uninterrupted spread.

The decision comes a year after Canada lost its measles-free status in November 2025, becoming the first country in the Americas to lose the verification.

In Mexico, the outbreak assessed by PAHO began on Feb. 1, 2025, and reached one year of continuous transmission in February this year. Meanwhile, in the U.S., the outbreak began on Jan. 20, 2025, and reached the 12-month threshold earlier in January.

PAHO explained that loss of status does not mean that there are outbreaks throughout the entire territory of these countries, but rather that the virus is circulating nonstop in some areas.

In Mexico specifically, the northern state of Chihuahua was one of the main drivers of the upturn, as declining vaccination rates in the United States helped bring measles across the border.

Speaking at President Claudia Sheinbaum’s morning press conference on Tuesday, Rafael Valdez Vázquez, Undersecretary for Health Policies and Population Well-being, said that between 2025 and 2026, Mexico registered a cumulative total of 20,601 measles cases among a population of 133 million inhabitants.

He added that there are currently 14 active cases, following a sustained decline since the peak of infections in February, when 1,314 cases were reported.

To regain measles-free status, Valdés said the federal government has outlined an action plan comprising two stages.

The first stage aims to bring the measles outbreak to an end by the second half of 2027. To achieve this, it will strengthen vaccination efforts in areas where transmission persists, actively seek out new cases and maintain epidemiological surveillance in states that no longer report infections.

The next step will be to demonstrate that the country has gone at least 12 months without endemic transmission. With this evidence, Mexico intends to regain recognition from the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) in 2028.

“The goal is to end the outbreak by 2027, and the next step, in 2028, is to move along the path toward having Mexico once again recognized as a measles-free country,” Valdés said.

Finally, he reported that twelve states have registered three months or more without a reported case, including Tamaulipas, Baja California Sur, Colima, Tlaxcala, Querétaro, Baja California, Sinaloa, Oaxaca, Hidalgo, Morelos, Michoacán and Sonora.

Meanwhile, México state, Mexico City, Chihuahua and Campeche have gone between one and three months without new infections.

With reports from The Associated Press and Infobae

Today’s mañanera underscored that there is frequent high-level engagement between Mexico and the United States on a range of issues. Sheinbaum’s meeting with Trump came at a time when Mexico and the United States are seeking to resolve a range of trade differences that contributed to the U.S. government’s decision in July to not renew the USMCA free trade agreement for an additional 16 years to 2042.

Rodríguez’s meeting with Johnson in Mexico City occurred as members of a large migrant caravan continue to walk through the southern state of Chiapas en route to Mexico City. Many of the migrants hope to eventually reach Mexico’s northern border and enter the United States.

Sheinbaum gives an update on her China trip

Flanked by Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard and Foreign Affairs Minister Roberto Velasco, Sheinbaum reported that she held a meeting on Wednesday morning with Vietnamese President Tô Lâm.

In a social media post, she wrote that the strength of the 51-year-old bilateral relationship was discussed at her meeting with the Vietnamese leader. “We expressed our interest in deepening the ties between both nations,” Sheinbaum added.

During her mañanera appearance, she also reported that she had visited a technologically advanced hospital in Shenzhen.

“We learnt about the use of artificial intelligence for health issues,” Sheinbaum said.

“We agreed to have a closer relationship with China on these issues,” she added.

Sheinbaum also said she attended a pre-APEC Leaders’ Meeting event.

On social media, she posted photos from the opening of the APEC Leaders’ Meeting. The photos include two in which she appears with Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan. Sheinbaum also posted a group photo of APEC leaders, including Xi, Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Sheinbaum reports on ‘very good’ meeting with Trump

Sheinbaum noted that she also met on Wednesday with Trump.

“Marcelo and Roberto accompanied me to a meeting with President Trump,” she said, adding that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller and Trade Representative Jamieson Greer were also present.

“It was a meeting of around 20 minutes and we mainly spoke about trade agreements,” Sheinbaum said.

She said that Trump was informed about the progress that has been made in bilateral trade talks.

“We can say we’ve made a lot of progress,” Sheinbaum said.

“It was a very good meeting, very pleasant. President Trump was in a very good mood,” she said.

“We agreed to meet again at the G20 meeting at Mar-a-Lago,” Sheinbaum added, referring to next month’s G20 Leaders’ Summit in Florida.

Rodríguez reports on migration-focused meeting with US ambassador

Rodríguez described her meeting with Ambassador Johnson on Tuesday as “cordial.”

“We reviewed progress in the bilateral cooperation to manage migration flows,” she said.

Rodríguez said that she and Johnson spoke about migrant caravans, adding that she reiterated the federal government’s public message. She and Sheinbaum have stressed that no migrant caravans have reached the northern border during Trump’s second term and explained that the government tries to persuade migrants to return to their countries of origin, in part by telling them how difficult it is to enter the United States.

Rodríguez said that she and Johnson also spoke about the need for cooperation between Mexico and the United States on development projects in countries migrants are leaving, especially Central American nations.

The Mexican government has long argued that tackling poverty and crime in migrants’ countries of origin is the best way to reduce irregular migration to the United States via Mexico.

Johnson wrote on social media on Tuesday that the “meeting with Mexican authorities reinforces the work we are advancing with the Government of Mexico to combat illegal migration and dismantle human smuggling networks.”

“We are delivering results and those results are saving lives, while helping ensure that migrant caravans do not reach the U.S.-Mexico border, as President @Claudiashein has emphasized,” he added.

World.title: MND Local BCS: Stargazing, unchecked growth and an epic Baja 1000 hits the finish line
World.content:
Dark sky tourism, or seeking out night skies whose brightness is undimmed by light pollution from cities, is a fast-growing travel category. Already estimated at US $10 billion worldwide each year, per Outside, its market value is expected to double within the next 10 years. Baja California Sur (BCS), home to the lowest population density in Mexico, is poised to be a major beneficiary, with skies perfect for stargazing in many locales.

Since December 2023, the astronomical societies Mira in La Paz and Merak in Mulegé, in collaboration with the Baja California Sur Council for Science and Technology, have been tracking the quality of night skies over BCS. Last year, they reported over 70 sites around the state with apparent visual magnitudes between 18 and 21, and seven more with magnitudes above 21.5, the threshold for a pristine “astronomical sanctuary” according to Dark Sky International.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by CERCA (@cercabcs)

As these regional vantage points from which to view cosmic glories have been increasingly recognized, so too have events celebrating them. The longest-running of these is “Noche de las Estrellas” (“Night of the Stars”), a national event observed in more than 120 destinations around the country, including La Paz, since 2009. The most recent edition of the astronomical fair, featuring over 20 participating organizations, took place on Nov. 14 in the state capital.

But for those who missed it, there’s another heavenly event upcoming in the state’s original capital, Loreto.

Festival Astronómico Cielo Mágico in Loreto

Loreto’s “Festival Astronómico Cielo Mágico“ (“Magical Sky Astronomical Festival”) brings together students and amateur stargazers, as well as scientists and astronomers — including David Rojas from the San Pedro Mártir Observatory in Baja California, Miguel Ángel Norzagaray from Mira, and Eduardo Sández Aguilar from Merak — for a two-day event in the Pueblo Mágico.

In addition to the telescopes set up for nighttime viewing (including at higher altitudes in the historic mountain community of San Javier), the festival will feature educational workshops, film screenings, visual exhibitions and astrophotography sessions that will help prep would-be entrants in the amateur night-photography contest.

Saturn, Jupiter, the Andromeda Galaxy and the Great Orion Nebula are all expected to be visible in Loreto in December.

Dates: Dec. 11-12

Location: Loreto and San Javier, Loreto Municipality, BCS

Cost: Free admission

Tackling unchecked growth in El Tezal

El Tezal emerged as a district composed of independent developments — from gated communities to condo complexes — about 20 years ago, and although outside the traditional boundaries of Cabo San Lucas, extraordinary growth since 2010 has brought the neighborhood within the expanding urban sprawl of the city.

Cabo San Lucas nearly tripled in population between 2010 and 2020 (soaring from 68,463 residents to 202,694), a massive leap that is still being felt in terms of the associated growing pains. This decade also saw boom times in El Tezal, as developments far outpaced infrastructure and public services. It’s not an uncommon situation in Los Cabos, but each rapidly-growing neighborhood develops its own unique collection of problems. In El Tezal, these include traffic bottlenecks, water scarcity, electrical grid overload, sewage issues and a lack of adequate parks, sidewalks and street lighting.

In an attempt to bring order to an increasingly chaotic situation, the Los Cabos City Council drafted a Partial Urban Development Plan (Programa Parcial de Desarrollo Urbano) for El Tezal in 2024, and recently opened the plan to public review and consultation before it progresses to final approval.



The consultation window runs from Nov. 12 to Dec. 2, with the first public hearing set for Nov. 17 (noon to 2 p.m.) at the Cabo San Lucas Delegation offices in Plaza León Cota Collins.

An epic finish to the 59th SCORE Baja 1000

The Baja 1000 has been run since 1967, so it took nearly 60 years for the iconic peninsular off-road race to take place entirely within the bounds of BCS, with the start and finish lines set in tourism hotspot Los Cabos (Avenida Centenario in San José del Cabo, to be exact).

It was worth the wait. The 59th SCORE Baja 1000 turned out to be one of the most remarkable in recent memory, thanks to the rugged yet picturesque routing and a record participation by Mexican drivers, with more than 121 competing, many hailing from the Baja California peninsula.

Ensenada native Alan Ampudia crossed the finish line first on elapsed time, but ultimately finished second after a post-race timing penalty. As a result, Bryce Menzies and co-driver Andy McMillin took the overall and Trophy Class crowns. Andy’s cousin Luke McMillin, who had already garnered Trophy Truck wins this year at the San Felipe 250, Baja 500 and Baja 400, finished third.

“It’s been incredible. San José del Cabo, the roads, the people,” Menzies said at the finish line. “At one point, it felt like we were racing through a forest … It was narrow and fast, with a great mix of technical terrain and wide-open stretches. That’s exactly the kind of racing I love.”

Chris Sands is a writer and editor for Mexico News Daily, and the former Cabo San Lucas local expert for the USA Today travel website 10 Best and writer of Fodor’s Los Cabos travel guidebook. He has also contributed to numerous other websites and publications, including The San Diego Union-Tribune, Marriott Bonvoy Traveler, Forbes Travel Guide, Porthole Cruise and Travel, and Cabo Living.

World.title: Injured Puma Rescued on Route 32, Where Only 2 of 20 Promised Wildlife Bridges Had Been Built
World.content:
An adult puma in Costa Rica with broken legs was rescued Wednesday morning in Guápiles after it was apparently struck by a vehicle on Route 32, the main highway linking San José with the Caribbean port of Limón. Firefighters received the call at 6:25 a.m. They found the cat lying in front of a store window along the highway, about 150 meters (490 feet) west of the Pequeño Mundo store, keeping its distance from the people nearby.

Police cordoned off the area while a veterinarian from the National System of Conservation Areas (SINAC) traveled to the scene. Officers kept onlookers back because the animal, although calm, could attack if frightened. Staff from SINAC’s Tortuguero Conservation Area assessed the puma and sedated it in a controlled way so it could be handled safely. Rescuers then wrapped the sedated animal in a white cloth and placed it in a box for transport.

The puma was taken to Toucan Rescue Ranch for veterinary evaluation. An initial examination found fractures in its legs, and the animal was expected to be moved to the National University’s Small Animal and Wildlife Hospital in Heredia. Its current condition has not been reported. No driver or vehicle has been identified.

Elena Vargas, director of the Tortuguero Conservation Area, urged drivers to keep a prudent speed and stay alert to road conditions because wild animals can appear without warning. Driving at an appropriate speed gives motorists time to react, she said, and the loss of wildlife on the country’s roads is something that can be prevented.

Wild cats are among the most exposed. The Las Pumas Rescue Center and Sanctuary in Cañas counted 76 wild cats hit on Costa Rica’s roads in 2025: 54 ocelots, 12 jaguarundis, five pumas, four margays and one jaguar. Eighty-eight percent died at the scene. Across all species, researchers estimate that about four wild animals are killed on Costa Rican roads every hour.

Route 32 has long been one of the deadliest stretches. It crosses nine protected zones, including seven biological corridors and Braulio Carrillo National Park. Studies from about a decade ago estimated that more than 1,200 wild animals died along the highway each year. The highway’s widening was supposed to come with protection for wildlife. Its environmental permit calls for 31 underpasses and 20 canopy bridges.

In a report to the Constitutional Court last November, the National Roads Council (Conavi) said 29 of the underpasses had been built but only two of the 20 canopy bridges. Six more bridges were under construction and 12 were still pending. The court’s deadline for the work expired in 2024, and in May 2025 it rejected Conavi’s request for another extension. Conavi said it expected to finish the remaining bridges during 2026.

Even where crossings exist, they may not work for an animal like a puma. A study by Panthera Costa Rica, supported by the Inter-American Development Bank, monitored underpasses and canopy bridges on Routes 1 and 160 for six months. Pumas, collared peccaries, margays, jaguarundis and nine-banded armadillos were never recorded using the structures, even though they lived in the surrounding forest.

The same study documented at least 14 collisions with large animals such as tapirs, pumas and deer. Some of them sent people to the hospital and destroyed vehicles. The researchers concluded that crossings reduce roadkill only as part of a complete system. That system includes exclusion fencing to steer animals toward the crossings, regular maintenance and continuous monitoring.

A new law aims to make that the standard. The Law to Guarantee Wildlife Crossings in Infrastructure was published in the official gazette La Gaceta on Sept. 7. It requires wildlife crossings and other safe-passage measures wherever roads cut ecological connectivity. The law applies to new projects and to the rehabilitation, widening, improvement and maintenance of existing roads. It requires the Public Works and Transport Ministry, municipalities and SINAC to coordinate.

Anyone who comes across an injured wild animal on the road should not approach it or try to move it. Keep a safe distance and call the Environment Ministry at 1192 or the 911 emergency line so trained personnel can respond.

World.title: My Night of Scorpion Stings in Costa Rica
World.content:
I’ve been stung by scorpions a handful of times. It’s like a wasp sting but it hurts more, lasts longer, and makes your lips tingle. Once I picked up a palm frond in my front yard and got stung on the thumb. I never saw the culprit. Another time I was clearing some dried leaves with my hand in front of a camera trap and, again, got stung in the thumb.

One night, I caught two stings while sleeping in bed, the first in the very worst place a man could get stung and a second time on the hand during the removal process. I can’t talk about it in polite company, but it was horrendous. So that’s four times. Unfortunately, that total was going to increase.

I had to get up earlier than usual for work. Being the very responsible man that I am, I called it an early night. At 12:30am a scorpion stung me in my left forearm as I slept. I immediately knew what it was and jumped out of bed, ripping the sheet to the floor. I grabbed my cellphone, turned on the flashlight, and told my startled wife that I had just been stung.

I furiously tore through the bed, pillows, and sheets and looked around on the floor but there was no scorpion to be found. Unsure of where the little devil was, I grabbed a sheet and a pillow and headed for my son’s room. My wife, being the Costa Rica veteran that she is, never even got out of the bed and just rolled over and went back to sleep.

As I walked over to my son’s room, I considered that the pillow or sheet could be hiding the scorpion, so I ditched the sheet on a rocking chair, pulled the pillowcase off the pillow and gave it another thorough inspection. Nothing. I slid into my son’s bed with a throbbing arm and lips tingling. It was going to be rough trying to go back to sleep. The front porch light makes his room too bright and he’s a sleep-flopper. Like a doped-up ninja, he began unconsciously attacking me with his gentle kicks and chops.

After about an hour, I finally fell back to sleep. At 3:30 am a scorpion stung the back of my left knee. Again, I jumped up, ripped the blankets off the bed, and grabbed my phone for light. This time I found it. A big, fat, dark scorpion in the sheets. I flung it out of the bed with my phone, and it crashed into a hamper across the room. I grabbed a nearby juice cup, because my son eats and drinks in his room and never puts the dishes in the sink, and squished the scorpion. My son, being blessed with the sleep of the youth, never woke up.

Not knowing what to do, I headed back to my own bed so at least I’m safe from the sleep ninja. I got back into bed, and my wife gave a little arm tap because she loves me. As I laid in bed with a throbbing knee-pit and, once again, tingling lips, I could only think of three possibilities for what just happened.

One. The scorpion was on my clothing the whole time. This seems unlikely because I was rolling all over the place dealing with the boy’s nocturnal karate. If it was on me the whole time, it should have stung me much sooner.

Two. I just got stung by two different scorpions in two different beds in the span of one night. This seems nuts because what are the chances? The upshot of this scenario is that I am a heroic father who saved his 11-year-old son from getting stung in his sleep.

The third option is the most unsettling. Perhaps one devious scorpion stung me twice. That would entail the scorpion stinging me in my bed, then biding it’s time while I got into my son’s bed, got kicked, eventually fell asleep, and started blissfully dreaming about camera trapping crocodiles. Then it would have had to walk across the house, get into another bed, and sting me a second time. I don’t want to believe this one because I’m the nature guy. I can’t have nature attacking me like that.

It’s currently 4:47am. I never got back to sleep after the second sting. My arm hurts, my knee-pit hurts, and my lips are tingling. I still don’t know what happened.

At least I got a Tico Times article out of it.

About the Author

Vincent Losasso, founder of Guanacaste Wildlife Monitoring, is a biologist who works with camera traps throughout Costa Rica. Learn more about his projects on facebook or instagram.

World.title: Prosecutors Investigate Rodrigo Chaves Over Turrúcares Landfill Offer
World.content:
Costa Rica’s Attorney General’s Office has opened a criminal investigation into former president Rodrigo Chaves, now minister of the Presidency and of Finance, for alleged influence peddling linked to public works he offered an Alajuela community if local officials dropped their legal fight against a proposed landfill.

The Fiscalía General said it opened the case in response to published reports and a complaint it received. The office confirmed the investigation on Monday, Nov. 16. Prosecutors declined to provide further details, citing the confidentiality of the preparatory stage under Article 295 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The opening of a case does not mean that criminal responsibility has been established.
