The rapprochement between Washington and Caracas has also been marked by agreements over Venezuelan oil and by the United States' strategy against drug trafficking in the Caribbean and the Pacific, which has caused the deaths of at least 240 people since September 2025 in attacks on vessels suspected of carrying drugs.

Hegseth's visit is part of efforts by Donald Trump's administration to expand its influence in Venezuela. The defence secretary is the third member of Trump's cabinet to travel to the country this year, following trips by the interior and energy secretaries, focused on Venezuela's oil and mineral resources.

World.title: Europe Tonight: former Estonian President Toomas Hendrik Ilves speaks on the future of the global order
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has arrived in China ahead of historic trilateral talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

 

The meeting is being compared to the 1945 Yalta Conference, which helped shape post-war global power and spheres of influence.

Presenter Mard Gwyn Jones speaks live with former Estonian President Toomas Hendrik Ilves to discuss what the summit could mean for Europe and the future of the global order.

World.title: Germany’s Digitalisation Minister Wildberger discusses Europe's AI race with the US and China
World.content:
Watch on Europe Tonight, Germany’s Digitalisation Minister, Karsten Wildberger, speaking on the importance of Europe catching up with China and the US in the AI race.

 

Wildberger also says that France and Germany are aligned on how to strengthen Europe’s homegrown tech industry, despite taking different approaches.

Don't forget to watch Europe Tonight from Monday to Friday, the show where we break down the news of the day for you with top analysts and guests.

World.title: Faster electrification is essential for Europe to escape fossil fuel shocks, Jørgensen warns
World.content:
Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen welcomed the recent deal struck by EU lawmakers on permits for energy infrastructure and clean power, describing it as a major win towards integrating more renewable electricity into Europe's energy system and allowing consumers to switch from gas and oil to electricity.

 

Speaking to Euronews' Europe Tonight, Jørgensen explained that getting those permits can take five years or even a decade, making lengthy approval processes one of the biggest hurdles to electrification.

The deal struck on Wednesday between the EU co-legislators, the European Parliament and the European Council, seeks to bring those permitsdown to just six months for most projects, a significant push intended to unlock investment and help electricity networks keep pace with growing demand.

"This is about making sure that we have the infrastructure to actually electrify our societies, to get the renewable energy into our systems so that we can drive our cars on electricity, we can have heat pumps and so forth," Jørgensen said.

Critics argue that faster permits do not automatically mean cheaper electricity, citing the lack of investment in infrastructure and the fact that network expansion will still have to be paid for.

EU countries are currently discussing the proposal, which has raised some divergences. Sweden pushed back hard, arguing Brussels would redirect money paid by Swedish power consumers and grid operators to fund electricity grids elsewhere in Europe instead of benefiting Stockholm.

Hailing electrification as a new climate doctrine, the Commissioner argued that expanding renewables, improving energy efficiency and connecting national electricity markets would help bring down energy costs.

"The main way of bringing down prices is to deploy more renewables, because renewables are cheaper than the fossil alternative," he said.

Europe has saved more than €30 billion annually through cross-border electricity connections, Jørgensen added, arguing that the potential for further savings remains much greater.

MEP Niels Fuglsang (S&D/Denmark), leading the file in the Parliament, described the deal to speed up the granting of permits as a "very important step".

The Danish lawmaker said the agreement will allow for faster rollout of renewables and grid infrastructure, to the benefit of our citizens, to mitigate climate change and to boost the EU's competitiveness.

A difficult winter exposes Europe's fossil fuel vulnerability

Despite the celebrations in Brussels over the agreement on permits, the Commission's longer-term electrification strategy is unfolding against an immediate energy security challenge. The deal struck on Wednesday won't alleviate energy prices in the short term.

With tensions in the Middle East threatening supplies and markets, the energy Commissioner warned that Europeans should not expect energy prices to return quickly to normal, even if the geopolitical situation stabilises.

"We don't even know if they will come down. What we do know is that it's a very unstable winter that we are going into (...) We also know that even if there's a normalisation of the situation, it'll take months for the prices to normalise," Jørgensen added.

The warning suggests Brussels is preparing for another winter in which households and businesses could face sustained pressure from energy costs, reinforcing the political argument for reducing dependence on imported oil and gas.

The Commissioner urged consumers to switch from gas and oil boilers to heat pumps, replace combustion-engine cars with electric vehicles and improve home insulation.

"We probably have to prepare, or not probably. We unfortunately, for sure, have to prepare for a difficult winter," Jørgensen said.

World.title: Hakeem Jeffries moves closer to becoming first Black US House speaker
World.content:
Hakeem Jeffries is one step closer to making history as the first Black Speaker of the US House of Representatives, after Democrats nominated him for the powerful role despite a small but vocal group of progressive dissenters.

 

Jeffries, who has served as House minority leader and leader of the House Democratic Caucus since 2023, secured the nod following a closed-door vote. 251 voted for his nomination, compared with 11 against. The move came ahead of a full House vote when the new Congress convenes in January.

Many of those who voted “no” are a group of progressive newcomers, who said in a statement that there is “still work to be done” to ensure their priorities.

Jeffries, who hails from New York, ran unopposed but says he is taking nothing for granted. He faces a restive party eager for a change after voters ousted Republicans in a rebuke of President Donald Trump and his underlings.

'Holding the crooks accountable'

Speaking after his nomination was announced, he vowed to "hold the crooks accountable", referring to Democratic plans to reverse Republican policies and investigate controversial moves by the Trump administration.

"We're going to fight to make sure that, in the face of the unprecedented corruption, chaos, and cruelty visited upon the American people, that House Democrats will hold the crooks accountable, not for partisan reasons, but for patriotic ones, because the American people deserve better," Jeffries told reporters.

His fighting talk came after Democrats unveiled plans for wide-ranging investigations into Trump officials and his business interests when they take control of the House in January.

On Wednesday, Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, sent 12 letters warning members of Trump's family and senior administration figures to preserve documents ahead of investigations into alleged corruption, immigration abuses and the handling of files related to sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

"This is just the beginning," Garcia cautioned.

Since the midterm elections earlier in November, Democrats, both established and newly-elected, say they’ve been flooded with phone calls and social media posts demanding a fresh start.

Last week, protesters heckled Jeffries during a Democratic conference in Denver, Colorado.

Those opposing Jeffries, including some backed by the Democratic Socialists of America, said conversations are ongoing about his potential new role.

“Whether on Medicare for All, stopping ICE terror, getting money out of politics, or ending the genocide in Gaza, our constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate on these issues,” they said in a joint statement.

“We have worked to secure commitments from Leader Jeffries in good-faith conversations.”

He was nominated alongside Rep. Katherine Clark of Massachusetts and Rep. Pete Aguilar of California, who would also be historic firsts, Clark as the first female majority leader and Aguilar as the first Latino to serve as the majority whip. Both also ran unopposed.

The trio will face another vote when the new Congress convenes for the first time on 3 January, 2027.

Jeffries, Clark and Aguilar have risen together, as a team, as the first new generation of leaders of the post-Pelosi era and will likely serve as leaders in the majority for the first time.

When Rep. Nancy Pelosi of California decided to step aside from leadership in 2022 after the party's electoral defeat that handed Republicans the majority, it set the stage for this very era.

Meanwhile, a similar upheaval with Democrats angling for change is happening in the Senate, where Senate leader Chuck Schumer of New York faces a challenge from Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland, a Democrat who’s been the senior United States senator for the state since 2017.

World.title: What the Crimean bridge attack means for Russia
World.content:
Ukraine's latest strike on the Kerch Bridge has disrupted a key transport link between Russia and Crimea. Beyond the damage, the attack could have serious consequences for Russian military logistics and Putin's prestige.

It had been a year and a half since Ukraine last attacked the 19-kilometer-long Kerch Bridge connecting Russian-annexed Crimea with Russia's Krasnodar region.

Now, Ukraine has struck again. The attack during the night of November 17 caused the highway section of the bridge to collapse into the sea. As a result, shipping traffic between the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov has also been disrupted.

Russia's ministry of transport announced a "temporary suspension" of road and rail traffic on the bridge, though later, rail services were resumed. Russian authorities have launched a criminal investigation into what they are calling a "terrorist attack." It was only after this announcement that the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) confirmed the attack.

The Kerch Strait bridge is considered one of Russian President Vladimir Putin's most prestigious projects. Its construction began after Russia's 2014 annexation of the Ukrainian Crimea peninsula, an act considered illegal under international law. The Kerch Bridge was completed four years later.

It has been targeted by Ukraine on several occasions since Russia's 2022 full-scale invasion. The most well-known strike occurred in October 2022, when an explosives-laden truck detonated on the bridge, causing extensive damage and several months of traffic restrictions. The most recent attack took place in June 2025, when the SBU reported that an underwater support structure was blown up.

A long time in the making

The latest Ukrainian operation lasted about a month, and consisted of seven distinct phases. "First, the SBU and armed forces systematically neutralized the enemy's air defense system. After that, the direct attack on the bridge began," says the SBU Telegram channel.

Some Russian military bloggers claim that the attack was carried out with the support of Ukraine's Western allies, or at least using their equipment and weapons.

Russian President Vladimir Putin (center) personally oversaw the bridge's construction Image: YURI KOCHETKOV/AFP

Ukraine has not confirmed this. It has instead pointed out that various Ukrainian-made weapons were used in the attack, ranging from a variety of drones, to FP-5 Flamingo and R-360 Neptun missiles. British daily The Times has cited Ukrainian military sources, saying that Ukraine attacked the bridge without the support of SpaceX's satellite network system Starlink. There has been no confirmation of this so far.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, meanwhile, described the strike as a response to Russian attacks: "Russia is attacking our infrastructure every day, particularly bridges in Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro, Kyiv, and the Odesa region." He said "we are rebuilding our infrastructure, but we also remind Russia that the war always returns to where it began."

Ukraine hits strategic Russian bridge to Crimea To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The impact on shipping

After the attack, pictures and videos of the bridge were shared on social media. The Krimskij Veter Telegram channel has highlighted damage to the railroad link and questioned why Russian authorities have opted to resume train services.

The Kerch Strait shipping channel is also completely blocked by debris. "This brings road traffic to a standstill, but also shipping between the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov," the channel writes.

Indeed, the Kerch Strait navigational channel is merely 120 meters wide, writes Mychajlo Hontschar of the Ukrainian Center for Global Studies "Strategy XXI" on Facebook. "The strait is shallow, only three to five meters deep."

As early as the 19th century, the seabed was dredged to allow heavier ships to pass from the Black Sea to the Sea of Azov and vice versa. "Now, Vladimir Putin's bridge-building efforts have brought shipping to an indefinite standstill," Hontschar said.

Not only will river-sea vessels no longer be able to leave the waters of the Sea of Azov, the Don, and the Volga, but boats and small ships from the Black Sea fleet and the Caspian flotilla based in Novorossiysk will also be unable to do so.

The military consequences

Many pro-Kremlin Telegram channels have been quick to claim that the bridge does not play an important role in the Russian army's logistics or in supplying Crimea.

The Dva Mayora (Two Majors) channel quotes the "Deputy President of the Republic of Crimea," Olga Kurlayeva, who described the bridge as a "purely civilian structure."

Ukrainian military experts interviewed by DW, on the other hand, point to the systematic disruption of Russian logistics. These efforts also included regular attacks on the R-80 highway leading through Russian-occupied territories of the Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, and Kherson regions.

Russia cannot replace the Kerch Bridge with any other land connection, says Oleksandr Kovalenko, a Ukrainian military expert with the Information Resistance Group that seeks to counter disinformation. He expects the damaged bridge will cause supply problems for the Russian armed forces: "If there is a resource shortage during attacks or in defense, then either the attacks or the defense will fail."

The bridge's road-traffic arch has collapsed into the sea Image: Ukrainian Security Service/AFP

That is why he does not rule out a decline in attacks from occupied Crimea on the rest of Ukraine. "There are many launch pads for kamikaze drones in Crimea — in the Hvardijsk area, at Cape Chauda and in Balaklava," Kovalenko told DW. "From there, many drones are launched toward Odesa, Mykolaiv, and the right bank of the Dnipro River in the Kherson region. They also fly over Crimea en route toward Ukraine. Then there are attacks using Iskander-M ballistic missiles, as well as Zircon and Oniks missiles, guided missiles, and glide bombs. And while they don't originate in Crimea, they are brought over via the Kerch Bridge."

A bad look for Putin

Kovalenko says the bridge strike has dealt a serious blow to Vladimir Putin's standing. It comes at a sensitive time as Putin is about to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, China.

Memes and witty comments about the bridge abound on X. Meanwhile, the Russian president's spokesperson Dmitry Peskov has promised to rebuild the bridge and assured that it will be "even better than before."

Andrii Korezkyj of the Kyiv University of Transportation, however, says this is not likely to happen anytime soon. "All in all, I would estimate that it would take between one and a half and three years [to rebuild]," Korezkyj told DW, adding, "I don't think they'll let the Russians build another [bridge] arch like that near the Ukrainian border without interference."

Pro-Russian commentators, known as Z-bloggers, agree with this view. "Unlike in 2022 and 2023, the Ukrainian armed forces are now able to launch strikes against floating cranes and repair teams."

"Even installing a pre-assembled arch under these conditions would constitute a challenging task," writes the pro-Kremlin Rybar Telegram channel.

This article was translated from German.

World.title: US Pentagon chief Hegseth signs military deal in Venezuela
World.content:
On a visit to Caracas, Pete Hegseth signed a deal that signifies the "reestablishment of our defense partnership." US-Venezuela ties were strained for years until US troops ousted ex-President Nicolas Maduro in January.

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth visited Venezuela on Wednesday, met with the country's interim authorities and also signed a military cooperation deal with the Latin American country.

What do we know so far about Hegseth's trip?

The Pentagon did not release any information on Hegseth's trip or confirm the visit, although it was broadcast on Venezuelan state media.

The visit comes after US forces in January ousted former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and took him along with his wife to New York to face drug trafficking charges. Since then, US President Donald Trump has backed acting President Delcy Rodriguez to lead the country.

Hegseth also met with new Venezuelan Foreign Minister Oliver Blanco, who had belonged to a party opposing Maduro Image: Miraflores Palace/Handout/REUTERS

Both Rodriguez and Hegseth touted the new military agreement between the two countries at the presidential palace in Caracas.

Rodriguez said the deal would strengthen training for the Venezuelan military while facilitating access to new technologies. She said this would allow the two nations to "face common threats."

Hegseth said the US sees the deal "as a reestablishment of our defense partnership and the opportunity to work together between our two great militaries."

The agreement includes intelligence sharing between the two nations in addition to joint training.

The Pentagon chief said the US seeks "to ensure the Venezuelan people are not threatened by foreign actors or narco-terrorists or criminals and that they are safe and secure inside sovereign borders."

Hegseth said Wednesday that since Maduro's ouster, Venezuela "has gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner."

How have US-Venezuela relations changed?

US-Venezuela relations were strained under Maduro, who had taken office in 2013. In 2019, Maduro cut off Venezuela's formal diplomatic relations with the US after Trump's first administration recognized Venezuelan opposition leader Juan Guaido as the country's interim president.

Is the US looting Venezuela? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

After the ouster of Maduro, the Trump administration urged Venezuela to comply with demands such as US access to the Venezuelan oil market. Trump had threatened Rodriguez, who was Venezuela's vice president, with a "fate worse than Maduro" if she didn't cooperate with Washington.

Trump has later praised Rodriguez as a "terrific person" who is doing a "great job."

Under Rodriguez, Venezuela has released political prisoners and facilitated the shipments of oil to the US, with the US then controlling the proceeds and returning the money under an energy deal. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has been overseeing Venezuela's transition and is in close contact with Rodriguez.

Elections after Maduro's ouster are expected at some point in Venezuela, but with Rodriguez's government acting favorably towards the US, it's unclear whether they would happen anytime soon. Nobel Prize winner and opposition leader Maria Corina Machado recently urged elections after arriving in Venezuela.

World.title: Would Ukraine trade land for NATO membership or protection?
World.content:
The US is exploring whether Ukraine would cede parts of Donetsk province still under its control in return for NATO membership or protection. Experts warn the idea is risky.

The US has asked Ukraine whether it would be willing to cede Donetsk province to Russia in return for NATO membership. Together, Donetsk and Luhansk constitute the so-called Donbas region. Russia currently controls most of Luhansk province, and large swathes of Donetsk, though Ukraine continues holding a number of major cities there, including Kramatorsk and Sloviansk.

So far, no concrete proposal had been put forward, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. He said he would publicly discuss the matter once the US and NATO member states had agreed on the plan, stressing that he could not make any such decision "on his own." Zelenskyy also said any potential agreement would go ahead "without recognizing Russia's occupation of these territories."

The Ukrainian leader said the US was talking about guarantees similar to those enshrined in Articles 4 and 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty, though did not envision US troops on Ukrainian soil. Article 4 provides for consultations among member states in the event of imminent threats, while Article 5 stipulates that an attack on one state is considered an attack on all. The US, however, has said it pictures bilateral guarantees for Ukraine similar to those established with Israel and certain Middle Eastern countries.

Russia has yet to comment on these proposals, with President Putin's spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stating that "we maintain our position that, in the interest of the peace process, it is not appropriate to disclose details of the talks between us and the Americans."

US special envoy Steve Witkoff and President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner recently met Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky (right) in Dublin Image: Paul Faith/AFP

Budapest Memorandum 2.0?

Experts interviewed by DW are skeptical of the land-for-security-guarantees idea, objecting that the US cannot uphold such an arrangement on its own.

"It seems to me that this is what happens to normal diplomacy when it's been run by real estate agents who are used to selling people something that doesn't really exist," Oleksandr Kraiev of the North America-Israel Research Program at Ukraine's Ukrainian Prism think tank tells DW. He says that at least half of NATO's member states have reservations about Ukraine's accession.

"We'll just end up with a second Budapest Memorandum, it'll just carry a different name," Kraiev told DW. The original 1994 Budapest Memorandum stipulated that Russia, the US and UK respect Ukraine's independence and sovereignty in its existing borders and refrain from the threat or use of force to change its territorial integrity. Ukraine in return committed to giving up all nuclear weapons.

The Budapest Memorandum, however, did not contain any commitment by the UK or US to defend Ukraine in the event of an attack.

A dangerous precedent

Most experts interviewed by DW are critical of the idea of holding a referendum to let ordinary Ukrainians decide whether their country should hand over full control of Donetsk province in exchange for NATO membership.

This is because ceding territory would not only violate Ukraine's constitution and harm its national interests, but would also undermine a world order "in which borders cannot be redrawn by force," Oleksandr Khara of Ukraine's Centre for Defence Strategies told DW. "It doesn't matter whether the citizens of Ukraine vote for or against such a proposal," Khara said, adding that any such referendum would set "a very dangerous precedent."

A survey by the Kyiv International Institute of Sociology (KISS) conducted between October 8 and 16 found that 61% of respondents categorically reject withdrawing troops from Ukrainian-controlled parts of the Donbas, such as cities like Kramatorsk and Sloviansk, even in exchange for US and European security guarantees. 35% of respondents said they would begrudgingly accept a land-for-security deal.

Donbas dilemma: Why Russia and Ukraine won't let go To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

What are the alternatives?

Defense analyst Khara doubts a bilateral agreement between Ukraine and the US, akin to those established between the US and Israel, would guarantee Kyiv any more support than it presently receives.

"This concerns financial support, joint weapons production and development, and the training of Ukrainian troops — everything that falls below the threshold of collective security," Khara told DW. "It is good that these commitments — security agreements, political declarations, and the allocation of funds in the budgets of the countries supporting us — are set out in writing, at least for the next five years." Yet to prevent another war, Khara believes that ideally, Ukraine needs "a nuclear shield," specifically, a "strategic one from the US" and a "tactical one from Europe."

Ukrainian experts already floated to the idea of an alternative security arrangement to NATO members in December 2023, says Sergiy Solodkyy of Ukraine's New Europe research center. The arrangement would see Ukraine join the alliance within its internationally recognized borders, though specific protocols would stipulate that only territories under Kyiv's control would be defended.

This arrangement could be modeled on the German case, where West Germany became a member of NATO first, while East Germany joined the alliance only after German reunification.

West Germany never gave up on reunification, Solodkyy told DW. "That means we, too, should not give up on our territory or recognize the border." That is why he says the land-for-security deal proposed to Ukraine is unacceptable.

"This is a trap that Russia and the US negotiators are trying to lure the Ukrainian side into," Solodkyy told DW.

This article was translated from German

World.title: Israel launches new ground operation in Gaza
World.content:
Israel has said its military is targeting Hamas infrastructure in central Gaza and urged civilians to avoid the area. The fight is unfolding against the backdrop of a dire food and shelter situation for Palestinians.

Israel says its military is involved in operations on Wednesday in central Gaza in an effort to dislodge Hamas militants.

France's AFP news agency reported "intense Israeli artillery shelling amid ongoing gunfire and airstrikes."

A statement from the Israeli military (IDF) said, "The IDF launched a precise operation within Gaza earlier today west of the Yellow Line to remove a threat posed to IDF troops operating in the Gaza Strip."

The Yellow Line in Gaza was established in an October 2025 ceasefire between Israel and Hamas, and separates Israeli and Hamas-controlled territory.

On Wednesday, COGAT, an Israeli military body responsible for civilian matters in the Palestinian territories warned international aid agencies and Palestinian civilians to avoid areas near the Al-Bureij and Nuseirat refugee camps and Gaza's main thoroughfare, the Salah al-Din road.

Has the war in Gaza weakened Israel? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Why are the IDF and Hamas still fighting?

Palestinian medics told Reuters news agency that one person had been killed in an Israeli airstrike in central Gaza and that two more had been killed in separate incidents unfolding in Deir al-Balah and Gaza City.

Hamas — which is listed as a terrorist organization by Israel, the US, Germany, the EU and others — blasted the Israeli operation, calling it "a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement and confirmation that the occupation has reneged on its obligations."

Israel's military countered that it was reacting to Hamas ceasefire violations and the group's attempts to rearm.

The October 2025 ceasefire halted major operations, but both sides have continued to carry out limited attacks. Gaza health authorities report at least 1,600 Palestinian deaths and Israel reports the loss of fewer than 10 soldiers since the ceasefire went into effect.

In all, Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed inside Gaza during Israel's retaliation for Hamas' October 7, 2023, assault — which killed roughly 1,200 Israelis, most of whom were civilians.

Israelis demand accountability for October 7 To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

How dire is the situation for Palestinian civilians in Gaza?

Beyond the threat of violent gunfire and airstrikes, civilians in Gaza continue to face ongoing food insecurity and lack of adequate shelter as winter approaches.

On Tuesday, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) and the UN's World Food Programme (WFP) warned that funding shortfalls and access restrictions put untold numbers of Palestinian lives at risk.

Currently, more than 1.7 million Gazans are displaced, with IOM and WFP saying 1.4 million face acute hunger and 1.98 million require shelter assistance.

With Gaza's infrastructure decimated by years of Hamas mismanagement and pounding Israeli attacks, more than 80% of Palestinians are unemployed, meaning they cannot afford food and have been forced to burn garbage to try to keep warm.

"Families in Gaza are facing their first sleepless nights of a very long winter ahead," said WFP Palestine Country Director Shaun Hughes. "Unless we get immediate support to scale up the humanitarian response, we risk this becoming not only a shelter crisis but also a deeper food security crisis."

World.title: Muslims to outnumber Christians by 2035, research shows
World.content:
Pew Research Center projections show that there will be 2.57 billion Muslims and 2.52 billion Christians by 2035. Researchers say differences in fertility rates account for the change.

Muslims are going to outnumber Christians by 2035, according to projections from the Washington-based Pew Research Center.

Pew said that while both religions are growing, Islam is growing faster than Christianity.

The main reason is Muslims tend to have more children than other major religious groups, according to the study .

"It's the babies,” Pew senior demographer Conrad Hackett told the AP news agency.

Pew data shows that Muslim women had an average of 3.1 children between 2020 and 2025, compared with 2.5 for Christian women. For all other women, the average was 1.6, lower than the 2.1 needed to replace each generation.

Why Gen Z men are embracing Catholicism in the US , To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

According to the center's estimates, there were 2.27 billion Christians and 2.02 billion Muslims worldwide in 2020.

New projections show that there will be 2.57 billion Muslims and 2.52 billion Christians by 2035. If current trend persists, the global Muslim population is projected to exceed 3.6 billion by 2070, while the number of Christians is expected to fall just short of 3 billion.

The US will no longer be Christian majority in 2070, Pew estimates

According to the report, if recent trends continue, by 2070:

More than half of the world's Christians will live in sub-Saharan Africa. This was, again, attributed to the region's high fertility and rising life expectancy.

An African country, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, will surpass the United States as the country with the greatest number of Christians.

The United States will no longer have a Christian majority, though Christians will remain the biggest religious group in the country.

Pakistan will have the largest Muslim population, followed by India, Nigeria and Indonesia, which currently has the most Muslims.

Hindus will increase most in absolute numbers in India, but they will grow faster in countries outside India, including the US

The overall populations of China, Japan and South Korea will shrink, and their Buddhist populations will drop by more than half.

Most countries will have more religiously unaffiliated people than they do now. But the increase will be entirely offset by population decline in China, where most religious "nones" currently live.

62% of all Jews will live in Israel, up from 46% in 2020.

Although the number of Hindus and Jews will grow in absolute numbers, they are projected to decline as a percentage of the global population.

Europe's population will shrink by 17%. The number of Christians will drop by 35.8%, from 505 million to 324 million, while the continent's Muslim population will increase from 6% to 13%.

Growth is not at the expense of Christians, says Pew researcher

Alan Cooperman, Pew's director of religion research, told AP news agency that most of the projected growth of Muslims and Christians was occurring in countries where they already are the majority. He says conversion plays only a minor role.

"I don't think this is a situation in which the growth of Muslims is coming at the expense of Christians. I do worry about mischief being made with headlines or narratives that take this finding and portray it as sort of a clash where Christians are losing to Muslims,” he said.

Gina Zurlo, a senior researcher at Harvard Divinity School specializing in religious demographics, said inter-religious relations are "extremely important" in light of the trends.

"I hope people seek opportunities for greater inter-religious education. Personal contact is important — when people have personal relationships across religious differences, it ‘humanizes' the ‘other' in fruitful ways," she said.

World.title: What makes 'Grand Theft Auto VI' more than just a game?
World.content:
When "GTA VI" is released on November 19, millions of people worldwide will rush to their consoles to play it. How has this video game created such a cross-generational buzz?

"Oh, it's so on now!" is the tagline in the latest trailer for the video game "Grand Theft Auto VI," or "GTA VI" for short.

"GTA VI" is a game of superlatives that's been crashing through records. The hype around it is unparalleled. No game in history has clocked so many pre-orders. It's thought that around 10 million people have already purchased it. There's no denying it: "GTA VI" is a global cultural phenomenon.

A few days before its release on November 19, fans can already start downloading the game. The file is so large that downloading it can take several days, depending on the internet connection. Providers have already registered a significant spike in data traffic.

As soon as the game is unlocked, players can start speeding through the fictional US metropolis of Vice City in a stylish sports car with criminal couple Jason and Lucia.

Miami gets cast as Vice City

To mark the launch of "Grand Theft Auto VI," its real-life inspiration — Miami — is getting a full-scale "Vice City" makeover. This promotional push includes the Miami Heat basketball team stepping onto the hardwood in custom "Vice City" jerseys for a home game, a local festival featuring artists from the game's official soundtrack, and roadside "Vice City" signage installed across the area.

Vice City is a fictionalized representation of the US metropolis of Miami Image: Rockstar Games

Expectations for "GTA VI" are sky-high. Nearly 5,000 people have been working on the game for more than 10 years. Development costs are estimated at around $1 billion (€900 million).

"Based on those figures alone — as well as the series' extremely successful and popular track record — this can certainly be described as a truly exceptional release," says Rudolf Thomas Inderst, cultural studies scholar and professor of Game Design and Game Studies at Germany's Neu-Ulm University of Applied Sciences.

When such an effort is put into a product, it's only natural for people to expect great things, he adds. Inderst is expecting "GTA VI" to showcase the absolute best of what modern gaming can do across gameplay, storytelling, visuals and tech.

Social satire and gameplay freedom

This video game series has been around for almost three decades, setting new standards through its different versions. A biting satire on US society and the American dream, "GTA" parodies politics, culture and the media.

The game is also renowned for its gameplay freedom and spectacularly staged chaos in a crazy world where players can do whatever they please. Shoot down helicopters with a bazooka, go to the hairdresser's, take a stroll on the beach, go to a nightclub, take part in car races and much more.

Pure escapism: In Vice City, there's shooting and dancing Image: Rockstar Games/dpa Picture Alliance

What makes it a standout among video games is how its NPCs — non-player characters, those not being controlled by a human player — are brought to life. They respond based on a player's interactions with them, displaying individualized behaviors and traits ranging from fear to hostility. "GTA VI" has an estimated 600,000 animations for the civilians in the fictional state of Leonida.

'Grand Theft Auto,' a long-running hit

"GTA VI" is essentially a huge adult playground, striking a chord across several generations. Millennials grew up with "Grand Theft Auto III," "Grand Theft Auto: Vice City," "Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas," and "Grand Theft Auto IV," while Gen Z grew up with "Grand Theft Auto V." Generation Alpha might still be too young for the latest edition, but will likely find ways to play it anyway.

In 'GTA VI,' Lucia and Jason play a gangster couple; the players' actions determine how close they become Image: Rockstar Games

Social media has certainly played a part in the series' ongoing success, particularly "GTA V" and its multiplayer spin-off, "GTA Online." Numerous content creators stream gameplay sessions on Twitch or YouTube, and particularly funny or crazy gameplay moments end up on TikTok.

At the same time, a dedicated role-play community has grown around the game. Players gather inside the world of "GTA" to act out specific characters, such as taxi drivers, judges or small-time criminals. They invent realistic backstories for their personas, and many even use accents to stay in character.

Perfectionism has its downsides

The hype surrounding "GTA VI" is not only good news for the game itself but could also boost the entire games industry by drawing more people back to their consoles. This is because the boom triggered by the COVID-19 pandemic was followed by studio closures and redundancies. Worldwide, it's estimated that 50,000 people in the games industry have lost their jobs since 2022.

But while publisher Rockstar Games is well-known for the meticulous polish of its titles and attention to detail, the perfectionism so prized by fans also has its drawbacks, especially for those working on the game. Rockstar, like many other game developers, has frequently faced major criticism regarding its labor practices.

'GTA' characters can relax at Leonida Keys, but game developers face high-pressure workloads in the lead-up to game releases Image: Rockstar Games

Former developers report extremely long working hours and a heavy workload that resulted in health issues. Trade unions accuse company managers of employee surveillance, resulting in a culture of workplace stress and low morale.

Coinciding with the launch of Rockstar's largest game to date, the developers behind it are pushing for trade union recognition. That move would give them a collective voice to address working hours, pay, pensions and parental leave. If successful, their campaign could set a major precedent for the wider video game industry, which continues to face challenges around fair labor practices.

This article was originally written in German.

World.title: US House Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker
World.content:
Jeffries is set to be the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives when Democrats take control of the chamber next year. He will be second in line to the presidency.

Democrats in the US House of Representatives on Wednesday nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be the next speaker.

What do we know so far about Jeffries and the speakership?

Jeffries, who represents a district in New York, would be the first Black person to fill the role. He received 251 out of 265 ballots cast in a closed-door, secret vote.

"Thank you House Democrats. Together, we will deliver bold change," Jeffries posted on X after the vote. "And make a big difference for the American people!"

Some progressive Democrats voted against Jeffries' speakership, with the congressman considered by some to be in the moderate wing of the party.

The entire House will do a roll call vote on January 3, 2027, to elect a speaker when the new Congress convenes. As Democrats won control of the House of Representatives in the midterm elections, claiming at least 257 of 435 seats in the lower chamber of US Congress, the 56-year-old Jeffries is all but certain to get the position.

In a rebuke of US President Donald Trump's Republican Party, Democrats also won 56 seats and control of the Senate, the upper house of US Congress.

Jeffries will steer Democratic priorities in the House, such as possible legislation and investigations of the Trump administration. He will also be second in line to the presidency after Vice President JD Vance.

Progress or not? Democrats, Republicans pick new leaders in Congress To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Which Democrats did not vote for Jeffries?

Following the vote, seven of the 11 Democrats who voted against Jeffries issued a joint statement.

"Whether on Medicare for All, stopping ICE terror, getting money out of politics, or ending the genocide in Gaza, our constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate on these issues," Representatives-elect Darializa Avila Chevalier, Adam Hamawy, Frederick Haynes, Melat Kiros, Donavan McKinney, Chris Rabb and Claire Valdez wrote.

"We have worked to secure commitments from Leader Jeffries in good-faith conversations. While we have seen meaningful progress, there is still work to be done to ensure that the direction our party takes this coming Congress reflects what our constituents are demanding of leadership," they added. "Those conversations are ongoing. As such, our vote in caucus today was no."

Who are the other leaders in the next Congress?

Under Jeffries, Massachusetts Representative Katherine Clark will serve as female majority leader, and Pete Aguilar of California will serve as majority whip. Clark will be the first woman to serve in that position, with Aguilar the first Latino to fill his elected role in the House.

For the Republican House delegation in the new Congress, Jim Jordan, a representative of Ohio, will be the next House minority leader. Jordan is a staunch Trump supporter.

In the Senate, Chuck Schumer of New York is the frontrunner to lead Democrats in the upper chamber, with Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen also in the running.

Republican South Dakota Senator John Thune, who currently serves as Senate majority leader, is expected to be minority leader next year.

World.title: Borussia Dortmund bows to fan pressure and end Rheinmetall deal
World.content:
Borussia Dortmund has reluctantly ended its association with a major sponsor after long-term fan protests. They are not the first Bundesliga club to u-turn, as commercial interests clash with politics and fan culture.

Two years of fan pressure and criticism has forced Borussia Dortmund to drop a sponsorship deal with Germany's largest arms manufacturer, Rheinmetall.

The Bundesliga club will not renew its deal with Rheinmetall beyond its expiry in June 2027, at the end of this season. Dortmund chairman Carsten Cramer confirmed the news on the club's website ahead of its AGM on Sunday, which may have proved a potential flashpoint. He acknowledged that "our partnership has been controversial from the outset" but lamented the loss of income.

"It reduces our financial room for manoeuvre. We will have to reprioritize planned investments and carefully examine how we can find viable solutions."

Though he welcomed the news, one of the leaders of the fan revolt against the partnership, Michael Schulze von Glaser, warned this is likely not the end of the road.

Germans protest Rheinmetall's plans for Berlin arms factory To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

"I think in the end it was a victory for the fans. But I'm also a bit skeptical about what the future will bring us," the Dortmund fan and former head of the German Peace Society told DW. "Football fans in Germany always must be skeptical and always must watch what the club is doing.”

Long held opposition

Many Dortmund fans have opposed the deal — which has seen Rheinmetall's logo on advertising boards and other surfaces at locations such as Dortmund's 83,000-capacity Westfalenstadion — from its beginnings in 2024. It was estimated to be worth between €7 ($7.68 million) and €9 million per year.

At the club's AGM that year, 556 of 855 members present voted against the deal in a non-binding vote. There were 247 votes in favour, with 52 abstentions. This, said Cramer, informed the eventual outcome.

Rheinmetall sells arms mostly to Germany, Ukraine and NATO but fans and critics feel that platforming any arms manufacturer goes against the club's statement of its core values. In that, Dortmund states its desire for "a club and a society that operate free of racism, anti-Semitism, LGBTQIA+ hostility, sexism, violence and discrimination."

The 50+1 rule: Bayern Munich and Cologne case studies To play this audio please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 audio

It has always been clear, said Schulze von Glaser, that this deal did not chime with that.

"In the end, they kill people. They are for war," he said of Rheinmetall. "The slogan of Borussia Dortmund is true love (Echte Liebe). But for me and many others, our love ends there…. I know some fans who have put fan merchandise in the trash because they were so shocked.”

In the Q and A on the club's website, Cramer said he was still a "personal advocate" of the deal but that Dortmund's commitment to the 50+1 model, which means German clubs are majority controlled by the members, meant they had to listen to fan voices. But he also warned that Rheinmetall must be an "absolute exception and an isolated case."

That set off some alarm bells for Schulze von Glaser.

"It's a bit concerning that there are constantly these attacks on professional football — a new sponsorship, investment deals," he said.

Dortmund not the first to climbdown on sponsors

Indeed, Dortmund's climbdown is not the first of its kind in Germany's top flight. Last year, after fan and media pressure, Bayern Munich ended its commercial deal with the tourism arm of the Rwandan government before its conclusion.

Fans had objected to the promotion of Rwanda, which many felt sought to divert attention from its poor human rights record and actions in the war with DR Congo, through sporting partnerships. Two years earlier, Bayern withdrew from a similarly controversial deal with Qatar Airways.

Both Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund have rethought sponsorship deals of late Image: Alexandra Beier/AFP

Elsewhere in the league, Werder Bremen fans objected to their long time shirt sponsor, Wiesenhof. Many supporters took issue with the factory farming practices of Germany's largest poultry producer. Though it was not given as a direct reason for the end of a shirt sponsorship deal in 2023, it likely played a part.

Union Berlin fans have also made their voices heard. When the club signed a new shirt-sponsorship deal with Luxembourg real estate company, Aroundtown, upon promotion to the top flight in 2019, many fans were frustrated at the tie up in a city where rent prices were skyrocketing.

German football's battle between commerce and 50+1

"It's a problem for a lot of people," fan Sven Dobberstein told DW at the time.

"We have to try to find a way between commercialization and what we have at the moment. It isn't easy."

Striking that balance can often be a source of tension for Bundesliga clubs. 50+1 ensures fans have a voice, preventing rich owners, or nation states, from taking control as they do in England's lucrative Premier League or in France or Spain. Indeed fan protests have also stopped the league signing a €1billion private equity partner and seen Monday night matches scrapped. For Schulze von Glaser, this needs to be protected.

"In Germany, the fan culture has an impact," he said.

”If there is something bad or terrible happening in your club and in the Bundesliga, there are the organized fans and they can have an impact if they want, if they stand together and, yes, they can stop the Rheinmetall deal."

Additional reporting by: Emmie Eernisse

World.title: La industria audiovisual española celebra su papel protagonista
World.content:
El sector ha crecido en empresas, profesionales, espectadores y en presencia internacional, pero debe afrontar ahora el debate de ver cómo la inteligencia artificial va a cambiar el papel de los creadores

La bola negra, la aclamada película de Javier Calvo y Javier Ambrossi, se ha convertido en uno de los principales temas de conversación entre los amantes del cine. Y también entre los profesionales de esta industria. Ignacio Segura, director ejecutivo de DeAPlaneta Entertainment, una de las principales compañías españolas de distribución y producción cinematográfica, celebra la gran acogida que ha tenido en taquilla la cinta de Los Javis. Y así se lo reconoce a Juan Carlos Tous, cofundador de Filmin, la principal plataforma nacional de streaming, cuya compañía integra desde este verano a Elastica, distribuidora en España de La bola negra. Para Tous, sin embargo, el impacto de la película va más allá de las cifras y se refleja también en el interés que está despertando entre las nuevas generaciones: “Ves el público joven que se acerca, que descubre quién era Lorca, que descubre cosas sobre la Guerra Civil española, que le está retando a saber más”, apunta durante la conversación que ambos comparten en el nuevo capítulo de El poder de las empresas, el pódcast de los que hacen, de Banco Sabadell.

La película es el éxito más reciente de una industria que crece de manera sostenida tras el fuerte impacto de la pandemia, señala Segura. Un informe del Observatorio Nacional de Tecnología y Sociedad (ONTSI) cifra en 3.776 las empresas dedicadas a actividades cinematográficas, de vídeo y programas de televisión que existían en 2025, frente a las 2.901 de 2020, lo que supone un crecimiento del 30,2 %. A esta evolución se suma el progresivo regreso del público a las salas, cuya afluencia podría recuperar este año o el próximo los niveles previos a la pandemia, según Segura. Una recuperación que refuerza el buen momento de un sector que representa el 0,65 % del producto interior bruto (PIB) nacional y emplea a 63.000 personas.

“En 2007 se nos decía que el 'streaming' no funcionaría porque nadie pagaba por ver cine. Sabíamos que el futuro del cine sería la distribución por internet” Juan Carlos Tous, cofundador de Filmin, sobre los primeros pasos del negocio en España

Las fortalezas Un sector con escuelas de prestigio y vocación internacional

Distinguido por su talento creativo. España cuenta con una nutrida cantera de directores, guionistas, actores y profesionales técnicos altamente cualificados y experimentados, explica Juan Manuel Guimeráns, presidente de la Spain Film Commission, organización dedicada a atraer rodajes audiovisuales al país. Conforman una industria cinematográfica y televisiva consolidada que ha demostrado capacidad para abordar todos los géneros, del suspense a la ciencia ficción, pasando por la comedia y el drama histórico.

Con escuelas de prestigio. Dos centros educativos españoles figuran entre los 15 mejores de todo el mundo, de acuerdo con la revista estadounidenseThe Hollywood Reporter dedicada a las noticias sobre espectáculos. Sonla Escuela de Cinematografía y del Audiovisual de la Comunidad de Madrid (ECAM) y la Escola Superior de Cinema i Audiovisuals de Catalunya(ESCAC).

Con visibilidad en el extranjero. El sector impulsa la marca España de tres maneras.

La exportación de contenidos. Las producciones españolas han ganado relevancia en el extranjero gracias a directores como Alejandro Amenábar y Juan Antonio Bayona, series como La casa de papel y Élite, y empresas como El Ranchito, especializada en efectos visuales para Hollywood.

La coproducción internacional. Guimeráns señala que cada vez más países quieren coproducir con España sus proyectos.

La atracción de rodajes. “Este es un país seguro, que dispone de todo tipo de paisajes en muy pocos kilómetros cuadrados. Además, hay buenos incentivos fiscales y unas redes de logística y servicios complementarios, como catering o transporte, óptimas”, resalta el presidente de la Spain Film Commission.

Una potencia de la animación. España cuenta con profesionales altamente cualificados que desarrollan series y películas animadas que triunfan en todo el mundo, indica Guimeráns. El sector cuenta con los éxitos recientesde Robot Dreams (2023) y Buffalo Kids (2024), que recaudaron en el mundo el doble de lo que costaron.

“Estamos en un resurgir de las salas de cine, viendo cómo mucha gente joven acude porque así rompe con la rutina, sale de casa, deja el móvil, queda con sus amigos. Cuando hay una buena película mueve a la gente” Juan Carlos Tous, cofundador de Filmin, sobre la relación de los más jóvenes con el cine

Los desafíos Fomentar el empleo femenino y adaptarse a los cambios que ha traído la inteligencia artificial

El impacto de la inteligencia artificial. La irrupción de la IA no solo ha traído nuevas herramientas tecnológicas; está cambiado la manera de crear, producir y distribuir películas y ha abierto debates sobre el futuro de los profesionales y sus derechos. El reto en este sector, incide Guimeráns, va a ser gestionar la propiedad intelectual de todas las creaciones, de la imagen de las personas a los guiones y la música. Sin embargo, el presidente de la Spain Film Comission cree que la IA abre nuevas oportunidades para la creación y pone un ejemplo: “Una empresa española acaba de crear un gemelo digital de la biblioteca y el patio del Monasterio del Escorial. Muchos pueden pensar que eso hará que nadie quiera venir ya a rodar aquí, pero lo que va a permitir es dar posibilidad a todos los rodajes a los que Patrimonio tiene que decir que no por tener el calendario copado o porque suponen un riesgo para el estado del edificio”, explica.

Combatir la desigualdad. El desequilibrio entre hombres y mujeres es patente en casi todas las profesiones de esta industria, especialmente en los puestos de dirección y responsabilidad técnica. Según el informe anual de la Asociación de Mujeres Cineastas y de Medios Audiovisuales (CIMA), en 2024, las mujeres ocupaban el 38 % de los principales puestos de responsabilidad en los largometrajes españoles, frente al 62 % de los hombres.

Adaptarse a nuevos hábitos de consumo. El público está cada vez más disperso entre plataformas, salas, televisión y redes sociales. El consumo se desplaza hacia formatos más cortos y las audiencias se fragmentan en comunidades con intereses muy específicos. El reto de la industria está en saber cómo llevar a este público hacia el consumo tradicional o desarrollar contenidos y modelos de distribución adaptados a estas nuevas formas.

“Desde la pandemia, el público ha tardado en volver a las salas, tanto es así que este es el primer año en que se espera que la recaudación supere a la de 2019” Ignacio Segura, director ejecutivo de DeAPlaneta, sobre la paulatina recuperación del negocio de la exhibición de películas

World.title: “Amas da Terra son mujeres que protegen la tradición gallega y tejen las redes del futuro”
World.content:
El proyecto de la chef Lucía Freitas actúa como punto de encuentro para las artesanas, cocineras y otras profesionales gallegas que, con oficios tradicionales, constituyen la esencia vital de un territorio y ensalzan sus señas de identidad, como la gastronomía

La iniciativa de Amas da Terra surgió durante un viaje a Japón de la chef Lucía Freitas (Santiago de Compostela, 44 años). Allí conoció a las amas, las legendarias buceadoras dedicadas a la pesca a pulmón; y encontró en ellas un reflejo de muchas mujeres de su tierra. Inspirada por su ejemplo, impulsó un proyecto social para reunir, apoyar y poner en valor a las trabajadoras gallegas. “Amas da Terra son una inmensa minoría de mujeres que, con su trabajo, protegen la tradición, nuestra cultura y también tejen las redes del futuro”, explica la fundadora del restaurante A Tafona, que cuenta con una estrella Michelin y tres Soles Repsol, y de la barra gastronómica Lume, ambos en Santiago de Compostela.

Freitas ha promovido una comunidad de pequeñas productoras, artesanas y viticultoras; también de redeiras, que cosen, montan, reparan y unen las redes y los aparejos de pesca; muiñeiras, que trabajan en los molinos de agua; y cocineras profesionales que alimentan las zonas rurales. Tres de ellas regentan locales especialmente singulares en Lugo, que abren sus cocinas para dejar que los clientes se sienten a comer alrededor de la cocina de leña. Son oficios minoritarios y populares, que forman parte de la identidad del territorio y que, gracias a personas como ellas, siguen vigentes. Freitas considera que ellas son quienes mejor representan a cada comarca, pueblo o aldea de su región.

La vocación de Freitas comparte la misma esencia de Gastronomía para una Inmensa Minoría, la iniciativa de Cervezas 1906 que se creó para destacar a aquellos proyectos culinarios que parten de la tradición para innovar. Lo conduce la chef Verónica Gómez, quien pregunta a las integrantes de Amas da Terra sobre lo que sienten al defender ocupaciones tan únicas. El objetivo de Freitas es que esa particularidad sea compartida: crear un espacio de encuentro en el que puedan surgir sinergias. Quiere ayudar a mejorar sus ecosistemas laborales y que ellas se sientan acompañadas y valoradas.

World.title: Las acciones de Take-Two se disparan un 7% horas antes del estreno del GTA VI
World.content:
La fiebre por el estreno de GTA VI traspasa los mandos de los jugadores y se deja sentir en Wall Street. Las acciones de Take-Two, propietaria de Rockstar Games, desarrolladora del videojuego, suben un 7% en la apertura de la Bolsa estadounidense, a pocas horas del lanzamiento de uno de los títulos más esperados de la historia del entretenimiento. Tras 13 años de expectación y varios retrasos, el juego llegará este jueves, 19 de noviembre, a las consolas PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X y S y promete una movilización de jugadores (y de recaudación por ventas) sin precedentes.

De hecho, el negocio ha empezado a dar sus frutos antes de que se lance el videojuego. Según las estimaciones de Sensor Tower, el portal que se usa como referencia en el sector, GTA VI acumula ya 17 millones de copias reservadas e ingresos por 1.650 millones de dólares. Las estimaciones de Bloomberg esperan unas ventas de entre 40 y 60 millones para el primer año y la gran acogida del juego podría elevar el resultado hacia la parte alta de ese rango.

Para Take-Two, el lanzamiento supone mucho más que un éxito comercial puntual. La empresa prevé registrar entre 8.000 y 8.200 millones de dólares en reservas durante su ejercicio fiscal 2027, impulsada en buena medida por las ventas de GTA VI, cuya edición estándar sale a la venta por 79,99 euros y la premium por 99,99 euros. El consejero delegado del grupo, Strauss Zelnick, ya ha asegurado que las reservas están superando ampliamente las expectativas iniciales.

Las primeras valoraciones están alimentando ese optimismo. GTA VI ha conseguido una puntuación de 99 sobre 100 en Metacritic, un portal que recopila las críticas de videojuegos de medios especializados a partir de más de 100 reseñas. Esa nota iguala la nota más alta publicada en la historia de la plataforma y supera el 97 que consiguió la edición anterior del juego, el GTA V.

Las dimensiones del fenómeno ayudan a explicar el entusiasmo bursátil. Grand Theft Auto se ha convertido en una de las franquicias más exitosas de la industria del entretenimiento. Su anterior entrega llegó al mercado en 2013 y se ha mantenido durante más de una década entre los videojuegos más vendidos.

Por ello, el desafío será estar a la altura de las enormes expectativas. Los inversores no solo estarán pendientes de las ventas de los primeros días, sino también de la recepción del público y de la capacidad de Rockstar para convertir el lanzamiento en una fuente de ingresos recurrentes durante los próximos años. Después de trece años de espera, GTA VI quiere superar el fenómeno generado por su predecesor.

World.title: Las marcas de lujo se pelean por estar con Robert Pattinson, el nuevo James Bond
World.content:
La pantalla de Piccadilly Circus muestra un anuncio en el que se indica que el actor británico Robert Pattinson será el próximo James Bond en una próxima película de Amazon MGM Studios, en Londres.

Omega, Aston Martin y Tom Ford se enfrentan a la competencia en una nueva era del espía inglés más famoso

James Bond tiene un nuevo protagonista masculino, y las marcas de lujo ya están compitiendo por un papel junto a él. Más de 60 años después de que Dr. No presentara a 007 al público cinematográfico, Bond sigue siendo uno de los vehículos de marketing más codiciados del mundo, con fabricantes de relojes, automóviles, casas de moda y marcas de bebidas que gastan millones en torno a cada película con la esperanza de asociarse con el agente secreto más conocido de Gran Bretaña.

La elección de Robert Pattinson, de 40 años, pone fin a años de especulaciones sobre quién heredaría el papel después de que la franquicia eliminara al Bond de Daniel Craig en Sin tiempo para morir (2021). Craig usaba relojes Omega y conducía un Aston Martin y fue vestido por Tom Ford. Según expertos en marcas, la primera película de Bond producida por Amazon MGM Studios y dirigida por Denis Villeneuve ofrece una oportunidad única para que los grupos de lujo transformen una de las carteras de emplazamiento de productos más vigiladas de Hollywood.

“James Bond ocupa un lugar especial en términos de imagen de marca”, dijo Eric Nebot, fundador y director ejecutivo de la agencia de colocación de productos Hill Valley, que trabajó con la joyería suiza Chopard en Sin tiempo para morir. “Es un icono del cine que se ha forjado en parte gracias a la ropa que viste, las marcas que usa y los cócteles que bebe.”

La presentación de Pattinson como Bond —sin reloj en la muñeca— causó revuelo en la industria de la publicidad encubierta de Hollywood. El actor atrae a hombres y mujeres de todas las generaciones, desde sus primeros seguidores de Crepúsculo hasta los de Batman.

“Me encanta la elección de Pattinson. Nos da mucho con lo que trabajar”, dijo Britt Johnson, CEO y fundador de Mediaplacement, una agencia que colocó a Diageo con el Vodka Smirnoff en el martini característico de Bond en la película de 2021. “Para Bond, tener una audiencia femenina es muy, muy importante”, añadió, haciendo referencia a la posición de Pattinson en el mundo de la moda.

Pattinson ha sido embajador de LVMH durante más de una década y en septiembre se convirtió en la imagen global de la marca suiza de relojes de lujo Jaeger-LeCoultre, propiedad de Richemont.

Guerra de relojes de pulsera

El acuerdo de Pattinson con Jaeger-LeCoultre podría crear tensiones con Swatch Omega, la marca oficial de relojes de Bond desde que Pierce Brosnan lució uno en GoldenEye (1995). Películas anteriores, así como las novelas originales de Ian Fleming, asociaban a Bond con Rolex.

“La categoría de relojes probablemente será el mayor conflicto a resolver”, afirmó Anne Biskin, cofundadora de SMG Entertainment en Portland, Oregón. Añadió que las marcas involucradas en películas anteriores de Bond podrían tener derecho de preferencia para regresar. Omega declinó hacer comentarios. Jaeger-LeCoultre no respondió de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios. Amazon MGM declaró que era demasiado pronto para comentar sobre posibles colaboraciones de marca.

Según fuentes del sector, los acuerdos publicitarios vigentes de Pattinson no se transferirían automáticamente a Bond, y es probable que Villeneuve y los productores tengan la última palabra sobre qué marcas aparecen en pantalla.

Dior publicó un mensaje de felicitación junto a una foto de Pattinson en Instagram el martes. La casa de moda francesa también podría intentar desbancar a Tom Ford, que ha suministrado los trajes de Bond desde Quantum of Solace en 2008, según Biskin.

Dior declaró estar “muy complacida de continuar” con Pattinson, quien ha sido embajador de moda y fragancias de la marca desde 2013, pero no hizo comentarios sobre posibles acuerdos con Bond. Tom Ford no respondió de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios. Desde el anuncio, Jaeger-LeCoultre también ha publicado tres fotografías de Pattinson en Instagram, aunque no mencionó su nuevo papel.

Imaginación de Villeneuve

A pesar del atractivo de Bond para las marcas de lujo, tanto Villeneuve como Pattinson se asocian con un enfoque más sobrio y artístico que el de muchas superproducciones de Hollywood, lo que podría limitar los vínculos comerciales explícitos e intensificar la competencia por un número menor de espacios publicitarios.

“Interpreto que la elección de alguien como Robert, que parece compartir la misma selectividad y preferencia por el lujo discreto, significa que no buscan que esta película sea excesivamente comercial”, dijo Biskin, añadiendo que era probable que Pattinson aportara una interpretación más oscura y menos convencional de Bond.

Con el estreno de la próxima película previsto para 2028, siete años después de la entrega anterior, las marcas también se enfrentan a un público más exigente, y los espectadores más jóvenes son especialmente críticos con las colaboraciones comerciales que parecen forzadas.

La franquicia también se ha enfrentado a la presión de evolucionar, y algunos críticos argumentan que la imagen machista tradicional de Bond no encaja bien con el público moderno.

Aston Martin, cuyos coches han aparecido en alrededor de una docena de películas de Bond, declinó hacer comentarios sobre si esperaba aparecer en el próximo estreno. “El dinero no será el factor decisivo en la próxima película de James Bond... Creo que el reloj que llevará dependerá de la historia”, dijo Nebot. “Todo esto está en la imaginación de Villeneuve”.

World.title: Así se pensó, diseñó y construyó uno de los museos más sostenibles del mundo
World.content:
El antiguo edificio Pereda de Santander ha alcanzado la máxima calificación BREEAM obtenida por un museo gracias a una rehabilitación que combina soluciones arquitectónicas singulares, tecnologías pioneras y una gestión integral de la sostenibilidad. Este proyecto que preserva su patrimonio mirando al futuro recibirá este noviembre su certificado definitivo

Dos edificios decimonónicos anexos, sede histórica del Banco Santander en el paseo de Pereda y frente al mar, se han convertido en uno de los museos más excepcionales y sostenibles del mundo. Así lo refleja el 92,96% obtenido en la certificación BREEAM, uno de los sistemas de evaluación con mayor trayectoria y reconocimiento internacional, que analiza distintas categorías como la eficiencia ambiental, el confort o la salubridad.

Es la máxima nota recibida hasta hoy por una institución museística en todo el planeta en este sistema de medida, un logro —más destacado si cabe por tratarse de una rehabilitación y no de un inmueble de nueva planta— cuyo mérito se reparten el estudio de arquitectura del ganador del Pritzker David Chipperfield, la firma de servicios de ingeniería, consultoría y arquitectura IDOM y el mismo Banco Santander, impulsor de un diseño pensado para la excelencia, para durar. Contamos cómo se ideó y parió Faro Santander.

Los diez criterios BREEAM para medir un museo sostenible BREEAM es un sistema internacional de evaluación y certificación de la sostenibilidad de los edificios 01 Gestión Seguimiento de consumos y control de residuos durante la obra 02 Confort y bienestar Climatización TABS, aire filtrado y control de humedad y CO₂ 03 Energía Geotermia y aprovechamiento de la inercia térmica del hormigón 04 Transporte Aparcamientos para bicicletas y acceso en transporte público 05 Agua Recogida de lluvia para aseos y riego de jardines 06 Materiales Recuperación de suelos, madera y piedra del edificio original 07 Residuos El 98 % de los residuos fueron reutilizados o reciclados 08 Uso del suelo y ecología Terrazas ajardinadas, polinizadores y recuperación de arbolado 09 Contaminación Energía de origen 100% renovable y medidas contra la contaminación acústica 10 Innovación Combinación pionera de geotermia y climatización TABS en una rehabilitación

“El edificio de Pereda era fundamental para la ciudad y estaba cerrado. Fueron oficinas. Y había que hacer de él un edificio público, abierto a la gente: que desde dentro uno estuviera en contacto con Santander y desde fuera tuviera ganas de internarse”, recuerda Jose Azevedo, arquitecto portugués responsable de proyectos del estudio de Chipperfield.

Hallar una forma que respaldase esa concepción tan crucial para el tipo de museo naciente fue el primer y gran reto del encargo. Una singularidad que traía aparejada su recompensa: “Normalmente”, cuenta Azevedo, “cuando llevas a cabo la rehabilitación o construcción de un museo, te basas en la historia y principios de la institución, sus necesidades instruyen al arquitecto. Aquí estábamos entre todos dando a luz a la institución. De alguna manera, nos sentimos parte fundadora de ese carácter que va a definir a Faro Santander”. Un lugar de exhibición y creación, para el arte y la tecnología. Para la gente.

Gracias a la combinación de la geotermia y la termoactivación de los forjados (TABS), que aprovecha la masa térmica del hormigón mediante circuitos de agua integrados en la estructura, el propio edificio contribuye a proporcionar calefacción y refrigeración

Las fachadas del siglo XIX de piedra de Boñar debían mantenerse, se restauraron con caliza de la cantera leonesa original. La complejidad de que un edificio histórico no perdiera un ápice de su identidad y, a la vez, albergara en sus tripas una transformación tan profunda, era de tal magnitud que el equipo de arquitectos decidió no abordarlo como una única operación. Desarrolló distintas intervenciones —las galerías, la cubierta, el arco— bajo un mismo concepto arquitectónico, hasta conseguir a posteriori que todas funcionaran como conjunto. “No fue un ejercicio fácil. Tuvimos que trabajar y trabajar y trabajar... hasta que todo casó”, explica Azevedo.

El arco, uno de los elementos vehiculares de la rehabilitación, articula el edificio. Se trata de una estructura suspendida cuya construcción requirió una meticulosa labor de ensamblaje. Pero su valor va mucho más allá del ingenio técnico o lo estético. Para Azevedo, se trata de la materialización de la idea de conectar visual y espacialmente Faro con Santander: “Cuando estás ahí, de veras te hallas frente al mar, a la vez dentro y fuera”.

Uno de los elementos arquitectónicos más destacados de la rehabilitación es esta escalera helicoidal de hormigón pulido, que preside el vestíbulo, justo tras el arco central. Faro Santander

La sostenibilidad, en los cimientos de la rehabilitación

La sostenibilidad condicionó cada paso antes aún de que se trazase el primer boceto de un plano. “Poner el lazo cuando las cosas ya están hechas no funciona”, dice Sergio Arús, consultor de IDOM y asesor de la Fundación Santander y del equipo de arquitectura durante el proceso de acreditación BREEAM de Faro Santander. Cada avance de diseño se sometía al más estricto control de los criterios técnicos.

“La primera gran decisión, tomada tras mucha meditación, fue vaciar el interior del edificio, acometer la demolición y excavar”, cuenta Arús. Un proceso en el que se consiguieron hitos que van a suponer un ejemplo a imitar en cualquier obra: un 98% de los residuos que se generaron pudieron reutilizarse o reciclarse, solo un 2% de los cascotes y desechos acabaron en el vertedero.

“Se reaprovecharon, bien restaurados, suelos de madera o de piedra; incluso se fabricaron cajas de registro o mobiliario con madera procedente de los encofrados”, cuenta Arús, que explica cómo, por ejemplo, se desecaron in situ los lodos que generó la excavación, para que no contaminasen ni hubiera decenas de camiones incursionando hasta el centro de Santander para cargarlos y transportarlos, con la polución que eso hubiera ocasionado. Ningún detalle se dejó al azar. Y aquellos restos que no podían tener una nueva utilidad se clasificaron y enviaron a gestores autorizados, para su tratamiento y posterior reciclaje.

Una rehabilitación integral que no renuncia a su esencia Mantener las fachadas decimonónicas de la antigua sede central del Banco Santander, realizadas con piedra caliza de Boñar (León), supuso un gran reto técnico.



Foto: Juan Baraja Tras una deliberación minuciosa, se decidió vaciar el interior del edificio y levantar una nueva estructura.



Foto: Juan Baraja La complejidad de la rehabilitación era tal que diseñaron individualmente cada intervención y luego las armonizaron. Eso sí, teniendo en cuenta criterios de sostenibilidad en cada paso.



Plano: Estudio de arquitectura

de Chipperfield La excavación sirvió para instalar el innovador sistema de geotermia. Aunque se generaron lodos, se desecaron y reciclaron en la misma obra para evitar contaminación.



Foto: Juan Baraja Es la única rehabilitación de un museo que ha obtenido una calificación BREEAM de 92,96% en todo el mundo.



Foto: Juan Baraja Alzado del diseño de Faro Santander llevado a cabo por el estudio de arquitectura de David Chipperfield, galardonado en 2023 con el premio Pritzker

Pero si hay una innovación que permite comprender hasta qué punto Faro Santander es un edificio diferente hay que buscarla bajo los pies de los visitantes. Oculto en la propia estructura del edificio está uno de los ingenios para regular la temperatura de sus más de 10.000 metros cuadrados de salas de exposición y pasillos. Un sistema llamado TABS (Thermally Activated Building Structures) que, como explica Azevedo, “integra tuberías en los forjados de hormigón”. Por ellas circula agua, que aprovecha la inercia térmica de la propia estructura para calentar o enfriar los espacios. En invierno, basta que el agua alcance unos 23 grados para mantener un ambiente cálido; en verano, a unos 19 grados ya enfría. El hormigón funciona “como una gran batería térmica que mantiene las condiciones ambientales con oscilaciones mínimas”, describe Arús.

¿Y cómo se calienta o enfría el agua de esas tuberías? Gracias a la geotermia. “Es la primera vez que, en mi experiencia”, relata Azevedo, “conseguimos aunar ambas técnicas en un edificio”. Varias sondas geotérmicas enterradas en el subsuelo santanderino, que mantiene durante todo el año una temperatura suave y estable, se conectan a esas tuberías de los TABS conformando un circuito cerrado. El fluido procedente de las sondas del subsuelo, en invierno, llega a unas bombas que extraen el calor del terreno y lo elevan; en verano el ciclo se invierte, y las bombas lo que hacen es disipar el calor interno del edificio y derivarlo al subsuelo, que actúa “como una gran piscina”, dice Arús, que añade que “de esta manera se pueden alcanzar ahorros energéticos muy importantes frente a soluciones convencionales, y además se evita depender de los habituales equipos exteriores de climatización. Así fuimos capaces de liberar de buena parte de la maquinaria la cubierta”.

Además de una temperatura estable todo el año, se controlan las emisiones de dióxido de carbono y la humedad del ambiente, lo que garantiza una buena conservación para la pintura y el resto de obras de arte de la colección. Xoan Vázquez (Faro Santander)

La calidad del aire también está cuidadosamente controlada. El sistema de ventilación introduce aire exterior filtrado y recupera parte de la energía del aire extraído antes de expulsarlo. Así, en los días fríos, el aire que entra en las galerías puede llegar previamente atemperado. Con estas medidas más las que se encargan de la regulación de la humedad relativa y del CO₂ lo que se obtiene es un ambiente perfecto y salubre. “Es la manera idónea para preservar la gran colección de pintura y obras de arte de Faro Santander, ¡pero también de procurar un gran confort a los visitantes y trabajadores del museo!, aduce Arús.

La azotea y los jardines

La cubierta, con vistas espectaculares de la bahía, es un espacio amplio y perfectamente accesible. Una zona en la que apetece estar, con cafetería y jardines, y en la que se instalaron, como los denomina Arús, “hoteles de insectos”, que cumplen una misión: la de polinizar a todas las especies de plantas y árboles de esos jardines. “Las zonas verdes y la biodiversidad son también una prioridad en BREEAM”, explica Arús, que cuenta cómo se trasplantaron aquellos árboles que hubo que reubicar por las obras, y cómo luego se plantaron otros nuevos, aumentando netamente la masa forestal.

También destacan el arquitecto y el consultor otro aspecto: la gestión del agua. Un depósito recoge el agua de lluvia, que se reutiliza en el riego de las terrazas y en los inodoros. Grifos y duchas de vestuarios y baños son de bajo consumo, y los sistemas de riego son todos inteligentes.

Vistas desde la azotea de Faro Santander J.A.C.

La ubicación de Faro Santander, en el centro de la ciudad, favorece los desplazamientos a pie o el buen acceso en transporte público. Otro de los aspectos que mide BREEAM. Sin embargo, para ofrecer más alternativas, planearon y construyeron aparcamientos cerrados de bicicleta, pensados sobre todo para los trabajadores.

“Hemos demostrado que se puede construir pensando en la sostenibilidad y en las generaciones futuras sin hacer ningún sacrificio”, presume Azevedo. Una reflexión que se une a la metáfora de Arús, perfecto colofón de esa idea: “Si dentro de cien años el edificio deja de ser un museo, el hardware seguirá siendo valioso, y con una pequeña actualización de software podrá tener cualquier otro uso”.

World.title: Szczecin, un oasis urbano poco conocido entre Berlín y Varsovia
World.content:
Si bien su curioso topónimo parece un acertijo, y quien lo resuelva podrá presumir de saber pronunciar la singular lengua polaca, también es compleja la historia que encierra su consonántico nombre. Se podría decir que Szczecin responde a la trayectoria de Polonia, que pasó de ser un imperio, a desaparecer del mapa, y reunificarse con distintas fronteras.
