World.title: Vukovar Procession to Carry the Names of the Missing
World.content:
November the 18th, 2026 – The Vukovar procession will have thousands of people wearing the names of those still categorised as missing on their clothing.

Today marks the 35th anniversary of the fall of Vukovar, one of the defining moments of the Homeland War and the place of the type of massacre unseen since WWII. Index reports that in this year’s Column of Remembrance, thousands of young people will participate wearing T-shirts with the names of missing persons. This is part of the “Instead of Them” (Umjesto njih) initiative, organised for the third consecutive year by the Student Catholic Centre (SKAC) from Osijek. As part of the project, an application was also designed to permanently preserve the memories and personal stories of the people in whose name the youth will walk the streets of Vukovar.

a tribute to those still missing – all 1,725 of them

In this way, young people want to pay tribute to the 1,725 people who are still being searched for. Their message is that the memory of fallen, missing, and suffering Croatian defenders and civilians must be preserved. Many of the participants will set out on foot from Osijek toward Vukovar during the night.

“It’s a big responsibility and a very honourable role to be able to wear the name of someone who gave their life for the homeland,” said Ana Pešikan, a member of Osijek’s SKAC. Vlatka Ivančičević, head of the SKAC office, shared what motivated her to participate. “When I looked from the side and saw the faces of people searching for the name of one of their own on a T-shirt, in that moment it became very real to me,” she said.

passing on the truth about the war

Although many of those planning to march wearing the names of Vukovar’s missing were not even born during the Homeland War, today they want to pass on the truth about the events of that time. “This year on our T-shirts we’re wearing the names of missing defenders, and by wearing white T-shirts with a universal message we will pay tribute to all civilians from the Homeland War,” explained Domagoj Galić, coordinator of the “Instead of Them” initiative.

So that participants can learn more about the people whose names they wear, the organizers are recording their life stories in a special web application. “We’re aware of how grateful we should be to those people who made it possible for us to live today in a free Croatia and enjoy freedom. This is the least we can do to show them respect and gratitude,” said Ivan Galić from the organising team.

World.title: Egypt expresses interest in Iraq’s Development Road project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Egyptian officials have renewed their push for national firms to participate in Iraq’s Development Road project and broader infrastructure initiatives.

Egyptian Minister of Transport Kamel el-Wazir said that Egyptian companies are ready to join the Development Road and railway projects with competitive pricing, quality standards, and fast delivery.

El-Wazir’s remarks took place during his meeting with the Iraqi Ambassador to Egypt, Qahtan Taha Khalaf, in Cairo, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Egypt’s Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs, Hussein Issa, also met with Khalaf to discuss expanding trade, investment, and Egyptian company involvement in Iraqi development and reconstruction projects.

During a regional transport summit held two weeks ago in Alexandria, Egypt, Iraqi Transport Minister Wahab al-Hassani said that Iraq is moving toward the early implementation of land transport agreements with Jordan and Egypt to boost regional trade and cross-border movement.

Al-Hassani confirmed that Baghdad has finalized several land transport agreements with Amman and Cairo that are expected to enter into force soon.

The deals build upon a previously signed memorandum of understanding between the Iraqi and Egyptian transport ministries covering the overland movement of both passengers and goods.

Alongside the deals with Jordan and Egypt, al-Hassani highlighted Iraq’s broader push to establish itself as a regional transit hub through the country’s strategic project of the Development Road.

The strategic corridor spans 1,200 kilometers from the al-Faw Grand Port in the southern province of Basra to the Turkish border, combining new highway and railway networks.

World.title: Baghdad replaces forces holding Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered on Wednesday the replacement of the forces holding Jurf Al-Sakher, following an investigation into alleged oil smuggling.

The move seeks to end the 12-year control of the strategic Babil province area by the Iran-backed armed faction Kataib Hezbollah.

Iraq’s Supreme Committee for Security Sector Reform, chaired by Al-Zaidi in his capacity as Commander-in-Chief, ordered the replacement of the current force stationed in Jurf al-Sakhar with joint units from the Iraqi army, federal police, and other Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) brigades.

The Energy Police, an Interior Ministry force, was officially assigned to secure the three branches of the strategic Basra-Haditha oil pipeline running through the area.

Findings from a government investigative committee alleging oil theft and pipeline tampering were referred to the judiciary for legal action.

Before Wednesday’s deployment order, al-Zaidi dismissed nine senior security, intelligence, and oil ministry officials—including the director of the Oil Pipelines Company—in connection with the smuggling investigation.

The orders follow escalating tensions between Baghdad and Kataib Hezbollah, which has controlled the area south of Baghdad since recapturing it from ISIS in 2014.

The armed faction rejected the smuggling allegations, claiming the sites inspected by investigators were abandoned facilities or fuel tanks for military vehicles.

World.title: Najaf refinery expansion to raise Iraq’s refining capacity by 70,000 bpd
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s oil refining capacity is set to increase further as the expansion project at the Najaf refinery progresses.

The project aims to add 70,000 barrels per day to the country’s refining output, aligning with Baghdad’s broader plans to boost the production of petroleum products and reduce reliance on imports.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi visited the refinery expansion site on Tuesday to evaluate the progress made and to assess the technical and logistical challenges encountered during the project’s implementation.

The project is being carried out amid Iraqi efforts to improve the efficiency of its refining sector and increase its capacity to meet the domestic market’s fuel needs.

The expansion of the Najaf refinery will increase fuel production to meet the requirements of surrounding industrial projects, create new job opportunities, and boost economic activity within the province.

The Najaf refinery expansion project includes the construction of a new refining unit with a capacity of 70,000 barrels per day. This development encompasses the completion of essential facilities and services needed to support its operation.

The project includes the development of energy infrastructure, an industrial water treatment unit, oil storage tanks, and other facilities associated with the refining unit.

The refinery’s current processing capacity stands at 30,000 barrels per day. With the addition of 70,000 barrels per day from the new unit, the expansion plans aim to increase the total capacity to 100,000 barrels per day.

World.title: Iraq aims to raise non-oil revenues to 19% in 2027 budget
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s draft 2027 federal budget aims to raise non-oil revenues to at least 19 percent of total government revenues, marking the highest proportion in the country’s history.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi government, Haider al-Aboudi, announced the target on Tuesday, noting that non-oil income had never exceeded 11 percent before 2026.

According to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), the government plans to achieve this increase and insulate the economy from oil shocks through several structural changes.

Authorities are automating customs procedures at border crossings, digitizing government operations, and strengthening tax collection.

The plan relies on tightening financial oversight to cut off sources of corruption and revenue leakage.

The bill introduces elements of program and performance-based budgeting, tying public spending to measurable goals rather than strictly to payroll and operational categories.

While the ministries of finance and planning have completed the draft, the bill has not yet been formally published or approved by the Iraqi cabinet.

The Iraqi government aims to spend 217 trillion Iraqi dinars (around $166 billion) in 2027, assuming an oil price of $58 per barrel, according to parliamentarians familiar with the draft budget.

The measures would result in a fiscal deficit of around 40 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $30.6 billion).

Members of the parliamentary finance committee told Reuters that the draft budget anticipates crude oil exports of around four million barrels per day, including shipments from Iraqi Kurdistan.

Oil exports generate the majority of the Iraqi government’s revenue, accounting for roughly 80 percent of the general budget’s resources.

The 2027 budget represents a structural transformation by allocating 150 trillion ($114.5 billion) for traditional line items and 50 trillion Iraqi dinar ($38.2 billion) for a new World Bank-coordinated program-and-performance model to measure expenditure efficiency.

World.title: Baghdad Court sentences six more French ISIS members to life in prison
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Al-Karkh Criminal Court in Baghdad sentenced six French nationals to life imprisonment on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, for membership in the Islamic State (ISIS) terrorist organization, raising the total number of French citizens convicted in the ongoing mass transfer case to 16.

According to a statement from the Supreme Judicial Council’s Media Center, the verdicts were pronounced in the presence of the defendants’ legal counsel and diplomatic representatives from the French Embassy in Baghdad.

The court issued the rulings under Article 4 (Paragraph 1)—read in conjunction with Article 2 (Paragraphs 1 and 3)—of Iraq’s Anti-Terrorism Law No.13 of 2005, applying discretionary sentence mitigation pursuant to Article 132 (Paragraph 1) of the Iraqi Penal Code to commute potential capital punishments to life sentences (equivalent to 20 years under Iraqi statutory law, subject to automatic Court of Cassation review).

The six convicts belong to a group of 47 French detainees transferred into Iraqi custody from detention facilities in northeastern Syria.

Initial inquiries were conducted by the First Al-Karkh Investigation Court with evidentiary and archival verification provided by the National Center for International Judicial Cooperation, before referring the suspects for trial.

Judicial proceedings for the group began on September 20, 2026, under tight security and without media access.

Today’s rulings mark the third wave of convictions handed down by the Al-Karkh Criminal Court in this case: on October 27, 2026, the court sentenced six French nationals to life imprisonment and a seventh defendant to 15 years in prison;two days later, on October 29, it issued life sentences to three additional French suspects, bringing the cumulative tally to 16 convicted individuals following Wednesday’s verdicts.

World.title: Fourth Arab SME Summit opens in Baghdad as CBI reveals 16.3 trillion dinar financing milestone
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) The fourth edition of the Arab Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) Summit kicked off at the Baghdad International Fairground on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, running through November 20 under the patronage of Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi and co-organized by Iraq’s Ministry of Planning and the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia (ESCWA).

Participating as a strategic partner and sponsor, the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) established a dedicated pavilion within the summit’s accompanying exhibition alongside commercial banks, corporations, and economic institutions.

Through informational publications and technical briefings, the CBI pavilion highlighted the banking sector’s role in executing national development financing initiatives and walked attendees through the application procedures for accessing SME loans—which carry a financing ceiling of 20 million Iraqi dinars per project through participating banks.

During the exhibition, the Central Bank unveiled updated cumulative figures detailing the scope of its developmental lending programs since their inception in 2015 through the end of October 2026.

Over that 11-year span, total CBI-backed financing reached 16.3 trillion Iraqi dinars, supporting the launch and expansion of more than 10,000 projects across Iraq’s private sector.

World.title: Iran-backed militia torture Iraqi environmentalist who refuses to abandon marshes
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Jassim al-Asadi, an Iraqi environmentalist, has returned to safeguarding the country’s southern marshlands after being kidnaped and tortured by an Iran-backed militia in 2023, according to a November 18 article by NPR correspondent Jane Arraf.

Al-Asadi, 69, co-founded the environmental organization Nature Iraq in 2004 and has spent decades fighting to restore the marshes, which were mainly drained under Saddam Hussein and were designated a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2016.

Nature Iraq is an Iraqi-registered non-governmental organization accredited to the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and also Iraq’s first and only affiliate of BirdLife International, an international conservation partnership.

Speaking with NPR, al-Asadi reported that armed men kidnapped him while he was traveling from Baghdad to his village of Chibayish in February 2023.

His captors accused him of spying for Israel and using his environmental expertise to aid foreign intelligence activities.

He said he was kept for two weeks, assaulted, shocked, and brutally suffocated during questioning.

When he was asked to confess or face death, he refused and instead composed a goodbye letter to his family.

According to NPR, al-Asadi was finally released due to pressure from his Bani Asad tribe, who mobilized hundreds of armed tribesmen to demand his liberation.

He denied an offer of refuge in Europe, preferring to stay in Iraq and continue his environmental efforts.

His homecoming comes as Iraq’s marshlands begin to recover after five years of severe drought.

Recent rains have boosted water levels, enabling some displaced buffalo herders to return, but pollution, water scarcity, and diminishing fish populations remain major concerns.

Despite threats against him, Al-Asadi continues to monitor water levels, help local people, and lobby for improved environmental protection.

The NPR investigation also highlighted the dangers confronting Iraqi environmental activists, especially those working with foreign organizations in regions where Iran-backed armed groups hold significant power.

Despite his suffering, al-Asadi remains determined to preserve the marshlands and its centuries-old way of life.

Nature Iraq organization focuses on conserving and rehabilitating Iraq’s ecosystems while safeguarding the cultural traditions and heritage connected to them.

World.title: CBI rules out dropping zeros from Iraqi dinar and favors banknote redesign
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) Spokesperson Mahmoud Dagher announced on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, that dropping zeros from the Iraqi dinar requires formal parliamentary legislation to overhaul financial transactions alongside large-scale currency printing, stating that under current economic conditions, the central bank views redesigning the physical appearance of banknotes as the most practical option.

Speaking during a televised interview with journalist Lana Al-Zahawi on Al-Nahrain TV, Dagher explained that redenominating the currency goes far beyond issuing replacement banknotes.

While passing enabling legislation through the Council of Representatives is legally feasible, he emphasized that re-indexing financial obligations, corporate shares, and market valuations introduces complex structural adjustments.

Citing the Iraq Stock Exchange as a practical example, Dagher questioned how shares currently priced at a nominal value of 1 dinar would be recalibrated without a comprehensive legal and accounting framework governing equity stakes and financial contracts.

Highlighting the industrial scale required for any currency overhaul, Dagher noted that replacing 10 million circulating banknotes requires printing an equal volume of new notes—a process contracted to premier international security printers such as “Theron,” which he ranked among the top four currency printing houses globally.

He underscored that banknote production is a specialized technical operation rather than a routine commodity order.

Instead of pursuing currency redenomination at this stage, the CBI favors updating the physical design and security features of existing denominations without altering their nominal face value or purchasing power.

According to Dagher, refreshing the banknote series delivers immediate economic and security advantages: it strengthens anti-counterfeiting protections, extends the physical lifespan of circulating notes, and incentivizes the return of hoarded cash back into the formal banking system.

World.title: 'Defence, security ties key': Jaishankar ahead of India-Japan 2+2 dialogue
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Ahead of India-Japan 2+2 dialogue, external affairs minister

has underlined the significance of defence and security cooperation between the two countries as well as greater scope for collaboration in areas like advanced manufacturing, critical minerals and semiconductors.

Jaishankar and defence minister

are in Japan for the 4th 2+2 dialogue. The ministers will also hold the Defence Ministerial Meeting and the India-Japan Foreign Ministers' Strategic Dialogue with their counterparts from Japan, defence minister Shinjiro Koizumi and foreign minister Toshimitsu Motegi, respectively.

"India-Japan Special Strategic and Global Partnership is anchored in shared values of democracy, freedom and respect for rule of law, and committed to a free and open Indo-Pacific that is peaceful, prosperous and resilient," said the ministry of external affairs.



Speaking at an event in Tokyo, Jaishankar urged Japan to develop policies and frameworks to work together in the fields of security and defence. He also called for deeper cooperation in clean energy and pharmaceuticals.

He listed shocks to the international system, weaponisation and chokepoints, extreme competition and greater risk-taking, de-risking and diversification, and trusted partnerships as five defining features of the current state of the world.

World.title: CJI averts 'potential religious row', pulls cases from SC judge
World.content:
New Delhi: CJI Surya Kant's decision to withdraw two cases from the bench headed by Justice Ahsanuddin Amanullah, which had expanded individual incidents of lapses on the part of authorities into pan-India judicial drives against similar illegalities, averted a potential religious controversy.

The bench's Aug 4 order directing all states and UTs to remove stray animals from public places created a controversy as it is known that the majority of strays comprise cows and calves. A UP resident filed an application before the bench apprehending that the order was "capable of being implemented in a manner that may result in cows and their progeny being rounded up, transported or disposed of without regard to the special constitutional protection they are entitled to".



'Wasn't permissible for that particular bench to create PIL jurisdiction'

The applicant said, "Cows have been worshipped and revered in Indian society since ancient times as 'gaumata', and religious sentiments of the public..., particularly the Hindu community, are gravely hurt whenever cows are slaughtered or otherwise ill-treated."

He said a blanket order for the removal of strays by SC ran "the real risk of stray cattle being pushed across state borders, herded into inadequ-ate holding pounds, or otherwise subjected to conditions violative of Prevention of Cr-uelty to Animals Act, 1960...





instead of being rehabilitated through properly funded and regulated gaushalas".

The CJI's decision to withdraw the cases, backed by the four most senior SC judges, was taken after they felt it was impermissible for a bench, not assigned the PIL roster, to create PIL jurisdiction for itself by expanding individual cases into pan-India exercises in violation of case-distribution discipline, which falls in the CJI's domain.

A decision on allocation to appropriate benches would be taken after that, they said.

One such case - Loganathan vs State of Tamil Nadu - started from the illegal construction of a ground plus one floor without a sanction plan and the failure of authorities to even notice it. The bench led by Justice Amanullah on March 25 said, "It is evident there are apparent widespread and blatant violations of building bylaws and land-use regulations. In view of the above, we deem it appropriate to examine the issue on a pan-India basis.

" It impleaded municipal corporations and municipalities of capital cities of all states and UTs.

World.title: Can an Italian raise slogans against govt while in India on visa? SC to hear PIL
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Monday agreed to hear a PIL asking whether it was legally permissible for an Italian visiting India on a conference visa, to raise the political slogan "vote chor, gaddi chhod" in support of opposition's campaign against

and Modi govt at the Bharat Summit organised by Telangana Congress govt in Hyderabad.

The plea alleges Giacomo Filibeck, the secretary-general of the Party of European Socialists, raised the "vulgar, derogatory and demeaning political slogan" and translated it for other foreign delegates as "vote thief, leave from seat."

Senior advocate Rizwan Ahmad sought an urgent hearing on the petition filed by Zahid Ali.

Telangana govt organised meet, examine its role: Petitioner

A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana agreed to list the petition before a bench Friday.



Ahmad informed the court that Filibeck, endorsing the leader of the oppositionâs campaign, told the audience that the largest democracy in India had become corrupted and declared that âwe stand by Rahul Gandhi, the Indian Congress party in defending the democracy in Indiaâ.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Ahmad said the petitioner did not question Indian politicians criticising govt but âthe endorsement and amplification of such domestic political positions by foreign political representatives, who are themselves associated with political organisations in other countries, raises a distinct concern regarding foreign participation in Indiaâs internal political discourse, particularly when such participation extends to the endorsement of controversial domestic political positions.





..â

The petitioner said when home ministry rules prohibited foreign delegates from taking part in any activity beyond the purpose of their visit to India, it was necessary for the court to examine whether Filibeck conformed to the visa conditions by getting involved in the political activities espoused by the opposition.

He sought judicial scrutiny of Filibeckâs conduct and requested the court to direct Union govt to take action. âThe role of Telangana govt also warrants consideration, particularly as the conference was organised by the state govt and provided a platform for the aforesaid political discourse involving foreigners,â he said.

The petitioner also requested SC to direct social media platforms to take down videos of the conference relating to the Italianâs remarks.

World.title: 35 yrs on, a landmark moment: Forces kill Kashmir's last active local terrorist
World.content:
SRINAGAR/NEW DELHI: Security forces killed 22-year-old

terrorist Mohammad Lateef Bhat in a shootout outside a mosque in Kulgam district early Wednesday, ending a weeklong hunt and eliminating Kashmir's last known active local terrorist, according to J&K police.

The killing marked what police described as a watershed moment in Kashmir's 35-year fight against terrorism, dealing a blow to Pakistan's efforts to project terrorist violence in the Valley as a home-grown movement. It also marked a turning point in Kashmir's counterterror campaign, with police saying local recruitment into terrorist ranks had fallen to almost zero. Home minister Amit Shah hailed the operation as a coordinated success of J&K police, Army, CRPF and intelligence agencies, saying Bhat was Lashkar's last known active local terrorist in the valley.



Bhat refused to surrender, was killed trying to escape

Lateef Bhat, who carried a Rs 15 lakh bounty, was killed outside a mosque in Zangalpora village after a week-long chase across south Kashmir. His associate, Nisar, a new recruit, was killed near Larnoo bypass on Nov 16.

J&K Police DG Nalin Prabhat called it a milestone in the fight against three decades of terrorism, saying local recruitment had fallen to almost zero. Only two Kashmiri youths joined LeT in the past two years, he said, adding that the force was working to dismantle the terrorist ecosystem.





âWe have been fighting Pakistan-sponsored terrorism for the past 35 years,â Prabhat said.

Lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha said only a handful of foreign terrorists remained and J&K would soon be terrorism-free.

Home minister Amit Shah posted on X, âLateef Bhat was neutralised in an operation in Kulgam in the early morning hours. One of his terrorist associates, Umar Nisar, was also neutralised in Kulgam, the day before.

The entire operation was marked by a very high level of synergy. The nation salutes the brave Jawans.â

Local recruitment has fluctuated sharply over the years. The number fell from 54 in 2010 to 16 in 2013 before climbing to 53 in 2014, 66 in 2015, 88 in 2016 and 126 in 2017, according to security agencies. It peaked at 196 in 2018, declined to 143 in 2019 and rose again to 174 in 2020. Of those recruited in 2020, 76 were killed and 46 arrested.

In 2021, 128 local youths joined terrorist groups â 73 were killed and 16 arrested.

Bhatâs killing followed a cat-and-mouse chase that began after the Nov 11 attack on a CRPF picket in Kulgam, in which three personnel were wounded. Human intelligence, CCTV footage, cyber surveillance and details from a phone Bhat had dropped while fleeing helped security forces trace him.

Bhat, a resident of Khrewan Chader village in Kulgam, had been wanted for the killing of a J&K police head constable in Anantnag and two migrant workers in Kulgam in July.

He had escaped a shootout in Shopian in July, when his LeT associate, Zakir Ganie, was killed.

Security forces cornered the duo in Kulgam on Nov 16. Nisar was killed near Larnoo bypass, but Bhat escaped, discarding his clothes to evade the cordon. He was traced to Jamia Mosque in Zangalpora Tuesday. Police cordoned off the area around 11pm.

Kulgam SSP Anayat Ali Choudhary said security forces made repeated attempts to persuade Bhat to surrender, including a video call.

Mosque committee members were also sent inside to convince him to lay down his arms. âWe told him that he was still young and should surrender but he refused,â Choudhary said.

Bhat opened fire around 3.45am Wednesday. Choudhary said forces exercised maximum restraint because Bhat was inside a mosque in the cordoned-off area. Bhat was killed outside the religious structure while attempting to escape. Unlike earlier operations, there was little local support for him.

World.title: Keralam ministers question CM's key calls at cabinet meet
World.content:
Thiruvananthapuram/New Delhi: Keralam CM V D Satheesan faced questions from ministers over key decisions at the cabinet meeting Wednesday, marking six months of UDF govt in office.

Later in the day, Satheesan, who flew to Delhi, acknowledged there had been differences but said they had been resolved through discussions.

"There were differences of opinion in the cabinet. This is democracy, not Pinarayi Vijayan's cabinet," the CM said.

The dissent centred on appointments to the Public Service Commission and Guruvayur Devaswom Board, and allocation of positions in boards and corporations.



Revenue minister A P Anilkumar objected to PSC nominees, questioning the lack of consultation. Satheesan said the appointments were urgent.

Power minister Sunny Joseph and others alleged the CM was taking unilateral decisions. RSP minister Shibu Baby John sought adequate representation for his party. Only health minister K Muraleedharan reportedly defended Satheesan. The discussion lasted nearly two-and-a-half hours before the differences were resolved.

In New Delhi, Satheesan said the UDF was not a group of sycophants and ministers were free to disagree. Even the youngest minister, O J Janeesh, could look him in the eye and express a contrary opinion, he said. "Team UDF remains Team UDF. All decisions taken by the UDF cabinet are collective decisions. If we cannot reach a consensus on an issue, we will defer it," he said.

NEW DELHI: Patients covered under Ayushman Bharat may soon get access to a wider range of routine medical treatments and surgical procedures, with govt proposing to expand packages reserved for public health facilities under the scheme from 23 to 112.The 89 additional packages cover conditions such as anaemia, hypertension, bronchitis, diarrhoea, urinary tract infections and diabetes-related complications. NEW DELHI: SC Wednesday initiated contempt proceedings against advocate Pravin Singhal for making derogatory remarks against CJI Surya Kant while appearing before his bench on Nov 16.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta, Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed the erring lawyer to file his response by Jan 8 and also ordered him to appear personally before it on the next date of hearing on Jan 20."Having perused the papers placed before us, which includes the requisite consent of the learned Attorney General for India under Section 15(1)(b) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, we are prima facie satisfied that the motion made by the petitioner - Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) - for initiation of proceedings against the sole respondent / alleged contemnor for the alleged derogatory remarks referred to in the petition together with the attempt to scandalise the authority of the Court deserves to be taken forward," the bench said in its order.The controversy arose after the lawyer, aggrieved by an alleged procedural lapse in non-listing of a petition, questioned the integrity of the CJI in open court proceedings and went to extent of telling him "You cannot sit in that chair. World.title: BJP turns to Mathura temple issue amid cadre unease, allies’ pressure
World.content:
Days after Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav made his ‘Dumdar Dalit’ outreach in Agra, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) responded on November 16 with ‘Radhe Radhe, Kamal Khila De’ and ‘Abki Baari Baanke Bihari’.

It was senior BJP leader and Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya who spelt out to reporters, during the party’s two-day conclave in Mathura earlier this week, that constructing a grand temple at the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi in Mathura would be at the centre of their campaign for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly election. The ruling party signalled that it would counter the SP’s ‘PDA’ [‘Pichhde’ (backward classes), Dalits and ‘Alpsankhyak’ (minorities)] card with the mantra of cultural nationalism, supplementing it with the ‘double-engine’ government’s “success stories” on the development and law and order fronts.

World.title: Cyclone 'Akvan' updates: Akvan likely to cross between Machilipatnam and Puri, says APSDMA
World.content:
Cyclone Akvan is now likely to cross the coast between Machilipatnam and Puri, along the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts, around noon on Friday (November 20) as a severe cyclonic storm, the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) said in an update at 12.10 p.m. on Wednesday (November 18, 2026).

The storm picked up speed to 7 kmph over the past six hours. It was about 580 km from Visakhapatnam, 590 km from Machilipatnam and 710 km from Gopalpur in Odisha, APSDMA said.

Also read | All you need to know about cyclone Akvan

Initially, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast that the weather system would strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday evening (November 17, 2026), but the system had either remained stationary or moved slowly. The Cyclonic Storm “Akvan” over central parts of South and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal moved slowly northwards with the speed of 03 kmph during past 06 hours and lay centered at 2330 hours IST of yesterday, the 17th November, 2026 over the same region, the IMD said in an update early Wednesday.

Also read | Andhra Pradesh experiencing a ‘rare event’

The system has changed its track slightly, and the probable landfall points may remain between Visakhapatnam and Nellore. Isolated heavy rainfall is likely in the northern districts of Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Parvathipuram Manyam, Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, and strong winds with speeds of 100 kmph to 110 kmph are likely along the coastal belt from Wednesday evening (November 18, 2026). Andhra Pradesh is experiencing a very rare event, since it is not often that a State sees three tropical cyclones crossing its coast within a month, said IMD Director General of Meteorology.

World.title: India’s CSR spending leaves gaps in health, water security, innovation: Report
World.content:
A significant share of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funding in India continues to flow towards established sectors, while several pressing development challenges receive comparatively limited attention, according to a report by Sattva Consulting and India Data Insights.

The analysis of CSR projects between FY23 and FY25 points to funding gaps in non-communicable diseases, women’s economic agency, school-to-work transition, groundwater resilience and innovation.

Nearly 80% of CSR funding is concentrated in five sectors, with education accounting for 35% and healthcare for 21%. However, the report finds gaps even within these established areas. Non-communicable diseases (NCDs), for instance, account for 60% of deaths in India, up from 45% in 2004-06. Yet, nearly 62% of identifiable NCD funding goes towards cancer, while cardiovascular diseases receive around 12%, despite accounting for over half of the NCD deaths.

The report also points to a gap between education and employment outcomes. Youth unemployment stands at 9.9% rising to 25.9% among graduates. Of the CSR funding for the school-to-work transition, 42% goes towards academic and skilling support. For every rupee allocated to these areas, only 24 paise goes towards giving young people exposure to the world of work.

A similar concentration is visible in funding for women’s economic agency. The area receives ₹1,122.8 crore or 29% of identifiable women-focused CSR funding, with nearly 77% directed towards skilling and livelihoods. The report also highlights barriers such as inadequate care infrastructure, unsafe mobility and limited market access.

In groundwater resilience, Punjab, Rajasthan and Haryana account for nearly 49% of India’s critical and over-exploited groundwater units, but receive only around 7% of identifiable CSR funding for the area.

Innovation and research also receive limited attention, with approximately ₹298 crore in CSR funding between FY23 and FY25. No industry directs more than 1.2% of its total CSR spending to this area.

“CSR has brought size and predictability to funding. It now needs agility. CSR cannot replace the government, but it can be patient and risk-tolerant in ways other capital often cannot. That allows it to test unproven models, build evidence on what works and help scale its adoption,” said Srikrishna Sridhar Murthy, co-founder and CEO of Sattva Consulting, a global impact consulting firm headquartered in Bengaluru.

“The question for corporates is no longer only how much they spend, but whether that spend is reaching the problems where it can make a difference,” Srikrishna added.

India’s annual CSR spending reached ₹40,794 crore in FY25, growing at 15% annually over the past decade.

World.title: Jwala Nagar building collapse: Co-owner arrested while trying to flee; police probe conflicting claims over tenant’s 40-year stay
World.content:
A day after a building collapse in east Delhi’s Jwala Nagar claimed two lives, including that of a three-year-old boy, the Delhi Police on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) arrested one of the two co-owners of the property while he was allegedly attempting to flee.

The accused, identified as Veer Singh, was arrested in Shahdara, Deputy Commissioner of Police (Shahdara) R.P. Meena said. He is the brother of Surendar Singh, the other joint owner of the property, who was arrested on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), following the collapse, the officer said.

According to the police, the property was originally registered in their mother’s name and was inherited by the two brothers after her death.

Meanwhile, preliminary interrogation has yielded conflicting statements about how long the family of the three-year-old victim, Devansh, had been living in the building. The police said Surendar Singh allegedly told investigators that the family had been occupying the room for the past three years. However, the family maintains that they had been living in the same rented room for nearly four decades.

The police said they were investigating the claims and verifying the ownership and tenancy details.

The bodies of the two deceased, identified as Devansh alias Laddu (3) and Pintu (32), were handed over to their families for final rites after postmortem examinations. The five injured persons continue to receive treatment.

The collapse occurred at around 10:09 a.m. on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), in Gali No. 6, near Peer Baba Mazar in the Sabji Mandi area of Jwala Nagar. The nearly 50-year-old building, which housed a gajak factory on the ground floor with residential rooms above it, gave way, trapping people under the debris.

The injured were identified as Devansh’s mother, Khushbu (30); Vikesh (30); Akash (27); Dalip (26); and Aman (32). All seven victims were taken to Dr. Hedgewar Hospital, where Devansh and Pintu were declared dead.

An FIR was registered under Sections 106(1) (causing death by negligence), 125(A) (causing hurt by a rash or negligent act endangering life or personal safety) and 223 (disobedience to an order duly promulgated by a public servant) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Mr Meena had said Section 223 was added as the owner had allegedly failed to verify the tenants living in the property.

The incident was the third building collapse in Delhi in November, following the collapse of an under-construction hotel in Paharganj, which injured eight workers, and a building collapse in Chawri Bazar on November 5, which claimed seven lives.

Residents had alleged that they had repeatedly raised concerns about the deteriorating condition of the building, including a leaking roof, cracks in the walls and exposed metal girders, but the owner had failed to undertake necessary repairs.

The MCD flagged the building’s proximity to the railway track (it stood approximately 24 metres away), and the vibrations caused by passing trains could have contributed to the collapse.

Investigation into the case is underway.

World.title: Delhi High Court asks Centre to look into objectionable content posted by police officials against lawyers
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) asked the Centre to look into the alleged objectionable content posted about lawyers on social media from the accounts of suspended Delhi Police ACP Manasvi Vashishta and another official, and to take appropriate action.

The High Court was hearing a plea by lawyers seeking action against Mr. Vashishta and other officials for allegedly threatening advocates, intimidating them, and passing derogatory remarks about them.

A Bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma was informed by the counsel for the Central Government that disciplinary action had already been taken against Mr. Vashishta and a chargesheet had been submitted to the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) for approval.

The Centre’s counsel said that the Ministry is expected to consider and approve the chargesheet within a reasonable time and added that a status report will be filed within four weeks in the matter.

On the issue of accounts maintained on social media by Vashishta and Sub-Inspector Vishal Yadav, the government counsel said if the material is supplied by the petitioner, the authorities will immediately look into it and take appropriate measures for the removal of objectionable articles in accordance with law.

“We permit the petitioner to provide the material, if any, in addition to the one given in the petition to the counsel for respondent 1 (MHA) within 48 hours to enable the respondent to look into the same and, if required, take appropriate action in the matter,” the court said.

The controversy stems from an October 23 incident at Shahdara police station, where advocate Lalit Bansal allegedly sustained a serious head injury during a scuffle.

The court was hearing a petition filed by advocate Karan Bir Singh alleging that videos circulating on social media depicted Mr. Vashishta making threatening and derogatory statements against lawyers, including remarks suggesting that advocates visiting police stations in groups could face detention and criminal proceedings.

On October 28, the Delhi Police transferred Mr. Vashishta, who was then posted as the Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) in Gandhi Nagar, to the Special Police Unit for Women and Children (SPUWAC). Inspector Arun Kumar, who was the Station House Officer (SHO) of Shahdara Police Station at the time, was transferred to the Security Unit.

World.title: Man arrested for desecrating Guru Granth Sahib at gurdwara in Delhi’s Tilak Nagar
World.content:
The Delhi police on Wednesday arrested a 40-year-old man for allegedly desecrating the Guru Granth Sahib at a gurdwara in west Delhi’s Tilak Nagar on Sunday. The police are also investigating allegations that members of the gurdwara management committee attempted to conceal the incident for two days, a police officer said.

The arrest came a day after tension gripped the area, with members of the Sikh community protesting outside the Tilak Nagar police station and demanding that the accused be handed over to them.

“The incident took place at Shahpura Gurdwara, also referred to as Gurdwara Sahibpura. The matter came to light only two days later when members of the gurdwara committee recognised the accused when he returned and alerted the police,” Deputy Commissioner of Police (West) Hareshwar V. Swami said.

Following a complaint by the gurdwara management on Tuesday, an FIR was subsequently registered at the Tilak Nagar police station under Sections 192 (wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause a riot), 298 (injuring or defiling a place of worship with intent to insult the religion of any class) and 299 (deliberate and malicious acts intended to outrage religious feelings by insulting a religion or religious beliefs) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

A separate complaint was also filed on Wednesday by a group of Sikh community members against five members of the gurdwara committee, accusing them of concealing the incident for two days. A police source said an FIR had not yet been registered in the matter and that the allegations were being investigated.

Strict action sought

The incident triggered outrage among members of the Sikh community.

Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee (DSGMC) president Harmeet Singh Kalka said the incident was “deeply distressing” and called for a thorough investigation into the motive behind it.

“We have asked the police to take strict action against the accused so that no one dares to do this again. Action should also be taken against the members of the management who tried to conceal the incident and did not inform the congregation, showing negligence in the matter,” the DSGMC president said.

Mr. Kalka appealed to Delhi Lieutenant-Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu to take cognisance of the incident and ensure a thorough investigation.

He also urged gurdwara management committees across Delhi to instal CCTV cameras, strengthen security arrangements and frame policies to deal with such incidents, while maintaining unity against acts of sacrilege.

Aam Aadmi Party MLA from Tilak Nagar Jarnail Singh also condemned the incident and questioned the gurdwara committee’s alleged silence for two days.

In a video statement on X, Mr. Singh said the committee should explain to the Sikh community why it had not informed its members about the incident, which allegedly took place two days earlier. He said the community had every right to know the truth and called for an impartial investigation and strict legal action against those responsible.

Mr. Singh also said he would raise the demand for legislation to prevent sacrilege in the Delhi Assembly, drawing inspiration from the Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Bill, 2026, passed in Punjab on April 13. The legislation amended the 2008 Act to strengthen safeguards against sacrilege and regulate the printing, publication, storage and distribution of copies of the holy scripture.

(With inputs from PTI)

World.title: UEF, IIT-M join hands for Tamil Nadu Growth Conclave 2026; focus on 10 key sectors
World.content:
The United Economic Forum (UEF) Chamber of Commerce has signed an MoU with the Indian Institute of Technology - Madras (IIT-M) to collaborate for the Tamil Nadu Growth Conclave 2026 scheduled to be held on December 8, 2026. The objective of this MoU is to facilitate knowledge sharing, industry academia collaboration, innovation, investment and stakeholder engagement towards Tamil Nadu’s economic growth.

The event will focus on 10 sectors, including Automotive & EV; Electronics & Semiconductors; IT, AI and Digital; Advanced Engineering & Capital Goods; Textiles & Technical Textiles; Pharma, Biotech & MedTech; Agri & Food Processing; Renewable & Green Energy; Logistics, Ports & Global Trade and Aerospace & Defence. Professors from the IIT-M ecosystem will lead each of these sectors.

V.Kamakoti, IIT-Madras Director through a video message said: “IIT Madras, and IIT Madras Research Park, and all our ecosystem are very happy to be associated with UEF to launch this Tamil Nadu Conclave 2026 as we march towards a multi-trillion economy.”

Mr. Kamakoti further said: “There are 10 highly emerging and extremely important from a societal angle verticals that have been identified, all the way from automotive, EV, electronics, semiconductor, IT, AI, technical, textiles, pharma, agri, renewable, green energy, aerospace, defense, logistics, and advanced engineering and capital goods.” He added, “And in each of these verticals, we are going to talk not just about the products, but also the supply chain, the logistics that is involved, the raw materials that are involved to make these, because many of them are deep tech technologies.”

Jinnah Rafiq Ahmed, Chairman, UEF – Tamil Nadu Growth Conclave 2026 and Executive Chairman and Managing Director, Kothari Industrial Corporation Limited (KICL), said that a few MoUs would be inked at the conclave. To a query on whether investments are moving out of Tamil Nadu, he said that a lot of companies want to come to Tamil Nadu.

“Tamil Nadu’s industrial growth will be there, will continue and it will be unimaginable. Definitely, Tamil Nadu’s industrial growth will be very aggressive in the coming years. An industry from Tamil Nadu going out of State will not happen. And if it is, it might be an additional project in other States,” he said.

Ahmed A. R. Buhari, President — United Economic Forum (UEF) said, “Tamil Nadu has set an ambitious target of becoming a $1.5 trillion economy by 2036. UEF’s Unnatha Tamizhagam vision aspires to contribute towards Tamil Nadu becoming a $4 trillion economy by 2047.” The United Economic Forum in association with Kothari Industrial Corporation Limited and Airtel Business is organising the Tamil Nadu Growth Conclave 2026.

World.title: Panjab University improves its global standing in interdisciplinary scientific research
World.content:
Chandigarh-based Panjab University (PU) has improved its global standing in interdisciplinary scientific research, climbing 24 places to secure the joint 150th position in the Times Higher Education (THE) Interdisciplinary Science Rankings 2027. The University’s overall score has increased to 55.0 from 52.8 in 2026 and 48.6 in 2025.

In a statement on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Vice-Chancellor Meenakshi Goyal said, “This improvement in Panjab University’s global standing reflects our continued commitment to strengthening interdisciplinary research and academic collaboration. It is the outcome of the collective efforts of our faculty, researchers, students, and staff. We will continue to build an enabling research ecosystem that encourages collaboration across disciplines, supports innovation, and addresses complex societal challenges aimed at Viksit Bharat through knowledge and research.”

The 2027 edition of the rankings, produced by Times Higher Education in association with Schmidt Science Fellows, assessed 1,058 institutions across 102 countries and territories, compared with 911 institutions in the 2026 edition. A total of 565 Asian institutions were ranked, up from 478 last year.

The Interdisciplinary Science Rankings assess universities’ contributions and commitment to research that brings together knowledge and methods from different academic disciplines to address complex challenges. The rankings cover collaborations involving multiple scientific disciplines as well as research combining scientific disciplines with areas such as the social sciences, education, psychology, law, economics, and clinical and health studies.

World.title: ‘Have the courage to listen to the debate you started’: Bilawal sticks to his guns after speaking his ‘truth’
World.content:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Wednesday maintained that his recent remarks on the country’s political situation were the “truth”, urging government representatives to have the “courage” to listen to his point of view.

Speaking in an interview on Hum News programme ‘Faisla Aap Ka’, Bilawal reiterated his stance from his Tuesday’s speech, cautioning against new provinces and calling for a “political reset” so public issues could be addressed.

Bilawal emphasised that he spoke in the context of the US-Iran war, which has impacted economies around the world due to rising energy costs.

“Elites do not have the idea of what kind of difficulties Pakistanis are facing,” he said, highlighting the need for politicians to set aside their partisan political perspectives and think about how to “fix the system”.

The PPP chairman asserted it was his right to provide his perspective on what shape a “reset” should take if someone was suggesting that a reset was needed, indirectly referring to Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s July remarks.

On the fact that his PPP was part of the ruling coalition, Bilawal contended that this was the exact reason to “listen” to him as he was a “major stakeholder”.

“These are not reasons to discount what I am saying […] I am telling you that this is the situation; these are my proposals to rectify it. You may disagree with my suggestions, but at least listen. You should have the courage to listen to the truth.”

The Bhutto scion added, “Because I am a stakeholder, I am saying: come to your senses.”

He further said, “Now let’s have the debate that you started. […] Have the courage to [continue] the debate that is now ongoing.”

Noting that the conversation had not been brought to the Parliament so far, Bilawal said, “You yourself decided to hold this debate in front of businessmen. It was decided on their own that this debate would be held through touts.”

The PPP chairman affirmed that Pakistan had not become so weak as a society that there would only be “one-sided debates”.

Replying to a question, he remarked that he “spoke too much truth yesterday, which was now hard to digest”.

Noting the ongoing “geopolitical atmosphere”, the former foreign minister wondered how many fronts the government wanted to fight on simultaneously, with India as an adversary, a near-war situation with Afghanistan and the fight against terrorism.

“The government has been deciding that we will fight the PTI; now the new decision is that they will also fight JUI, and it seems that after my truth, they have also decided they must fight me too,” Bilawal remarked.

“If you are going to fight everyone, and fight everyone internally as well, then who will lead Pakistan and its people out of this economic crisis?” he wondered.

The PPP chairman said the reactions from federal ministers to his remarks were “yet another proof that Pakistan’s politicians do not have the courage to hear the truth”.

“If you or they do not have enough courage or patience to listen to me, then what about the people of Pakistan who have no access to the prime minister, his ministers, or the National Assembly?”

‘Want PM Shehbaz to be strengthened’

Asked about his view if the government insisted on forming provinces, Bilawal said: “I would want to say to the incumbent government that the power of ‘kun fayakun’ belongs only to Allah Almighty and no one else.

“And if anyone is under the misconception that a decision was made, spoken, and thus done, then it will have an impact and consequences on our society, on our federation, on our politics, and on the lives of our people.”

On the PPP’s allyship with the PML-N, Bilawal said his party was with the government, keeping the national interest in view. He added, “Otherwise, there is political loss for me in bearing the burden of this government and this system.”

At the same time, he affirmed that his party still stood with the government and wanted Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to be successful.

Clarifying any “misunderstanding” that PML-N might have, Bilawal said the aim of his address yesterday was that PM Shehbaz’s “hands are strengthened”.

Asked if he could leave the ruling coalition if he was not heard, the Bhutto scion said, “There is no extraordinary interest in sitting on the treasury benches or opposition benches.”

He added that if the government “did not have enough courage to tolerate the well-meaning input of their allies, then I wouldn’t lose any sleep if I was sitting on the opposition benches”.

‘Unaware of what is behind provinces debate’

Bilawal said he was unaware of “what was behind this debate because till today, despite being such a major stakeholder”, neither the prime minister nor a federal minister nor a political or any other stakeholder had discussed with him or the president that they wanted new provinces to be created.

“No attention” was being paid to the ongoing historic economic crisis, the ex-minister added.

Reiterating that he had not started the debate on governance, Bilawal quipped whether “only the PCB chairman had the right to tell how and why the system has collapsed”, referring to Naqvi, who also serves as the cricket board chief.

“If a reset has to happen, then has the PCB been given the responsibility that you have all powers to decide how the system will be reset, whether provinces should be divided? […] Should I go home quietly? This is not possible.”

Asked whether his remarks meant that PPP would take the path of resistance, Bilawal refrained from terming it that, adding that he provided his voters’ perspective and did not issue any protest call.

“I suggested to everyone that a political reset is needed, a democratic reset is needed, so that instead of politicians grabbing each other’s collars, fighting each other, we all join hands to pull the public out of this hardship,” he explained.

The PPP chairman termed the government’s reaction to criticism by Maulana Fazlur Rehman as “completely frivolous, irresponsible conduct”. “If he criticises, the reaction is to demolish the house, arrest his son and pressure his party workers,” he added.

Asked whether his warning regarding the division of Sindh was a threat, the Bhutto scion affirmed that his party was not one that engaged in violence.

He referred to Sindh’s history, particularly from the 1980s onwards, adding, “Was what I said outside of a historical context or precedent? This wasn’t organic; it was orchestrated to create division in Sindh’s politics.”

He declared, “And this risk is still present today, which is why I was warning that if Sindh is divided forcefully, I would not do such things but there will be a reaction.”

Bilawal warned that while he would not want it, the law and order situation would worsen so much that it would be difficult to put out the “fire”.

‘Not disowning 27th Amendment’

On him questioning the 27th Amendment, Bilawal stressed that the amendment lacked the same “unanimous consensus” that was present for the 1973 Constitution and the 18th Amendment.

He stated that the 26th Amendment was passed with input from the opposition through the JUI-F chief, but it was the 27th Amendment that was followed by resignations of senior judges.

He emphasised that he was not calling for withdrawing the amendments, but that the opposition’s input be considered in such legislation.

In a separate interview on Geo News, Bilawal clarified he was “not disowning the 27th Amendment”.

He elaborated that there was a “difference” in the 18th, 26th and 27th Amendments regarding the consensus each of them had.

The PPP chairman declared he was “proud that we formed a constitutional court”, and that it had equal representation from all provinces.

Bilawal emphasised that he had presented suggestions on how confidence can be restored not just in the judiciary, but in other institutions as well, including the Parliament and the election commission, if there was to be a “political reset”.

“Do I believe the 27th Amendment could be more powerful with more input? Absolutely,” the PPP chief stated, stressing that he still believed judicial reforms were needed so that judges did not interfere in irrelevant matters.

“If you don’t want a reset, if you don’t want to improve the situation, then continue things as they are. But it can’t be that only one person is allowed and only one point of view is legitimate and any other is illegitimate.”

‘Reserved seats a low-hanging fruit if political reset pursued’

Speaking on Hum News about his remarks on reserved seats, Bilawal termed it a “low-hanging fruit if there was to be a political reset and if the opposition’s confidence was to be restored”.

“If we are to have a political reset, if we are to work towards a system that solves the economic issues of the people of Pakistan, one of the low-hanging fruits to improve the confidence of the opposition to convince them to start trusting Parliament in the political system is this suggestion — not this direction, not this insistence or red line.”

Asked about how such a process could begin as it would alter the coalition’s strength in the Parliament, Bilawal replied it could only happen if everyone agreed.

“If the government says no, we do not want to do so, then I cannot force anything,” said the PPP chairman about their ally PML-N.

Responding to a query about reserved seats on Geo News, Bilawal emphasised that his suggestion was “in the context of a political, democratic reset that could restore the trust of the opposition parties”.

He remarked that in the case of such a reset, considering giving back PTI its reserved seats “through the courts or legislation could be part of a confidence-building measure”.

On the PPP possibly giving up its reserved seats, Bilawal contended that this was “not the legal position as of now”, adding that they would not go to PTI even if his lawmakers resign.

“I think there’s an attempt of purpose to sensationalise what I said, to delegitimise and take out of context what I said, to serve some other purpose,” he further said.

World.title: PTA says submarine cable fault may cause internet connectivity issues
World.content:
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) said on Wednesday that a fault in one of the international submarine cable systems may result in users experiencing internet connectivity issues.

“One of the international submarine cable systems, the SEA-ME-WE 5 (SMW5), has reported a fault at about 11km from Pakistan’s shore, which may cause some internet users to experience intermittent connectivity issues and a decline in service quality,” the authority said.

“Transworld Associates is coordinating with the SMW5 consortium to identify the root cause of the fault and determine the estimated time for restoration,” it added.

In the meantime, the authority said internet traffic was “being rerouted through alternative international links to minimise the impact and ensure service continuity to the greatest extent possible”.

It added that it was in close coordination with the concerned stakeholders and will “continue to monitor the situation to facilitate the earliest possible restoration of normal internet services across the country”.

Internet monitor NetBlocks confirmed later that a decline in internet connectivity was causing slow service.

“The incident is consistent with a fault on the SMW5 international subsea cable system with operators now attempting to establish alternative routes,” it said.

On July 1, a fault in the SMW5 international submarine cable system caused widespread connectivity issues in Pakistan. The fault was resolved on July 3.

World.title: Petrol and diesel prices reduced by Rs3 per litre each
World.content:
The government on Wednesday reduced the prices of both petrol and diesel by Rs3 per litre, marking the twelfth consecutive decrease in the rate of petrol.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs322 per litre, while HSD will remain at Rs355 on Nov 19 (Thursday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

Following Tuesday’s reduction of the petrol price to Rs325 per litre, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar highlighted the government’s “proactive measures including policy changes and structural reforms in petroleum policy” that had brought prices back down from their April 3 peak and provided relief through a fuel subsidy scheme.

“The government of Pakistan remains committed to continue making all possible efforts to ease the financial burden on the common man amid global challenges,” he said.

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

Since July 17 , the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: ICJ report sees 'judicial capture' in Pakistan after 26th, 27th Constitutional Amendments
World.content:
A report released by the International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) on Wednesday said that the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments led to a “systemic judicial capture” in Pakistan.

The 26th Amendment , passed in October 2024, carved constitutional benches out of the Supreme Court, with their members chosen by a reconstituted Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) in which judges no longer held a majority.

Barely a year later, the 27th Amendment turned those benches into an entirely separate court, the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC). It also made significant changes to the judicial system, the military’s chain of command and granted immunities to government officials. Two of the SC’s senior-most judges resigned in protest the day it became law.

On Wednesday, the ICJ released a report — titled ‘Judicial Capture: Independence of the Judiciary in Pakistan after the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments’.

It said that after analysing the institutional framework governing higher courts following the two amendments, the judiciary in Pakistan no longer enjoyed institutional guarantees of independence required under international law and standards.

“The 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments were a decisive break from the model of judicial independence that Pakistan had built after the restoration of the judiciary in 2009,” the report noted.

However, it observed that the “erosion of judicial independence” was done through constitutional amendments, rather than the overt removal of judges.

The report said that while the government argued that amendments were made to “check judicial overreach, reduce the backlog of cases, end the perceived politicisation of the SC’s original jurisdiction and give Parliament a role in judicial appointments comparable to that of legislatures in other democracies”, the claims did not justify “changing the judicial structure in a manner that is glaringly inconsistent with Pakistan’s obligations under international law”.

It also acknowledged that the Supreme Court had “encroached into roles of Parliament and other institutions”. However, it also noted that with the 26th and 27th amendments, the Parliament failed to ensure these “deficiencies” were fixed in line with judicial independence.

“Instead, the 26th and 27th Amendments have led to systemic judicial capture by other branches of the state and the dismantling of the rule of law in the country,” the ICJ stated.

It was found that the ruling coalition had “exploited” the public’s grievances over the functioning of courts in a “self-serving manner” to control the judiciary.

“As a result, even the highest courts of the land in Pakistan no longer serve as a check on the executive or the Parliament and their function as avenues for redress of victims of human rights violations is seriously impaired,” the report stated.

Call for comprehensive review

In its recommendations, the report appealed to the government to begin a comprehensive review of the amendments and their implementation in “light of international law and standards”, particularly under the framework of Pakistan’s obligations under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR) and by holding “transparent and broad” public consultation.

It suggested that the government engage in international cooperation, including seeking technical assistance from the UN special rapporteur on the independence of judges and lawyers and inviting them for a country visit.

In its recommendations to the JCP, the ICJ called on it to revise the criteria for judicial appointments in accordance with international law, standards and best practices.

It further suggested: “Ensure the published criteria are the sole basis for nomination of judges to the FCC, the SC, the high courts and constitutional benches of the high courts.”

It also called on the commission to establish a transparent procedure for appointments and publish reasons for each appointment that “demonstrate the published criteria are being implemented in practice”.

It also called on the JCP to refrain from transferring a high court judge without their consent.

In its recommendations to the Supreme Judicial Council, the ICJ said: “Define ‘inefficiency’ in a manner that is consistent with international standards to only mean serious incompetence that renders judges unfit to discharge their duties.”

For the Special Parliamentary Committee, which has the power to nominate the chief justice of Pakistan, the report called for it to adopt “clear and transparent criteria and procedures” for the appointment of the SC and FCC top judges and to publish the reasons for each selection.

Lastly, the report urged the FCC, the SC and the high courts to “interpret and apply the provisions of the 26th and 27th Amendments, to the greatest extent possible, in a manner consistent with the independence of the judiciary as guaranteed by Article 14 of the ICCPR”.

World.title: Pakistan's mango exports fall 36pc amid US-Iran war: exporters' association
World.content:
Pakistan’s mango exports fell 36 per cent this year as the US-Iran war disrupted shipping routes and drove up freight costs, industry figures showed on Wednesday.

According to All Pakistan Fruit and Vegetables Exporters Association, the country exported 78,000 tonnes of mangoes this year, compared with 123,000 tons last year.

Exports to the Middle East, a major market for Pakistani mangoes, dropped from 36,000 tonnes last year to 14,500 tonnes this year, the association said.

Waheed Ahmed, head of the association, told Anadolu that the ongoing conflict had reduced the country’s mango export earnings from approximately $100 million to around $60m.

He cited the months-long near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping route, and rising freight rates as major factors behind the decline, particularly in exports to Middle Eastern countries.

“The freight rate that was $1,000-1,400 before the US-Iran war, now stands at $8,000. Secondly, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz also increased the shipping period, which affected the exports of perishable items like mangoes,” he said.

Ahmed said the United Arab Emirates and Oman were the main Middle Eastern destinations for Pakistani mangoes, particularly the internationally acclaimed Chaunsa variety, followed by Saudi Arabia.

Kuwait and Qatar also import significant quantities of Pakistani mangoes, according to the association.

Mango exports to neighboring Afghanistan were also disrupted by frequent border closures amid strained relations between the two countries, Ahmed said.

Pakistan produced 1.9m metric tonnes of mangoes annually until 2018, ranking sixth globally behind India, China, Thailand, Indonesia and Mexico.

However, production has declined over the past four years, with the association attributing the drop to global warming.

Climate change has reduced Pakistan’s total mango production by 35pc, according to the association.

World.title: Pakistan conducts successful launch of Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile: ISPR
World.content:
The Pakistan Army on Wednesday successfully launched the Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile, according to the military’s media wing.

In a statement, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said, “The Pakistan Army successfully conducted the launch of the Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile, marking another significant milestone in strengthening Pakistan’s national defence capabilities.

“The weapon system is equipped with advanced navigation and propulsion systems and is capable of engaging targets at long range with high precision and lethality at supersonic speed,” it said.

It added that the missile would “significantly enhance the operational flexibility and strike range of the Pakistan Army’s Rocket Force Command, further strengthening the country’s overall conventional deterrence and defence posture”.

According to the statement, the Army Rocket Force Command commander, senior officers from the armed forces, scientists and engineers witnessed the launch.

It added that President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, and the services chiefs congratulated the team on the successful launch.

They appreciated the dedication and commitment of all personnel involved in achieving this significant milestone in Pakistan’s defence development, the statement concluded.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar termed the development a “testament to the relentless hard work, skill and innovation of our teams in strengthening Pakistan’s defence capabilities and national deterrence”.

“The entire nation takes immense pride in their unwavering commitment to keeping the country strong and secure,” he said.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi congratulated the nation on the successful launch. According to the interior ministry, he said that the launch represented a “significant advancement in the defence sector”.

“The successful test of the Fatah-3 supersonic cruise missile marks a major milestone in the country’s defence capabilities,” Naqvi said.

Earlier this month, the Pakistan Air Force performed a successful flight test of the country’s first indigenously developed air-to-air missile, Fa’az.

ISPR said that the flight test marked “another significant milestone in the advancement of national aerospace and defence capabilities”.

World.title: KP governor forms 8-member commission to probe illegal placer gold mining
World.content:
PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Wednesday constituted an eight-member inquiry commission to probe illegal placer gold mining in the province.

The commission, according to a notification issued by the provincial home and tribal affairs department, will be headed by retired Justice Asadullah Khan Chamkani.

It will also include as members Barrister Mohammad Yaseen Raza, legal adviser/member Sher Akbar Khan, Deputy Inspector General of Police Wasif Rahman, Health Department Additional Secretary Engineer Ziarat Khan, and representatives of intelligence agencies.

According to the notification, the commission will inquire into the extent, history and nature of illegal placer gold mining in KP, particularly in Kohat, Nowshera, Karak and other affected districts. The inquiry includes the scale, duration and locations of illegal operations.

In addition to this, the commission will identify persons, groups and networks involved in illegal mining, including beneficiaries, and determine their “respective roles, financial gains and individual or institutional responsibility for facilitation, corruption, negligence, abuse of authority or failure to discharge legal duties”.

Similarly, it will also inquire into “allegations of patronage, facilitation and connivance by political figures, public representatives, government functionaries, law enforcement personnel or any other persons or institutions, including corruption, abuse of authority, deliberate inaction or protection provided to illegal mining operations”, the notification said.

The commission will also examine the financial dimensions of illegal mining, including the estimated quantity and value of gold illegally extracted, losses caused to the public exchequer, movement of proceeds, money laundering, smuggling and possible links with organised crime, terrorist groups or terrorist financing.

It will additionally examine the role and performance of concerned government departments, district administrations and the police in “preventing illegal mining, monitoring lease conditions, taking enforcement action, registering and investigating cases, prosecuting offenders and dealing with seized machinery, gold and other property”.

The commission has also been tasked to determine the reasons for the continuation or recurrence of illegal mining in spite of repeated complaints, government directions, enforcement operations and criminal proceedings, including negligence, deliberate failure to enforce the law, interference or facilitation by those responsible for enforcement.

In addition to this, it will also inquire into the circumstances surrounding the Kohat incident of Nov 11, including any links between illegal mining networks and the attack on police personnel, possible planning, financing, facilitation or support, and any relevant operational or security lapses, without prejudice to ongoing criminal investigations, the notification said.

Eighteen terrorists were killed while 10 cops were martyred on Nov 11 when a police team came under attack on its way back after completing an operation against elements involved in illegal gold mining.

The committee will also examine previous inquiries, reports, complaints and decisions, including those of the National Accountability Bureau (NAB), Provincial Cabinet Inquiry Committee (PCIC) and other competent authorities, assess the implementation of their findings and recommendations, and examine any fresh material or evidence warranting further inquiry.

The commission will assess the financial and environmental damage caused by illegal mining, including loss of government revenue and damage to riverbeds and adjoining areas, while identifying persons or entities against whom recovery, compensation or other legal action may be warranted.
